title: Self-powered fire alarm system based on Ti3C2Tx MXene/PVP/Piezoelectric fibers multilayers embedded with additively manufactured TPMS spacers with tunable stiffness
authors: Zhong Wei Guo, Chih Chia Chen, Yi Ting Huang, Yiin Kuen Fuh
conclusion: In conclusion, we present a self-powered fire alarm. The nanogenerator part consists of PVDF-TrFE nano-fibre, FPCB, and encapsulated PDMS layers. It is self-powered, which means that the system does not require an additional power supply. The maximum Voc and Isc are 5.97 V and 58.5nA, respectively. The optimal resistance value matching is 14.8 MΩ, with a peak power output of 97.9 nW. The aforementioned findings demonstrate the capability of MPSFS to independently charge the capacitor within the circuit by the NGs. The PVP-modified MXene film was integrated into this substrate, and the modified MXene paper exhibits flexibility, outstanding flame resistance, and adjustable initial resistance. MXene paper is highly flame-retardant. It is especially useful for reusable fire alarms that are sensitive to complex environments. As a result, MXene/PVP films offer ultra-fast fire alarm response and recovery times (approximately 3.0 s), high resistance switching sensitivity, and reliable cyclic fire alarms. In addition, the combination of MXene/PVP paper with silane functionalization produces a versatile, reusable material. Additionally, the lower material distribution density in thinner structures further decreases their load-bearing capacity, resulting in a lower stiffness under stress. The thinnest 0.2 mm spacer provided a higher enhancement in the voltage output of the nanogenerator compared to the other two thicknesses. These findings indicate that varying the thickness of TPMS structures can yield different stiffness, providing a basis for optimizing TPMS design in applications. This system can be easily applied to fire alarms to closely monitor high fire risks in complex environments. The addition of water-soluble polymers to MXene paper, which boasts excellent fire resistance and reusability in fire response, has also led to the identification of the optimal TPMS spacer design for MPSFS, maximizing the output performance of the self-powered system. Its stability and reliability have also been tested. This innovative system significantly reduces fire risk and demonstrates great potential and application prospects in advancing fire safety technology. title: The surface functional modification of Ti3C2Tx MXene by phosphorus doping and its application in quasi-solid state flexible supercapacitor
authors: Xiaochun Wei, Man Cai, Fulin Yuan, Dan Lu, Cong Li, Haifu Huang, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Jin Guo
conclusion: In summary, we reported a simple preparation method of P-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes, in which sodium hypophosphate was used as a phosphorus source and phosphorus was doped by the heat treatment. The P-doping level is in the range 0.9–1.11 at% by this method. After heat treatment, the expansion of layer spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene promotes the rapid transport and diffusion of electrolyte ions into electrode interface. At the same time, the d-spacing of MXene is further expanded because the introduction of P atoms increases the adsorption effect. The P O and P C bonds generated provide more active sites, resulting in the enhanced energy storage performance of the electrode. As expected, the specific capacitance of P-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene is as high as 476.9F g−1 , far larger than that of raw Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Furthermore, the quasi-solid flexible supercapacitor assembled by Ti3 C2 Tx -P-3h film electrode can reach high energy density of 15.8 Wh kg−1 at power density of 250 W kg−1 . These results demonstrate that P doping plays an important role in improving the structure, composition and electrochemical performance of MXene materials. This work also provides a new way to achieve high specific capacitance and excellent retention performance of MXene electrodes. title: Flexible Ti3C2Tx MXene/V2O5 composite films for high-performance all-solid supercapacitors
authors: Wenlong Luo, Yue Sun, Zhongtai Lin, Xue Li, Yongqin Han, Jianxu Ding, Tingxi Li, Chunping Hou, Yong Ma
conclusion: In summary, the MV films with tunable thickness have been prepared by a combination of minimal delamination method, redox method and vacuum-assisted filtration techniques. MXene, as the backbone of the films, provides high electrical conductivity, good flexibility and large specific surface area. V2 O5 nanofibers act as spacers to effectively enlarge the interlayer spacing of MXene nanosheets and suppress their self-stacking phenomenon, increasing the ion accessibility surface area and multi-directional ion transport channels. The fabricated MV2 film as electrode shows considerable capacitance performance (319.1 F g‐1 , 0.5 A g‐1 ) and cycling stability (70.4 %, 5000 cycles, 3 A g‐1 ). Moreover, the SSC exhibits a specific capacitance of 92.1 F g‐1 at 1 A g‐1 , a capacitance retention of 72.1 % after 8000 charge/discharge cycles at 2 A g‐1 , and an energy density of 18.43 Wh kg‐1 at 603.2 W kg‐1 power density. The ASC has a specific capacitance of 66.67 F g‐1 at 0.5 A g‐1 , and still has 83.9 % capacitance retention after 8000 charge/discharge cycles at 2 A g‐1 . And the ASC displays an energy density of 20.83 Wh kg‐1 at a power density of 374.94 W kg‐1 , indicating its superior energy storage capability. This strategy provides a new idea for the application of MXene in flexible wearable devices. title: Tin(IV) selenide anchored-biowaste derived porous carbon-Ti3C2Tx (MXene) nanohybrid: An ionic electrolyte enhanced high performing flexible supercapacitor electrode
authors: Shrabani De, Chandan Kumar Maity, Myung Jong Kim, Ganesh Chandra Nayak
conclusion: In summary, a successful synthesis of SnSe2 nanorod decorated APC/Ti3 C2 Tx via facile hydrothermal method has demonstrated and established using different characterization techniques. In three-electrode configuration, the ternary APC/M/SnSe2 nanohybrid delivered excellent electrochemical properties with a high Sp.C of 815 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 . Additionally, electrochemical performances of the assembled ASC device (APC/M/SnSe2 // M (Ti3 C2 Tx )) were studied in two different electrolytes; ionic and organic. An outstanding Sp.C of 227 F g −1 , and ED of 102 W h kg−1 at 1 A g −1 were obtained in the case of ionic electrolyte along with desired volumetric ED. Subsequently, the flexible ASC device was also made-up using viscous [(NEt3 H)+ (HSO4 )− ] electrolyte and it was capable to glow a red LED in different bending modes. Overall, the synthesized ternary electrode APC/Ti3 C2 Tx /SnSe2 can be recognized as an appealing candidate for the real-time flexible ASC. Overall, the construction of an effective energy storage device employing biowaste-derived APC-based SnSe2 -Ti3 C2 Tx composite may provide a solution to the problems of waste management and the energy crisis. 5 Supporting information Excremental section including materials and characterizations; FESEM images of carbon, Ti3 C2 Tx , and SnSe2 ; XRD pattern of APC; EDS analysis; Table for the D and G band positions with corresponding ID /IG ratios of synthesized materials obtained from Raman spectroscopy; CV analysis of M and SnSe2 ; Trasatti analysis; Table for Fitted data values of Nyquist impedance plot; Device assembly process; Representation of the device; Electrochemical performances of the SuCap device in organic electrolyte; A comparison table for the eelectrochemical properties with some similar previously reported electrodes; Calculation of volumetric energy density; Flexible device assembly process; and Images of flexible SuCap device. title: Photothermal processing of crumpled Ti3C2Tx MXenes with nitrogen/sulfur co-modification for boosting capacitance performance
authors: Hailong Shen, Hongying Zhao, Liqing Yan, Jiaheng Xu, Lin Li, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Haifu Huang
conclusion: In this study, nitrogen and sulfur were successfully doped into Ti3 C2 Tx using UV photo-assistance. This process involved the elimination of harmful –F surface functional groups and the incorporation of nitrogen and sulfur atoms, resulting in an enhancement of the material's electrical conductivity. This improvement is favorable for charge transfer, thereby endowing the material with superior rate performance. DFT calculations further indicate that doping with N and S atoms increases the DOS near the Fermi level of Ti3 C2 Tx and opens up new electron transfer pathways. Additionally, during the doping process, the increased spacing between the MXenes interlayers and the modification of the surface functional groups led to an increase in energy storage sites, significantly improving the charge storage capacity of the material. For instance, the NS-Ti3 C2 Tx -P electrode exhibited a high specific capacitance of 424 F g−1 at a scan rate of 2 mV s−1 and maintained 365 F g−1 even at a scan rate of 100 mV s−1 . These results demonstrate the excellent rate capability of the NS-Ti3 C2 Tx -P electrode. Furthermore, after 3000 cycles, the electrode retained approximately 95 % of its initial specific capacity, indicating outstanding cycle stability. When assembled into an aqueous symmetrical supercapacitor, the device achieved a specific energy of 18.61 Wh kg−1 at 500 W kg−1 . This study improved the energy storage performance of MXenes as electrode materials for supercapacitors by co-doping with dual atoms assisted by ultraviolet light. It explained the reasons for the improved electrochemical performance through simulation calculations, paving the way for further research on the energy storage performance of supercapacitors. title: Unlocking the key roles of N,P co-doping in Ti3C2Tx MXene for lithium-ion storage: lower lithium ion diffusion resistance and more lithium active sites
authors: Yunhao Wu, Zhen Wang, Zijun Du, Di Zhang, Jiaxuan Li, Juan Zhang, Jianling Li
conclusion: In conclusion, by using a hydrothermal method and regulating the feeding ratio, we successfully synthesized N,P double-doped MXene materials, in which the N,P elements are uniformly anchored on the surface of MXene materials. The N,P modification on the MXene surface has been demonstrated to enhance the electronic conductivity of Ti3 C2 Tx , while simultaneously extending the ion transport path by enlarging the interlayer space. Furthermore, the introduction of P elemental doping has been shown to provide additional electrochemically active sites. Compared with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, N,P-MXene has excellent Li-ion storage capacity and cycling stability, and still has a discharge specific capacity close to 200 mAh/g after 1700 cycles at 150 mA/g. Furthermore, in situ EIS and Raman characterization provide comprehensive illustration of the effects of N and P element doping on the SEI film formation process of MXene materials and the evolution of surface groups during charging and discharging. Additionally, DFT calculations are employed to elucidate the distribution of P elements on the MXene surface and the change of adsorption energy in greater detail. This work demonstrates that bi-elemental co-doping can provide new reactive active sites while modulating the diffusion of lithium ions on the surface, producing bi-doped MXene materials with optimized electrochemical properties, and effectively facilitating the application of MXenes in the field of energy storage. title: Rational design of cobalt ion chelated quasi-monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene with abundant surface loading for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitor
authors: Guandan Lu, Xuteng Xing, Jia Zhang, Xiaoyang Xu, Xiangjing Zhang, Haining Liu, Jiye Fan, Bingzhu Zhang
journal: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
conclusion: The cobalt ion chelated Ti3 C2 Tx MXene (Co@Ti3 C2 Tx MXene) composite is designed/prepared by employing Ti3 C2 Tx MXene supernatant as the precursor, together with further alkalization, and cobalt ion chelation processes. The obtained Co@Ti3 C2 Tx MXene composite can exhibit the highly dispersed monolayer and abundant surface -OH functional groups, accelerating the surface loading of Co2+ ions. After optimizing the composition, the 1-Co@Ti3 C2 Tx MXene displays the highest specific capacity of 48 mAh/g at the current density of 1 A/g, much higher than Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, which is attributed to the highly dispersed nearly-monolayer structure, additional Faradaic redox reaction of Co (Ⅱ/Ш), and enhanced conductivity from Co element. In order to evaluate the potential practical application, the Co@Ti3 C2 Tx MXene//AC asymmetric supercapacitor device is assembled by using optimal 1-Co@Ti3 C2 Tx MXene and AC as positive/negative electrode materials respectively, also exhibiting good performances including high energy density of 19 Wh/kg and good cycle stability. The metal ion chelation is a simple and effective strategy to inhibit the stack and enhance electrochemical performances for Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. title: Bacterial cellulose modified polyaniline/Ti3C2Tx MXene fiber to enhance robust and electrochemical activity for wire-shaped supercapacitors
authors: Yang Zhang, Kangxin Qi, Xiangxiang Pi, Qingqing Tang, Qingquan Xue, Wei Chen, Diwei Gu, Jian Xu, Shenao Zhang, Yusen Wang, Yunxia Liang, Bin Sun, Wangyang Lu
conclusion: In summary, the flexible and robust PBT fiber was assembled via s simple wet spinning method for high-performance wire-shaped F-SC. Particularly, insertion of BC nanowire and PANI nanoparticles between Ti3 C2 Tx interlayers is useful to regulate the layer configuration. The issue of self-restacking of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheet can be effectively alleviated, thus enhancing the ion permeation ability. Besides, hybridizing the conductive PANI in interlayer can provide rich redox active sites and large pseudo-capacitance, leading to outstanding ion accumulation ability. Moreover, the synergistic effect between BC and Ti3 C2 Tx via hydrogen bond significantly improves the mechanical properties of hybrid fiber. As a result, the PBT fiber shows high mechanical strength (123.42 MPa), large mass capacitance (337 F g−1 at 2 A g−1 ), superior rate performance (129 F g−1 at 10 A g−1 ) and long cycling life (84 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles). More importantly, the solid-state symmetric F-SC shows considerable capacitance (259 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ), outstanding cycling stability (86 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles), large energy density of 7.28 Wh kg−1 and favorable mechanical endurance, which illustrates a bright future in wearable system. title: Synergistic integration of amorphous MoSx nanoparticles with Ti3C2Tx MXene layers for high-performance ammonium-ion supercapacitors
authors: Jinhe Wei, Fei Hu, Chenglong Lv, Xinyu Quan, Qiuyun Ouyang
conclusion: In summary, we have developed excellent host electrode material with the crystalline Ti3 C2 Tx /amorphous MoSx on carbon cloths for wearable ammonium-ion supercapacitor. The ultra-thin nanosheets are uniformly covered in the Ti3 C2 Tx layer, which simultaneously reduces accumulation. The formation of sulfur vacancies and defects can further enhance the electronic properties of the material and increase the formation of hydrogen bonds. At the same time, the amorphous structure can protect the composite structure from collapsing in the NH4 + insertion/de-insertion. Impressively, the resultant Ti3 C2 Tx @MoSx electrode yields an excellent specific capacity of 196.94 mAh·g−1 and remarkable capacitance retention (more than 91.01 % after 10000 cycles). The constructed symmetric ammonium-ion supercapacitor shows the maximum energy density of 50.08 Wh·kg−1 at a power density of 500.81 W kg−1 , along with outstanding cycling stability, maintaining 85.98 % of its specific capacity after 10000 cycles. The design not only provides a new host material for NH4 + storage but also proposes a new strategy to increase the electrochemical properties of MoS2 . title: An intercalated structure MXene@CCNS: cuttlefish ink-derived carbon nanospheres composite Ti3C2Tx MXene for supercapacitors
authors: Dawei Wang, Yue Lian, Qiuping Zhou, Hongliang Fu, Yongfeng Hu, Jing Zhao, Huaihao Zhang
conclusion: In summary, we have prepared a heterostructured composite MXene@CCNS, composed of MXene and cuttlefish ink-derived carbon nanospheres through an electrostatic self-assembly method, and investigated the impact of heterostructure on material's ion/electron transport capability and capacitive performance. The heterostructure formed by intercalating cuttlefish ink-derived carbon nanospheres into MXene layers effectively increases the spacing between MXene layers, and prevents them from self-stacking. As a result, larger active surface area and more active sites are exposed on MXene, which enhances the ion adsorption capacity and shortens the ion transport path to improve the capacitive properties. Furthermore, the heterostructure mitigates volume changes of electrode material during continuous charging and discharging cycles, leading to enhanced stability. DFT calculations further prove the elevated charge transfer by this heterostructure. Accordingly, the MXene@CCNS delivers 264 F g−1 of specific capacitance at current density 0.5 A g−1 , and also demonstrate favorable rate performance and cycle stability. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor based on this electrode material offers 12.8 Wh kg−1 of energy density at 0.2 kW kg−1 of power density while maintaining a capacitance retention of 91.7 % even after 5000 cycles. title: g-C3N4/MoO3 heterostructure decorated Ti3C2Tx MXene film as a flexible electrode for supercapacitors with high energy density and low temperature tolerance
authors: Qing Xu, Yuqing Chen, Yongjie Huang, Chunyan Xu, Chun Hu, Ningyi Jiang, Liying Yang, Shougen Yin
conclusion: In summary, a self-supporting g-C3 N4 /MoO3 -Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid film was prepared by vacuum filtration method, which exhibits good electrochemical performance in a wide temperature range from −20 to 40 °C. The optimal electrode exhibits a specific capacity of 1168 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 in 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte and satisfactory cyclic stability with capacitance retention of 96.8 % after 5000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . When used as the electrode for the button-type asymmetric SCs, it also presents an energy density of 316 Wh kg−1 , a power density of 1250 W kg−1 , and remarkable cyclic stability. Even at low temperature (−20 °C), the CMM asymmetric SC demonstrates an energy density of 230 Wh kg−1 , a capacitance retention of 81 % and coulombic efficiency of 92 % after 5000 cycles. It is believed that the incorporation g-C3 N4 /MoO3 heterostructure on MXene nanosheets prevents the re-stacking of MXene nanosheets, expands the potential window, effectively enhancing the performance of SCs. Our work provides an effective and simple strategy of incorporation g-C3 N4 /MoO3 heterostructure on MXene nanosheets to improve the stability of MXene in application of energy storage. title: Compression-tolerant supercapacitor based on NiCo2O4/Ti3C2Tx MXene/reduced graphene oxide composite aerogel with insights from density functional theory simulations
authors: Maozhuang Zhang, Degang Jiang, Fuhao Jin, Yuesheng Sun, Jianhua Wang, Mingyuan Jiang, Jiangyong Cao, Bo Zhang, Jingquan Liu
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: In summary, we have developed heterostructured NCO/MGA-300 with hierarchical and interconnected porous structures by using an intrinsically conductive and compressible MGA as host template. Benefiting from the synergistic effects of hierarchical porous structures and heterostructures, the NCO/MGA-300 electrode exhibits exquisite electrochemical performance in terms of high gravimetric capacitance (1633F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ), excellent rate performance (1492F g−1 at 10 A g−1 ), and stable cycling stability (∼86.6%) after 10,000 charge–discharge cycles, superior to reported compressible flexible capacitors. Based on the compressible NCO/MGA-300 electrodes, the assembled aNCMSC devices can retain intact structure and stable electrochemical performances under different strains, or after 100 compression-release cycles, suggesting the high reliability and security of the NCO/MGA electrodes. We thus believe this work should contribute to achieve advanced electrodes with both good compressibility and high energy storage capability for wearable devices, and this synergistic effect of heterostructures can also be applied to other metal oxides and two-dimensional carbons materials during the compounding process. title: Synthesis and characterization of a nanocomposite consisting of Ti3C2Tx (MXene) and WS2 nanosheets for potential use in supercapacitors
authors: Pınar Talay Pınar, Mehmet Gülcan, Yavuz Yardım
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  Ti 3 C 2 Tx-MXene, WS 2 nanosheets, and MXene/WS 2 nanocomposite materials were prepared using a straightforward and efficient single-step strategy. Electrochemical measurements were conducted on Ti 3 C 2 T x- MXene and MXene/WS 2 nanomaterials, revealing CV curves indicative of good EDLC behavior, resembling a double-layer capacitor. WS 2 -GCE, MXene-GCE, and MXene/WS 2 -GCE exhibited low charge transfer resistance (R ct ) values of 5.25 Ω, 3.41 Ω and 2.29 Ω, respectively, alongside maximum C s values of 47 F/g (WS 2 -GCE), 71 F/g (MXene-GCE) and 373 F/g (MXene/WS 2 -GCE) achieved at current densities of 0.4 A/g for each material.  The performance of the MXene/WS 2 nanocomposite on the GCE electrode can be attributed to several key factors related to its composition and structure. MXene's high electrical conductivity facilitates efficient electron transfer during electrochemical reactions, while WS₂ enhances performance by providing a large surface area and excellent catalytic properties. The combination of these materials, along with the use of polyvinylidene fluoride as a binder in the modification process, improves the composite's adhesion to the GCE surface, enhancing the electrode's mechanical stability and electrochemical performance. The high capacitance of the MXene/WS₂ composite results from the synergy between its components, surpassing similar previous studies. Its 2D structure promotes electron and ion transport, with MXene sheets forming a conductive network and channels that improve ionic mobility. This design increases active sites for WS 2 , enhances electrode-electrolyte contact, and enables efficient ion diffusion and electron transport during charge/discharge cycles. We anticipate that the efficient performance of the MXene/WS 2 composite will contribute to the advancement of other TMDs and MXene-based materials for supercapacitor applications. Additionally, this composite has the potential to extend its applications to areas such as separation, adsorption, catalysis, and electrochemical sensing.

title: 2,6-Diaminoanthraquinone modified MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/graphene as the negative electrode materials for ionic liquid-based asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Li Sun, Lujia Chai, Liangqi Jing, Yujuan Chen, Kelei Zhuo, Jianji Wang
conclusion: In summary, DAAQ-modified MXene and graphene composites (DAAQ-M/G-y ) were successfully fabricated through covalent and non-covalent interactions. DAAQ-M/G-40 as the negative electrode exhibits an outstanding specific capacitance of 226 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 in EmimBF4 electrolyte, which is mainly due to the high electronic conductivity and added Faradaic contribution. Anchored-DAAQ with redox activity can undergo fast reversible Faradaic reactions to contribute capacity. At the mass-balancing mass-ratio of the negative and positive electrodes, the HQ-RGO-360//DAAQ-M/G-40 ASC device delivered a high energy density of 43 Wh kg−1 with an excellent cycle stability. MXene-based composites modified by organic molecules would provide alternative electrode materials for developing excellent energy storage devices. title: Significantly enhanced electrochemical performance of Al-Ti3C2Tx MXene synthesized from Al-Ti3AlC2 MAX phase
authors: Haiyan Chen, Kefan Chen, Mingqing Lai, Ping Cai, Lixian Sun, Ruixiang Gao, Yaoben Xu, Siyuan Li, Tangyou Sun, Fen Xu, Hongliang Peng
conclusion: In conclusion, Ti3 AlC2 and Al-Ti3 AlC2 MAX phases were used to synthesize Ti3 C2 Tx and Al-Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes, respectively, by the same method of HF:HCl etching and LiCl intercalation. The freestanding Ti3 C2 Tx and Al-Ti3 C2 Tx film electrodes were further prepared through vacuum filtration from the Ti3 C2 Tx and Al-Ti3 C2 Tx dispersions. Compared with the Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode, the Al-Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode with slightly increased interlayer spacing and obviously higher conductivity offers more efficient ions transport and charge transfer, thereby achieving significantly enhanced electrochemical performance. The Al-Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode achieves enhanced capacitance (399 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ) and higher rate performance (63.6 % retention from 1 to 10 A g−1 ). Moreover, the Al-Ti3 C2 Tx -based flexible sandwiched supercapacitor also exhibits superior energy storage performance. The impressive results indicate that Al-Ti3 C2 Tx MXene synthesized from Al-Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase possesses the great application potential in flexible supercapacitors. title: VOx anchored Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructures for high-performance 2.2 V supercapacitors
authors: Kiran Kumar Garlapati, Surendra K. Martha, Bharat B. Panigrahi
conclusion: In summary, this work presents the synthesis of VOx -anchored Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes via solvothermal followed by an annealing process for supercapacitor applications. Pure vanadium oxide synthesis results in the formation of VO2 porous spheres, and heterostructure synthesis shows VO2 porous spheres, V2 O3 porous rods, and uniformly grown VOx on Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes, as confirmed by HRTEM. The decomposition of Ti3 C2 Tx surface functional groups and entrapped H2 gas creates a reducing environment during annealing, leading to the growth of quasi-metallic V2 O3 along with semi-conducting VO2, as elucidated from ex-situ synthesis and DSC analysis. The heterostructure of VOx anchored Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes benefits from the (i) metallic conductive Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes and quasi-metallic V2 O3 for quick e− transfer, (ii) more redox active sites offered mixed phase formation of VO2 and V2 O3 and (iii) layered structure of Ti3 C2 Tx to permit easy electrolyte ions migration into the electrode. The optimized heterostructure VOx M2 delivers a higher specific capacitance of 364 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 than pure VO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx in a stable voltage window of 1.9 V owing to the high decomposition potential of 0.5 M K2 SO4 electrolyte and intrinsic activation barrier of VOx anchored Ti3 C2 Tx electrode. The developed SSC delivers an energy density of 45.7 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1.1 kW kg−1 with 78 % capacity retention after 10000 cycles. The SSC shows a stable open circuit voltage of 1.34 V after 12 h with a leakage current of 0.09 mA cm−2 owing to the SSC's vanadium redox couple-driven pseudocapacitive charge storage mechanism. title: A review of how to improve Ti3C2Tx MXene stability
authors: Wei Cao, Junli Nie, Ye Cao, Chengjie Gao, Mingsheng Wang, Weiwei Wang, Xiaoli Lu, Xiaohua Ma, Peng Zhong
conclusion: 5  Summary and outlook  Recently, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene has attracted considerable attention in many fields, such as energy, electronics, and biomedicine, due to its excellent electrical, optical, mechanical, and catalytic properties, and so on. However, the degradation of MXene into TiO 2 and amorphous carbon by exposure to air and water can significantly compromise the microstructure of the material, thus reducing its physical and chemical properties in a myriad of ways. Consequently, the large-scale synthesis of MXene and its practical applications are severely constrained. Thus, effective measures to slow or inhibit the degradation of MXene are urgently called for to ensure its extended service life in natural and extreme environments. This review begins with a brief introduction to MXenes, which serves to show their structures and synthesis processes, as well as the areas where they can be applied. Secondly, the degradation mechanism of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene are discussed, focusing on oxidation and hydrolysis. Oxidation and hydrolysis are the main degradation reactions for MXene in the environment, which always initiate from defective sites of MXene. Upon exposure to harmful factors (e.g., water and/or oxygen), MXene might undergo microscopic changes in morphologies, structures, and surface functional groups etc, which further influence the diverse properties and applications of this unique material. It is of great importance to unveil the degradation mechanisms of MXene from the angle of microstructural evolutions, so as to find targeted methods to enhance the MXene stability. Thirdly, MXene has attracted great attentions because of its excellent physicochemical properties and thus the wide applications. The effects of MXene degradation on its electronic, optical, mechanical, and catalytic properties are comprehensively discussed. The changes in physical and chemical properties of MXene are mainly attributed to its variations of morphologies, structures, and surface functional groups, e.g., the formation of cavities and TiO 2 nanoparticles on the surface of MXene, and changes in terminal compositions and proportions. Finally, the current strategies to improve the stability of MXene are systematically summarized. These strategies can be divided into four main categories: optimization of the MXene preparation process, post-processing of MXene, promoting the storage environment of MXene, and encapsulation of MXene.   (1)  Several specific methods can be employed to optimize the preparation process of MXene so as to obtain a high-quality product. By selecting a high-quality MAX phase, the surface of the as-synthesized MXene would have few defective sites after etching, leading to substantially enhanced MXene stability due to the improved quality of the material itself. By selecting an appropriate etchant and dosage, the terminal type and proportion of MXene (i.e., −F, –OH, −O) can be directly adjusted during synthesis. Generally, the oxygen-terminated MXene shows higher stability than the fluoride-terminated one. However, it should be noted that the surface functional groups greatly influence the specific properties of MXene. For example, the −F functional group promotes the electrical conductivity of MXene, while the −O group gives MXene a higher electrocatalytic activity. Different etchants and dosages can be used selectively by balancing the stability and required properties. Large lateral sizes of MXene are closely related to high conductivity and stability due to high-quality single crystals. Preparing large-size sheets could guarantee ideal stability for MXene. However, in some cases, the sizes of MXene need to be tailored within an optimal range to adapt to specific applications. For example, as for the MXene ink for inject printing, the MXene sizes should be controlled to less than 1 μm due to the limit of the nozzle size. For electrocatalysis, the MXene sheets with small sizes provide plentiful active sites, resulting in enhanced catalytic performance. Meanwhile, many defective sites exist in the small-size MXene, which might induce decreased stability.    (2)  After the synthesis of MXene, post-treatments could be employed to enhance its stability, including ionic shielding of the MXene edges or surfaces, surface modification, annealing treatments, and the formation of MXene-based composites. The surface of MXene is negatively charged due to the presence of functional groups, while the edges of MXene have been shown to be positively charged. Degradation often initiates at the edges first. The use of anionic surfactants or polyanionic salts in combination with positively charged edges can largely prevent water and oxygen from intruding into the MXene. However, the introduction of these substances might also affect the electrical conductivity and other properties of MXene. In addition, cations can be employed to interact with the negatively charged surface of MXene, which forms a dense shielding layer to block water and oxygen. Similarly, surface modification can be employed to impede water intrusion into MXene by grafting hydrophobic substances onto the MXene surface. However, the poor dispersion of the modified MXene in solutions might restrict the applications. Annealing is an effective method for removing residual water molecules at the interlayers of MXene nanosheets. With an appropriate temperature and duration, a protective layer could also be formed on the MXene surface, thereby enhancing its stability. Given the limitations of stability and functionality for individual MXene, the use of MXene-based composites is a feasible and facile option to prolong MXene life. Nanocomposites can provide a quick way to enhance the stability of MXene by taking advantage of the antioxidant properties of other materials.    (3)  Once MXene has been prepared, it is necessary to consider whether it can be stored for an extended period, whether the properties of the material change after long-term storage and so on. These factors would directly affect the large-scale production and commercial applications of MXene. Optimizing the storage environment of MXene can enhance the long-term stability of the material through the use of simple operations    (4)  In addition to optimizing the stability of MXene itself, it is also possible to consider the use of commercial processes to treat MXene-based devices. One such process is the encapsulation technology, which can be used to separate the device from the external environment. The encapsulation can effectively exclude the intrusion of water and oxygen, enhancing the stability of the MXene device in various environments. However, the research on the use of existing mature processes to enhance the stability of MXene still needs to be sufficiently comprehensive and systematic. A more detailed and extensive investigation of mature processes to deal with MXene-based devices would greatly facilitate the commercialization of MXene.     Although many methods have been developed to enhance the environmental stability of Ti 3 C 2 T x , from material synthesis and storage to applications, the role that one single strategy is limited. However, few reports on enhancements of the MXene stability by combining multiple strategies. One simple example is the first synthesis of a high-quality MAX phase, which can secondly be etched by selecting the appropriate etchant and dosage, followed by a heat treatment to remove the excess water molecules. It is anticipated that a combination of a series of suitable techniques would render the synthesized MXene with substantially enhanced stability. However, it remains unclear whether the various treatments will interact with one another and whether subsequent treatment operations will compromise the efficacy of previous ones. Further in-depth research and analysis in this area may facilitate the development of MXene with optimal environmental stability through a limited number of operations.  In addition, the accelerated advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) in recent years, driven by its extensive data collection and sophisticated computational capabilities, can be projected to research the stability of MXene and its family. The application of AI for deep learning and analysis of MXene degradation mechanisms would prompt AI to learn, analyze, and use its powerful computational ability to predict effective methods to enhance the stability of MXenes. Furthermore, it is important to deepen our understanding of the degradation mechanisms of MXene. As the research depth and analysis methods for materials continue to evolve, it is essential to carry out deeper study of the degradation mechanism of MXene in line with technological advancements. For example, the continuous development of in - situ characterizations and deep learning simulation might enable more effective and in-depth studies. A deeper understanding is expected about how MXene is invaded by oxygen, water and other adverse factors during the degradation process, how this invasion affects the surface of MXene, and what structural changes occur as a result. A comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the degradation mechanisms of MXene would enable researchers to more accurately and effectively direct their efforts towards stabilizing MXene.

conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In this work, hybrid supercapacitor electrode films were obtained using Ti 3 C 2 T  x  and nanodiamonds. The obtained capacitance was attributed mainly to the H + redox reaction with O terminations. In comparison to the pure Ti 3 C 2 T  x  film, the excellent performance of the Ti 3 C 2 T  x  /NDs-10% is due to the pillaring effect that effectively prevented the restacking of the MXene sheets. Current investigations have verified that integrating the T-MCs with MXenes improves an ion transportation channel and steadies the electrode structure, whereas the combination of MOFs permits the hierarchical porosity and better mechanical strength. title: Recyclable PVA/starch/Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposite films with superior mechanical and barrier properties
authors: Ming Dong, Emiliano Bilotti, Han Zhang, Dimitrios G. Papageorgiou
conclusion: This study investigated the fabrication and characterization of PVA/starch/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanocomposite films, focusing on their mechanical, barrier, and recyclability properties. The addition of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene into the PVA/starch blend significantly enhanced the composite films' mechanical strength, water resistance, and oxygen and water vapor barrier performance. Specifically, the addition of MXene led to notable increases in Young's modulus and tensile strength, as well as a dramatic reduction in water vapor and oxygen permeability. These improvements are attributed to the effective dispersion and alignment of MXene nanoplatelets, which create more tortuous pathways for gas and moisture molecules, improving the film's barrier properties. The recyclability of the PVA/starch/Ti3 C2 Tx films was also demonstrated, with only minor reductions in mechanical and barrier properties after recycling. This finding highlights the strong potential of these nanocomposite films for sustainable applications, as they can be recycled without significant loss of performance, supporting environmental sustainability and the circular economy. Overall, the study establishes Ti3 C2 Tx MXene as a highly effective reinforcing nanofiller for PVA/starch blends, offering a promising solution for developing high-performance, biodegradable, and recyclable packaging materials. These findings open up new possibilities for the use of MXene-reinforced biopolymers in various industrial applications, particularly in packaging, where both mechanical strength and barrier properties are crucial. Among the synthesized MXene-based films (MX-14, MX-35, MX-47), the thinner MX-14 film demonstrated superior electrochemical performance in a 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte. The c-LP of Mo2 C MXene, estimated based on (002) peak, was calculated to be ∼ 16.3 Å The FESEM images displayed the multilayered structure of Mo2 C MXene with well-aligned nanosheets exhibiting large surface area. From cyclic voltammograms, the pseudocapacitive nature of the MXene-based electrode was specified by the presence of oxidation/reduction or redox peakes and non-rectangular shape of area under the curves. The large-scale diffusion of electrolyte ions, excellent electronic conductivity and minimum charge transfer resistance was displayed by EIS Nyquist plots. It was determined from the XRD, that TGO-based samples, such as TGO-MnO2 and TGO-3 % FeNi-MnO2 , showed a mixed phase of tetragonal α-MnO2 and cubic α-Mn2 O3 . The TC-based samples, namely TC-MnO2 and TC-3 % FeNi-MnO2 , exhibited an identical mixed-phase structure. title: Metal-organic framework–derived NiCo2S4@Co3S4 yolk-shell nanocages/Ti3C2Tx MXene for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors

Furthermore, the novel structure of NiCo2 S4 @Co3 S4 /Ti3 C2 Tx composite as electrode material could accelerate the thermodynamic stability, suppress the textural instability, and moderate the unavoidable volume change of active substance. Benefited from the above merits, the NiCo2 S4 @Co3 S4 /Ti3 C2 Tx electrode demonstrates a significant specific capacitance (1872 F g−1 at 2 mV s−1 ), and remarkable rate capability in the high current density that combine with low resistance and outstanding pseudo-capacitance. title: Modulation of biaxial strains on the optical responses of defective Ti3C2 Tx (T = F, O, OH) MXenes
authors: Yulong Zhang, Zhongwei Zhao, Jieyun Yan, Huajie Song, Wenting Lv, Yu Yang
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, we investigate the effects of biaxial strains on the electronic and optical properties of three typical functionalized MXenes Ti 3 C 2 F 2 , Ti 3 C 2 O 2 and Ti 3 C 2 (OH) 2 with hole defects. On the whole, the strain makes the optical absorption coefficient of ultraviolet region decrease obviously. For Ti 3 C 2 F 2 , with the increase of strain, the F p-orbital energy range shrinks gradually, and the peak of optical absorption coefficient gradually shifts to the low energy end. For Ti 3 C 2 O 2 , the regulation of strain on the low energy end of infrared region, visible region and ultraviolet region is not monotonous, but for the high energy end of ultraviolet region, the principle of absorption coefficient is lower with greater strain. The P1 defect causes the main peak to split, while the H1 defect makes the absorption curve smoother for both of them. For Ti 3 C 2 (OH) 2 , the strain not only affects the ultraviolet region, but also the infrared region and the visible region in the plane direction. At the same time, P1 defect and H1 defect can significantly reduce the absorption peak of Ti 3 C 2 (OH) 2 in the range of 4 eV–6 eV. These results will further improve the identification of defects in MXenes under strain conditions and help to establish the relationship between defects and optical response in real situations.

title: Design of NiCoMn-OH@Ti3C2Tx composite electrode with hollow rhombic dodecahedral structure for efficient supercapacitor

The NiCoMn-OH@Ti3 C2 Tx electrode exhibits the dodecahedral hollow structure covered with nanosheets of Ti3 C2 Tx , which enhances both its capacity behavior and conductivity compared to the original NiCoMn-OH electrode. title: Experimental and DFT investigations on multifunctional Ti3C2Tx MXenes/PDAAQ free standing interlayer for enhancing the cycle life and high-rate performance of Na–S batteries

conclusion: In summary, the utilization of MXene/PDAAQ film as an interlayer has significantly improved electrochemical performance of Na–S battery. The conductive MXene layer acts as an effective sulfur host, promoting redox reactions while restricting polysulfide migration. Concurrently, the PDAAQ functions as a trapper for Na+ ions. The discharge capacity for MXene/PDAAQ remained at 1002.8 mAh g−1 after 160 cycles at a current density of 1 C (C = 1675 mAh g−1 ). In comparison, the cells that solely contained MXene or PDAAQ recorded a discharge capacity of 848.9 mAh g−1 and 651.3 mAh g−1 after 160 cycles which is significantly lower than that of the MXene/PDAAQ cell. Additionally, according DFT calculations, MXene layer functions as a catalytic surface for the dissociation of polysulfide chains. Moreover, the combination of MXene with PDAAQ as an efficient interlayer, suggests a cost-effective processing method, presents a fresh perspective on the advancement of high-performance Na–S batteries. Future research ought to focus on the characteristics of electron transport. PDAAQ, which possesses redox activity, and MXenes, which have high electrical conductivity, can be utilized to enhance the electron transport properties of composite materials. The redox activity of DAAQ and the conductivity of MXene combine to increase electron transfer rates, which enables them for applications such as practical batteries for developing the new generation of EVs. title: Recent advances in supercapacitors based on carbon nanomaterials/MXene: Material design and functional integration
authors: Jinyuan Cao, Zhe Liu, Xuanxuan Wu, Jin Duan, Gege Hang, Yuxin Fu
conclusion: 7  Summary and outlook  This paper reviews recent research developments in carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites as supercapacitor electrodes. Overall, there have been significant breakthroughs in structural engineering between carbon nanomaterials and MXene over the past few years. The combined use of electrical double-layer carbon materials and pseudocapacitive MXene solves two major problems: self-stacking and oxidation of MXene. This synergy also drives the enhancement of other properties of supercapacitors, such as energy density, cycle life, rate performance, mechanical properties, low-temperature resistance, biocompatibility performance, and wearability. Carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites play a great role in flexible wearable supercapacitors, micro-supercapacitors, self-powered supercapacitors, and low-temperature resistant supercapacitors. The universality of the properties of carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites makes them worth being investigated in other applications.  Solving the problem of MXene self-stacking involves more than just interpolating spacer materials, as imprecise preparation methods often decrease the density of MXene-based composites, especially top-down methods. Ideal optimization of the MXene structure should enable precisely regulated layer spacing, providing enough space between layers to prevent stacking while keeping the spacing small enough to ensure high density and capacity. For the oxidation of MXene, adding antioxidants such as l -ascorbic acid and L-cysteine successfully solved this problem. The heating-free method circumvents the binding of MXene with oxygen in water or air. In-situ sacrificial metal templates (Zn, Fe, Al) as the reductant and crosslinking agent have been demonstrated to achieve the same antioxidant effect. Hence, it is necessary to investigate other sacrificial metal templates.  0D carbon nanoparticles/MXene composites are well suitable for the preparation of solar supercapacitors due to their excellent light harvesting and photothermal conversion capabilities. This will help to promote the multifunctional integration of practical supercapacitors. For 1D carbon nanomaterials, the high aspect ratios not only connect the MXene nanosheets to create a stable structure with high mechanical strength but also form a connecting ion-transportation channel, which is good for the electrical conductivity of the composite materials. The wide adaptability of CNT/MXene electrode materials can be concluded from the strategies of changing CNT structural features, introduction of third conductive materials, gelation, etc., which leads to a great potential for exploitation in other fabrication methods. Nanocellulose makes an excellent contribution to the mechanical properties of MXene composites, up to 340 MPa for films (cellulose nanofibers/MXene films) and 74 MPa for fibers (cellulose nanocrystals/MXene fibers). Due to the inherent insulating characteristics of nanocellulose, researchers generally introduce a third active substance to enhance the electrochemical properties of the composites. Currently, the conducting polymer has the greatest influence on the electrical conductivity, specific capacitance, and energy density of nanocellulose/MXene composites. For example, the MXene/CNF/PANI-based SSC exhibited a voltage window of 1.2 V, an ultra-high volume specific capacitance of 522 mF cm −2 (5 mA cm −2 ), and an energy density of 94.7 μWh cm −2 at power density of 573 μW cm −2 . For 2D rGO, improves overall interfacial structure, contributing to the expansion of the contact area between the electrolyte and the electrode material, which greatly increases the ion-accessible sites and improves the charge transfer efficiency. Especially in the preparation of gel composite electrodes, the 3D interconnect structure enables the material to maintain a capacitance retention rate of over 90 % after 10,000 cycles of charging/discharging, providing excellent long-term cycling stability. For 3D carbon materials, the multilevel pore properties make them show great advantages in material structure design. Derived carbon materials exhibit significant differences in interfacial effects when composited with MXene due to the diversity of precursor sources. Therefore, further investigation of the interfacial binding mechanisms of different precursor-derived carbons with MXene is of great scientific significance and application value for optimizing the electrochemical properties of the composites.  Overall, the main issues that still exist in the current development of supercapacitors are i) low energy density; ii) high cost and low yield; and iii) difficulty in meeting commercial-grade standards. Therefore, a better balance between the electrochemical performance, mechanical stability, and processing technology of SCs is still needed in the future. Here, the future development trend of SCs in terms of performance optimization is summarized ( Fig. 16  ):   1)  In recent years, Ti 3 C 2 T x /carbon nanomaterials have made significant progress in the field of energy storage, but there is a lack of research on other types of MXene (Zr 3 C 2 T x , Nb 2 CT x , Mo 2 CT x , etc.)/carbon nanomaterials composites. This research imbalance limits the overall optimization of MXene-based composite properties and the expansion of potential applications. Different species of MXene have unique electronic structures, surface chemistry and interlayer interactions. For example, Zr 3 C 2 T x exhibits enhanced oxidative stability, while Mo 2 CT x has a higher intrinsic conductivity. Therefore, the interfacial interactions between various MXene and carbon nanomaterials need to be investigated;    2)  Surface modification is used to modulate the microstructure of materials to stimulate the maximum potential of MXene-based materials. For example, the density and distribution of defects on the surface of the material can be precisely controlled by plasma treatment and chemical vapor deposition to build abundant active sites. The electronic conduction efficiency and ion diffusion kinetics of the electrode materials can be effectively improved by modulating the type and concentration of surface termination groups (e.g. -OH, -COOH, Cl, etc.). Or doping with heteroatoms to modulate the electronic structure of the composite material. The doping of heteroatoms such as N, P, and S has already appeared, in the future, we can continue to explore the enhancement effect of doping with other heteroatoms;    3)  Binary composites are limited by the limited properties of the materials and not as good as ternary composites or multicomposites. Ternary composites are able to achieve a good balance between the preparation strategy and the electrochemical and mechanical properties of the materials through the multidimensional charge transport network, hierarchical structural design and synergistic reinforcement of the materials. Currently, conductive polymers (e.g., PANI) contribute significantly to the specific capacitance and energy density of carbon nanomaterials/MXene-based SCs, but the cycling stability of SCs is poor. Therefore, a combination of advanced characterization and intelligent algorithms is needed to achieve accurate and practical material design;    4)  Currently, interlayers, stacked structures, core-shell structures, honeycomb structures, cellular lattice networks, and dot-wire-sheet hetero-structured fibers have greatly influenced the properties of MXene-based hybrid electrodes. Therefore, building precise 3D porous interconnections to expose active sites and mitigate the volume expansion effect, is a key strategy to improve the performance of carbon nanomaterials/MXene-based SCs;    5)  Nanocellulose is a promising carbon nanomaterial because it is in line with the requirements of sustainable development. Currently, the application of CNC in MXene composites has not been fully explored. CNC can not only significantly enhance the mechanical properties of the materials, but also act as a spatial stabiliser to effectively inhibit the stacking of MXene flakes. CNF and BC have similar effects and are biocompatible, which can provide a new research direction for the development of high-performance MXene-based composites;    6)  Advanced manufacturing technologies such as microfluidic spinning and 3D printing can be used to accurately construct the microstructure (including orientation arrangement, pore distribution and interfacial interactions) and multi-scale morphology (such as fiber, film, or three-dimensional porous network structure) of carbon nanomaterial/MXene composites, thereby achieve the directional optimization of the electrical conductivity, mechanical and electrochemical properties of the composites;    7)  The limitation of the low energy density of MSCs can be broken through by studying multi-scale regulation strategies such as hybrid electrode combinations and new electrolyte systems;    8)  For different application scenarios such as flexible wearable and self-powered systems, the development of multifunctional MXene-based supercapacitors that combine high energy density, excellent mechanical flexibility and environmental adaptability will be a promising direction. For example, biological supercapacitors (BSCs) can be integrated with various energy capture technologies such as sweat energy harvesting and solar energy conversion. The unity of efficient energy storage and self-powering is achieved by integrating biocompatible electrode materials and clever supercapacitor structural design;    9)  Both the synthesis strategy of composite electrode materials and the fabrication method of SCs should aim at saving more time and cost with multiple advantages such as simpler, finer, more efficient, and more convenient.

title: Microfluidic-oriented assembly of MXene composite fibers for flexible zinc ion supercapacitors with high energy density
authors: Fanyu Xie, Yuan Du, Menghan Chu, Xiaoyu Jia, Hui Cao, Rui Zhang, Hongwei Li, Mei Zhang
conclusion: In summary, the three-dimensional rGO/ MXene fibers with the ordered sheets were fabricated by microfluidic combined wet spinning technology. The constructed flexible symmetric supercapacitors exhibit a high specific areal capacitance of 1613 mF cm−2 in PVA/H2 SO4 electrolyte. 70 % rGO/MXene@Zn fibers as anode materials were prepared by electrochemical deposition method to assemble the high-performance ZIHSCs in PVA/Zn(CF3 SO3 )2 gel electrolyte. The flexible ZIHSCs expand the operating voltage window of 0–1.6 V and realize a high specific areal capacitance as high as 1180 mF cm−2 , which achieve an excellent energy densigy of 104.9 μWh cm−2 , outstanding bending stability and good capacitance retention of 90 % after 6500 cycles. The multiple ZIHSCs in series further expand the energy outputs for practical applications in wearable electronic area. Three-dimensional network structure with the axial ordered sheets and good interfacial effect of cathode materials, and the optimized anode electrode contribute the superior electrochemical performance of ZIHSCs. This research proposes an avenue for the controllable construction of the advanced fiber electrode and high-performance zinc ion supercapacitors, broadening the practical application for wearable electronics. title: A novel strategy for high energy density supercapacitors: Formation of cyanuric acid between Ti3C2Tx (MXene) interlayer hybrid electrodes
authors: Chao Feng, Bingzhe Jia, Han Wang, Yan Wang, Xinming Wu
conclusion: during the formation of Ti3 C2 Tx /CA composite electrode, CA replaced the -F group that does not participate in the pseudocapacitive reaction, but did not change the original –OH and -O groups, and the pseudo capacitance of MXene was fully retained [13,21–23,45] . In addition, thanks to the unique hydroxyl structure of CA terminal and symmetry of CA, CA can form short chains during charging in aqueous electrolytes and the formation of short chains can realize the storage of electrons. At the same time, the formation of short chains further provides a large number of new pseudocapacitive reaction sites for MXene and the highly electronegative N and O atoms in CA also improve the electric double layer capacitor of the composite electrode to a certain extent. Therefore, the energy density of Ti3 C2 Tx /CA composite electrode (51.1 Wh kg−1 ) is much higher than that of Ti3 C2 Tx electrode (29.7 Wh kg−1 ) (Fig. 5 (e), Table S3 and Table S4 ). 4 Conclusions In summary, we synthesized a novel highly N-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene through multi-step reaction by introducing small organic molecules, dicyandiamide, into the interlayer of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Benefiting from the unique hydroxyl structure and symmetry of CA terminal, CA enables charge storage by forming short chains, providing new pseudocapacitive reaction sites and higher bilayer capacitance. The prepared Ti3 C2 Tx /CA composite electrode has a high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability. More notably, it achieves an amazing energy density of 51.1 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 2000 W kg−1 , which exceeds the energy density of MXene based electrode reported in the current literature. This work provides a new idea for the design of commercial MXene based electrodes by the method of Ti3 C2 Tx doping with small organic molecules.

title: Ti3C2Tx-MXene based 2D/3D Ti3C2–TiO2–CuTiO3 heterostructure for enhanced pseudocapacitive performance
authors: Muhammad Noman, Mirza Mahmood Baig, Qazi Muhammad Saqib, Swapnil R. Patil, Chandrashekhar S. Patil, Jungmin Kim, Youngbin Ko, Eunho Lee, Jinwoo Hwang, Seung Goo Lee, Jinho Bae
conclusion: In this paper, we have demonstrated that the pseudocapacitive charge storage of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene can be significantly improved by developing oxidation-controlled MXene-derived 2D/3D heterostructures via a two-step process. In the first step, partial oxidation led to the formation of in-situ 3D floral Ti3 C2 –TiO2 nanoribbons. Afterward, in the second step, further controlled oxidation in the presence of Cu ions successfully transformed these 3D floral nanoribbons into a 2D/3D Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 heterostructure. This transformation harnessed the synergistic effects of MXene, TiO2 , and CuTiO3 , which resulted in increased interlayer spacing, a higher concentration of redox-active sites, and mitigation of the conductivity issues associated with TiO2 nanoribbons. At an applied current density of 2 mA/cm2 , the Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 heterostructure exhibited a notably improved capacitance, achieving 599.2 mF/cm2 (437.3F/g @ 1.46 A/g), surpassing both the pure MXene 249.16 mF/cm2 (158.7F/g @ 1.46 A/g) and the 3D floral Ti3 C2 –TiO2 nanoribbons 498.5 mF/cm2 (352.1F/g @ 1.46 A/g). Furthermore, the practical application of this material was demonstrated through the fabrication of an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device, Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 //AC, which achieved an energy density of 31.1 Wh/kg, power density of 1041.7 W/kg and capacitance retention of 83.7 % after 5000 continuous charging/discharging cycles. These findings highlight the potential of the controlled oxidation technique to develop MXene-derived 2D/3D Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 heterostructures, enhancing the pseudocapacitive properties. title: High-performance flexible supercapacitor based on PEDOT:PSS wrapped delaminated Ti3C2Tx composite: Experimental and DFT validation
authors: Gourab Nandy, Swati Shaw, Subhradip Ghosh, Ashok Kumar Dasmahapatra
conclusion: In this work, we have adequately synthesized delaminated Ti3 C2 Tx (d-Ti3 C2 Tx ) by a low-cost method, integrating the mixed acid etching method followed by DMSO intercalation. Furthermore, PP/d-Ti3 C2 Tx binary composites have been prepared with different ratios by the solvent mixing method and coated on the flexible activated carbon cloth. The conformation of the prepared composites was validated by several characterization techniques such as XRD, RAMAN, UV–Vis, FTIR, FESEM, EDS, and FETEM. In three electrodes electrochemical performance PP, and d-Ti3 C2 Tx with a ratio 1:2 respectively (P1M2) exhibit great results in 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte. The P1M2 electrode shows a brilliant specific capacitance value of 741. 23 F g−1 at a scan rate of 5 mV/s, and 718. 67 F g−1 at a current density of 3. 5 A g−1 . P1M2 electrode shows brilliant E s 35. 93 Whkg−1 (at P s 1049. 90 Wkg-1 ), and 5. 68 Whkg−1 (at Ps 5996. 48 Wkg-1 ). Detailed DFT calculations confirmed that the charge transfer is doubled in the case of PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx in comparison to PEDOT@Ti3 C2 Tx . The charges flow from PEDOT and MXene to PSS. Consequently, PSS possesses the electron-rich region. The DFT calculated solar absorption spectrum for PEDOT:PSS, Ti3 C2 Tx , and PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx agree very well with the experiments. Such excellent agreement substantiates the proposed morphology of the composite i.e. PEDOT wrapped d-Ti3 C2 Tx , aided by multiple PSS carrier pathways. For a flexible and wearable electronic device, we prepared a P1M2-P1M2 SSC and a P1M2-rGO ASC assembly using a gel electrolyte (PVA-H2 SO4 ). The highest specific capacitance has been achieved at 260. 23 F g−1 (at 0. 5 A g−1 ) by the P1M2-P1M2 SSC device; whereas P1M2-rGO ASC has a value of 176. 46 F g−1 (at 0. 1 A g−1 ). The specific energy (specific power) was from 13. 01 Whkg−1 (600 Wkg-1 ) to 2. 63 Whkg−1 (12035 Wkg-1 ) for the SSC device; and from 35. 29 Whkg−1 (240 Wkg-1 ) to 26. 22 Whkg−1 (1200 Wkg-1 ) for ASC device. Both SSC and ASC exhibit excellent performance over various bending and twisting cycles, ASC can operate in a larger potential window and longer durations at low current regions. Moreover, the ASC device shows excellent specific capacitance retention of 89.03 % for 5000 GCD cycles. Subsequently, a red LED was glowed using three ASC devices in series. Hence the P1M2 electrode possesses enormous potential to be used in portable and wearable electronics. title: Hierarchical MXene/NiCo2S4 electrodes derived from MXene/ZIF-67 composites for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Jiawei Wu, Yuanqing Chen, Xujiang Liang, Haolin Dong, Ying Zhang, Huan Cao, Weibai Bian
conclusion: To summarize, the MXene/NiCo2 S4 composite material, synthesized using MXene/ZIF-67 as a precursor, boasts a distinctive structure and morphology. This composite is characterized by spherical NiCo2 S4 nanoparticles that are uniformly loaded onto MXene nanosheets. This architecture not only provides a large specific surface area but also enriches the number of active sites. Leveraging the synergistic effects between the 3D nanospheres and 2D MXene nanosheets, the MXene/NiCo2 S4 composite delivers exceptional electrochemical performance. Specifically, at a current density of 3 mA/cm2 , the area-specific capacity reaches an impressive 1.99 mAh/cm2 , representing a nearly threefold increase compared to its pre-sulfidation state. Moreover, the CV curves maintain excellent symmetry across various scan rates, underscoring the composite’s superior rate capability. After undergoing 10000 charge-discharge cycles, the composite retains 86.17% of its initial capacity, highlighting its remarkable cycling stability. Of even greater significance is the MNCS-1//AC HSC hybrid supercapacitor device assembled from this composite. The voltage windows of the positive and negative electrodes are well-aligned, ensuring efficient energy storage. The CV curves remain stable across different scan rates, and the area-specific capacity peaks at 2.73 mAh/cm2 within a current density range of 5 to 30 mA/cm2 . After 10000 cycles, the device retains 86.19% of its initial capacity. It achieves a maximum energy density of 0.97 mWh/cm2 and a power density of 34.20 mW/cm2 , outperforming numerous previously studied supercapacitor devices. Investigations into the energy storage mechanism reveal that the electrochemical reactions of MXene/NiCo2 S4 are predominantly governed by diffusion-controlled battery-type behavior. This allows ions to penetrate deep into the bulk of the material, facilitating reactions and endowing the composite with robust energy storage capabilities. Beyond its material innovations, this study successfully fabricates high-performance composite electrode materials, offering new directions for the design and preparation of supercapacitor electrodes. title: Optimization of MXene/CNT free-standing composite electrodes for enhanced electrochemical performance in symmetric supercapacitors
authors: Yasar Ozkan Yesilbag, Ahmed Jalal Salih Salih
conclusion: This study demonstrates that MXene/CNT composite electrodes, particularly the MX1 electrode with 10 % CNT content, exhibit superior electrochemical and structural properties for energy storage applications. The homogeneous distribution of CNTs within the MXene matrix enhances interlayer spacing, improves ion diffusion, and maintains electrode flexibility without compromising structural integrity. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the MX1 electrode outperforms others in terms of specific capacitance, rate capability, and cycle stability, achieving the highest specific capacitance of 254 F g⁻1 at 0.5 A g⁻1 and retaining 85 % of its capacitance after 5000 cycles. Additionally, the SSC assembled with the MX1 electrode performs efficiently at high voltages and low scan rates, achieving a power density of 13.9 kW kg⁻1 and an energy density of 14.1 Wh kg⁻1 . These findings highlight the significance of optimizing CNT content and electrode architecture to achieve high-performance energy storage systems. title: Tailoring surface terminals of Ti3C2Tx MXene microgels via interlayer domain-confined polyphosphate ammonium for flexible supercapacitor applications
authors: Yongfang Liang, Hailong Shen, Jianghai Li, Hongying Zhao, Jiaheng Xu, Haifu Huang, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Jin Guo
conclusion: In summary, we design a simple interlayer domain-confined strategy to widen the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene interlayer spacing and trigger its microgelation via cross-linking APP between layers. The APP not only acts as a binder to induce Ti3 C2 Tx gelation, but also provides both nitrogen and phosphorus sources for MXene. Furthermore, this allows us to effortlessly assemble Ti3 C2 Tx microgels into MXene film electrodes. After heated at 350 °C for 3 h, the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h film has about 2.0 at.% nitrogen doping and 0.89 at.% phosphorus doping, as well as the reduce of –F functional group. The nitrogen present in the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h sample is predominantly in the form of pyrrolic nitrogen (N2), which offers superior electrochemical performance enhancement. Additionally, the P atoms interact electrostatically with the surface –O groups, and the formation of P–O bonds enhances redox activity, providing more active sites for charge storage. DFT further indicates that the introduction of N and P atoms increases the density of electronic states near the Fermi level of Ti3 C2 Tx , predicting higher electronic conductivity. Consequently, the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h film exhibits remarkable mechanical flexibility and electrochemical properties. Specifically, the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h film electrode boasts a high specific capacitance of 597.8 F/g and exceptional cycling stability, maintaining 98.5 % of its performance even after 10,000 cycles. Moreover, a quasi-solid-state flexible Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h supercapacitor achieves an impressive energy density of 12.5 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 250 W kg−1 . Remarkably, its electrochemical properties remain virtually unchanged even under bending conditions. Therefore, Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h emerges as a promising candidate for high-performance flexible electrode materials in energy storage applications. This study presents a novel approach for MXene gelation and heteroatom doping, paving the way for enhanced electrochemical energy storage performance in MXene electrodes. title: Unlocking highly stable and reversible in-situ integration of defect-rich 2D vanadium sulfide with Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructures: Boosting asymmetric supercapacitor performance
authors: Rohan B. Ambade, Swapnil B. Ambade, Ganesh Kumar Veerasubramani, Ki Hyun Lee, Yarjan Abdul Samad, Tae Hee Han
conclusion: In summary, in this study, we carefully demonstrated suitable strategies for integrating and chemically tailoring an interface using different materials at the nanoscale. It was demonstrated that 2D Ti3 C2 Tx -MX acts as a suitable hard template for the in-situ integration of sulfides (VS2 , in this study) via a controlled nucleation and growth strategy. The findings of this study indicate that integrated architectures have significant potential for maximizing the capacitive storage from 2D Ti3 C2 Tx -MX and VS2 through their synergistic effects. The 2D VS2 –Ti3 C2 Tx -MX heterostructures, when used as an electrode material for fabric-based supercapacitor application, exhibited excellent electrochemical performance (specific capacitance of 750 F g−1 ), a high rate-capability, and excellent long-term stability (∼93 % retention after 10000 cycles) in a three-electrode system. Our synthesis strategy is straightforward, offers high throughput, and is suitable for mass production. It should be noted that the VS2 –Ti3 C2 Tx -MX0.25 //Ti3 C2 Tx -MX ASC device provides a high capacitance, an excellent energy density of 52.08 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 750 W kg−1 , and prolonged cycling stability. Owing to the straightforward, simple, and scalable synthesis and fabrication strategy of the in-situ integration of the conductive heterostructures, excellent electrochemical performance in practical applications can be anticipated for other species, such as oxides, nitrides, chalcogenides, and conductive polymers, over the conductive framework of different pseudocapacitive materials and various other MXenes (V2 CTx , Mo2 CTx ). Furthermore, the electrochemical capability of the integrated VS2 –Ti3 C2 Tx -MX heterostructures can be extended to batteries and fuel cells by tuning their morphology and modifying their structural and electrical properties. Thus, we envisage that the facile, scalable, and straightforward approach of this work paves the way to designing advanced nanostructured electrodes for flexible high-performance electrochemical energy storage and conversion applications and next-generation electronic devices. title: Zn2+ ions induced gelation of low concentration Ti3C2Tx MXene under the confinement of melamine sponge and electric field as self-supporting electrode for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Debin Cai, Shuai Wu, Wenlong Yan, Li Guo, Yanzhong Wang
conclusion: In summary, MXene@MS hydrogels were synthesized via the gelation induced by Zn2+ in the three-dimensional structure of melamine sponge (MS) under the external electric field. The three-dimensional porous framework of MS is an ideal support for loading MXene@MS aerogels and thus enhancing their mechanical strength. The electrophoretic force generated by the electric field makes negative charge MXene nanosheets move to the positive electrode. At the same time, the zinc plate as positive electrode is oxidized and releases zinc ions, which induces the gelation of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets on the framework of MS. When the concentration of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets is only 6 mg mL-1 at the DC voltage of 3 V, the as-prepared MXene@MS aerogels exhibit high loading mass and mechanical strength. Due to the unique three-dimensional porous structure, the area capacitance of MXene@MS-3V-6 M is still as high as 610.77 m F cm-2 even at a high scan rate of 1000 mV s-1 , and the capacitance retention rate is 78.57 %, showing good rate performance. It is worth noting that the constructed asymmetric supercapacitor achieves high energy densities of 120.74 and 90.21 μWh cm-2 at power densities of 800 and 79,992 μW cm−2 , respectively. In addition, the capacitance retention can reach 93.37 % after 10,000 cycles, demonstrating high cycle stability. This paper presents a new method for preparing self-supporting MXene-based aerogels with high mechanical strength and electrochemical performance by using low-concentration MXene suspension. title: Dimensionally integrated hybrid films of Ti3C2Tx MXene and cellulose nanocrystals for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Seulgi Kim, Segi Byun, Seoyeon Yuk, Sunghee Choi, Sung Ho Song, Dongju Lee
journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
conclusion: We successfully developed freestanding hybrid film electrodes by integrating MXene and CNC, two low-dimensional materials, using a simple vacuum-filtration method. This solution-based mixing approach is highly versatile, cost-effective, and readily adaptable to other materials. MXene provides the fundamental properties and structure as a 2D material, while its properties have been enhanced through the incorporation of CNC, a 1D material. Notably, the inclusion of CNC in the hybrid electrodes led to significant improvements in both rate characteristics and lifespan, with increases of up to 45.5% and 24.8%, respectively. These enhancements are attributed to the increased accessibility of active sites for ion diffusion, due to the expanded interlayer spacing, and to the enhanced structural stability provided by CNC acting as mechanical support. This strategy demonstrates potential applicability in the fabrication of electrodes based on other 2D materials for future energy storage devices.

title: Gallium hydroxide coated Ti3C2Tx MXene for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitor
authors: Zhi Wan, Peilin Zuo, Zhiyuan Chen, Jizhou Yang, Mingxin Ren, Zhenghang Tian, Gangfeng Li, Peng Hu, Feng Teng, Haibo Fan
conclusion: In summary, we successfully synthesized GaOOH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene composites through a simple one-step hydrothermal method, utilizing an environmentally friendly and cost-effective approach. GaOOH nanorods grow uniformly on Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, and the combination of both materials prevents the self-stacking caused by van der Waals forces between the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene layers under optimal growth conditions. This not only increases the number of electrochemically active sites but also facilitates the rapid transport of ions and electrons. The synergistic effect of GaOOH and MXene's excellent electrical conductivity endows the GaOOH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene composites with outstanding electrochemical properties. Our results demonstrate that GaOOH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene exhibits a remarkable specific capacitance of 542 F·g−1 at a current density of 0.5 A·g−1 and an excellent cycling stability of 96.6 % after 5000 cycles. This study presents a strategy for optimizing the performance of MXene-based metal hydroxide electrode materials, paving the way for the development of high-performance electrode materials with significant potential for supercapacitor applications. title: Development of micro flower petal-structured NiCo2S4/Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets on nickel foam for superior supercapacitor applications
authors: Moo Young Jung, Hyobeen Cho, Ji-Won Son, Sankaiya Asaithambi, Yongseok Jun
journal: Journal of Industrial and Engineering Chemistry
conclusion: We successfully synthesized micro flower petal-like bimetallic NiCo2 S4 combined with the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheet as a binder-free electrode material using a nickel foam conductive substrate for high-performance hybrid supercapacitors. The synergistic effect of the spherical and micro flower petals on the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheet provides more active sites and electrolyte-available channels, augmenting the electrical conductivity and mitigating the internal resistance, thereby accelerating electron transport during electrochemical redox reactions. title: MoS2@Ti3C2Tx/GO heterostructure gelatin: Harnessing synergy for high-performance supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Yanan Liu, Luyao Wang, Wenhui Li, Junwei Huang, Hongna Xing, Juan Feng, Yan Zong, Xiuhong Zhu, Xinghua Li, Xinliang Zheng
conclusion: In summary, this work presents a novel hierarchical MoS2 @Ti3 C2 Tx /GO heterojunction gel synthesized via a synergistic 3D crosslinking and in-situ growth strategy. This design integrates three critical innovations: (1) a GO-bridged porous network preventing MXene restacking while retaining conductivity, (2) vertically aligned MoS2 nanoflowers acting as oxidation barriers and pseudocapacitive units, and (3) semiconductor-metal heterojunction interfaces enabling rapid ion/electron transport.
