title: Ti3C2Tx MXene integrated hollow carbon nanofibers with polypyrrole layers for MOF-derived freestanding electrodes of flexible asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Ishwor Pathak, Debendra Acharya, Kisan Chhetri, Prakash Chandra Lohani, Tae Hoon Ko, Alagan Muthurasu, Subhangi Subedi, Taewoo Kim, Syafiqah Saidin, Bipeen Dahal, Hak Yong Kim
conclusion: In summary, we synthesized Ti3 C2 TX MXenes and integrated them into hollow carbon nanofibers followed by outside-inside decoration of PPy layers. The as-prepared PPy@MXHCNF was sufficiently flexible, and highly conductive due to the MXene nanosheets and PPy layers, and it could be used as an efficient and novel material for making freestanding electrodes exhibiting robust performance in supercapacitors. Using the self-designed PPy@MXHCNF as a substrate, ZnCoMOF was grown, and both the cathode and anode materials were designed from the same bimetallic MOF via a controlled heat treatment process in a “two from one” strategy. The optimized positive electrode, ZCO@PPy@MXHCNF, delivered a Cs of 1567.5 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and outstanding cycling stability (91.2% retention after 10,000 cycles). Additionally, the negative electrode, NPC@MXHCNF, also furnished a high Cs of 477.21 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 with high capacitance retention (95.6%) after 10,000 GCD cycles. Utilizing the as-developed freestanding electrodes and a PVA-KOH electrolyte film, a flexible ASC device (ZCO@PPy@MXHCNF//NPC@MXHCNF) was assembled that delivered a Cs of 172.4 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 with 92.8 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles. The E of the device was 61.3 Wh kg−1 at a P of 796.8 W kg−1 . Hence, this work describes a facile technique for MXene modification, the use of PPy@MXHCNF as a novel electroactive substrate and ZnCoMOF grown on PPy@MXHCNF as a common template with which to design efficient cathodes and anodes for flexible asymmetric supercapacitors.

title: Influence of the synthesis protocol on the electrochemical properties of Ti3C2Tx MXene supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Vinícius dos Passos de Souza, Luís Marcelo Garcia da Silva, Rafael Kenji Nishihora, Sydney Ferreira Santos
conclusion: In this study, we investigated the effects of different fluorine sources on the synthesis of Ti3 C2 MXene from Ti3 AlC2 . Initially, we explored a mixed fluoride system consisting of NaF and LiF to enhance delamination. This approach was based on the trend in solvation radii (Li+ > Na+ > K+ ), where a smaller solvation radius for [Na(H₂O)]+ , combined with a larger one for [Li(H₂O)]+ , was expected to improve delamination efficiency, as seen in the XRD (Fig. 1 ). Electrochemical characterizations, including cyclic voltammetry, chronoamperometry, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), revealed the crucial role of surface terminations in ion transport. Among the tested materials, the Ti3 C2 Tx sample synthesized with LiF alone exhibited superior performance, with a high initial capacitance of approximately 380 F/g and a progressive increase to 800 F/g after 1800 cycles—a 210 % enhancement. This represents a significant advancement compared to previous reports, where increases typically did not exceed 170 %. In contrast, the mixed-fluoride systems, despite promoting exfoliation, resulted in lower capacitance values. This decrease was attributed to less favorable surface chemistry, as confirmed by XPS analysis. The Ti3 C2 Tx -LiF sample exhibited higher concentrations of F and Cl terminations, which are associated with enhanced electrochemical stability and performance. title: The effect of mild oxidation induced by heat treatment on the pseudocapacitance performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Jiaheng Xu, Yiwei Lu, Hongying Zhao, Lin Li, Hailong Shen, Yi Fan, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Zhiqiang Lan, Haifu Huang
conclusion: In summary, this study employed a straightforward thermal treatment strategy to mildly oxidize the surface of MXene, enabling the in-situ construction of Ti3 C2 Tx /TiO2 heterostructures that enhance the material's electrochemical performance. The results demonstrate that the mass-specific capacitance of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx reaches 358.29 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , while thermal modification induces varying degrees of improvement. Optimal performance is achieved through 3-hour annealing at 300 °C, yielding a maximum specific capacitance of 394.10 F g−1 . Remarkably, the thermally treated MXene maintains 105 % of its initial capacity after 9000 charge–discharge cycles, demonstrating exceptional cycling stability. This work provides a simple yet effective strategy for developing high-performance MXene-based supercapacitors through rational structural engineering. title: Recent advances in optoelectronic properties and applications of Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Stanly Zachariah, Ravanan Indirajith, M. Rajalakshmi
conclusion: 6  Summary and outlook  Ti 3 C 2 Tx MXene has garnered significant attention across various optoelectronic applications. This comprehensive review provides an in-depth overview of its synthesis, electrical and optical characteristics, and novel applications. Among MXenes, Ti 3 C 2 Tx stands out as the most extensively researched, commonly produced through the exfoliation process from the MAX phase. Solution-based synthesis enhances Ti 3 C 2 Tx MXene by introducing functional groups to its surface, allowing for versatile adjustments in chemical and physical properties. Its optical transparency, high conductivity, and chemical diversity make it an ideal candidate for thin-film optoelectronic devices. The main obstacles in the synthesis of hydrofluoric acid (also called HF) are related to environmental and health issues. When producing thin films in aqueous solutions, mxene experiences oxidation problems that are made worse by the temperature at which oxygen is present. More currently, efforts have been directed towards investigating less hazardous chemicals for synthesis and towards enhancing thermal and oxidative stability. Optoelectronic performance can be improved by adjusting the study's functions and plasmon surface energies thanks to the external functional groups on MXene. Ti 3 C 2 Tx MXene has electrochromic characteristics, meaning that when an electric field is applied, it will dynamically change colour.  Combining MXene with other materials addresses issues of low electrical conductivity and reversible ion intercalation in conventional electrochromic devices. The material's robust nonlinear optical response benefits diverse applications such as photothermal sun energy harvesting, therapy, and imaging. Ti 3 C 2 Tx MXene offers advantages like large-area, versatile, visible conductive electrodes in a range of optoelectronic devices that are suitable for it because of their excellent transmittance, inexpensive production costs, and ability to modify work performance. and Figure of Merit (FoMe). Experimental studies demonstrate MXene's adjustable characteristics and potential in transparent form as a photoactive substance solar cell, with improvements achievable through chemical processes, heterostructure design, and interface engineering. Ti 3 C 2 Tx MXene's hydrophilicity, biocompatibility, and high absorption rate make it promising for biomedical applications like drug administration, bioimaging, and photothermal therapy. In the near-infrared (NIR) region, Ti 3 C 2 MXene showcases the Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) effect, applicable in biological sensing, environmental pollution detection, and food safety. Despite its superior electrical, optical, and mechanical qualities, the configuration of MXene nanosheets in high-performance nanocomposites remains a challenge, limiting its practical applications. The oxidation-prone nature of MXene requires careful consideration in optoelectronics. While MXenes exhibit remarkably low photoluminescence (PL) response in aqueous solutions, metallic conductivity and hydrophilicity pose a limitation in optoelectronics. However, adjustments to work function and surface termination hold the potential to modify MXene's properties. This analysis strives to provide a comprehensive summary of the evolving optoelectronic uses of 2D Ti 3 C 2 Tx MXene, addressing current challenges and exploring potential opportunities.

title: 2D (Ti3C2Tx) MXene: A comprehensive review of advancements in synthesis protocols, applications in supercapacitors, sustainability targets and future prospects
authors: Suresh Jayakumar, P. Chinnappan Santhosh, S. Ramakrishna, A.V. Radhamani
conclusion: 12  Conclusion and future perspectives  MXene is an advanced 2D material and can compete in energy storage applications, making it superior to conventional 2D materials. Further, we summarize the valuable key points below.   12.1  MXenes in energy storage  MXenes have high conductivity, hydrophilicity, and structural diversity, making them a promising material for energy storage, especially in supercapacitors. Even though Ti 3 C 2 T x is a promising material, it also has some obstacles, like limited availability of precursors, high synthesis cost, etc., that are shown in Fig. 26  . However, the MXene Material industry globally is expected to grow significantly by 2029, with revenue projected to increase from $32.84 M in 2023 to $119.53 M with a CAGR of 24.03 %. Sales volumes are expected to surge from 415.57 Kg in 2023 to 1522.80 Kg by 2029, with a CAGR of 24.17 %, with robust expansion expected in the North American, European, and Asia-Pacific markets.    12.2  Research progress and synthesis methods  MXene has been pivotal in various applications, particularly as electrode materials for supercapacitors, with Ti 3 C 2 T x being extensively researched. The predominant method for synthesizing MXene remains top-down etching, primarily using HF or HCl/LiF. However, the use of fluoride etchants poses risks due to their hazardous nature. Different etching methods yield varying effects on MXene's capacitance performance. For instance, HF etching efficiently generates numerous layers, potentially enhancing capacitance through increased surface area and active ion adsorption sites, albeit with high hazards. The Acid-Fluoride Salt Etching method, involving LiF and HCl, produces MXene layers akin to HF etching but requires longer processing times. Resultant MXenes often exhibit improved capacitance and cyclic stability due to fewer defects and controlled surface terminations. The emerging Supercritical Etching technique offers high yields of MXene production and potential for large-scale manufacturing, although it may necessitate sophisticated equipment and precise conditions, such as high pressure. Molten Salt Etching, as a sustainable alternative, avoids hazardous chemicals and yields high-quality MXene with good electrochemical performance.    12.3  Addressing etching challenges and exploring eco-friendly solutions  MXene synthesis is a complex field that involves the use of fluoride etching. However, this method has many drawbacks that can compromise the electrochemical properties of MXene. Although fluoride etching is easy and cheap, it poses significant risks that call for safer and eco-friendly alternatives. Therefore, it is crucial to explore greener etching methods that do not rely on fluorine, such as molten salt etching. These sustainable alternatives have been able to significantly improve the properties of MXene without the need for delamination agents [ 151 ].    12.4  Comparing the performance of Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene composite  MXene is known for its high energy and power density, and it plays a crucial role in technological advancements. When combined with other materials, it improves the electrochemical capabilities of supercapacitor electrodes. The combination of bimetallic oxide or metal oxide with MXene is particularly notable for its outstanding electrochemical properties, thanks to its porous structure with a large surface area that facilitates rapid faradaic reactions. However, blending MXenes with hydrophobic polymers presents a research challenge. Finding an effective method to incorporate MXenes into these polymers could lead to innovative applications in the future.    12.5  Future perspectives     •  Exploration of New MAX Phases  The discovery of new MAX phases and corresponding 2D materials with improved stability and ease of preparation should be the focus of future research, leading to the development of novel energy storage materials with minimal economic cost.    •  Bottom-Up Synthesis Methods  MXene synthesis is currently dominated by top-down methods; however, in order to solve scalability and production issues, bottom-up methodologies must be investigated for easy and affordable MXene preparation.    •  Enhancing Environmental Stability  It is important to focus on making MXenes more environmentally stable than graphene to fully utilize their uses and reduce their adverse impacts on the environment.    •  Improving Electrochemical Stability  Addressing the limited electrochemical stability of MXenes requires further investigation into structural modifications and material engineering strategies to extend their cycle life and enhance performance in energy storage devices.    •  Cost-Effective Scale-Up  Overcoming the economic barriers associated with MXene-based energy storage materials is crucial for large-scale progress in the energy sector. Developing cost-effective and scalable synthesis routes will drive the widespread adoption of MXenes and catalyze advancements in energy storage technology.

conclusion: In this study, we successfully synthesized the two-dimensional nanomaterial Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene at low temperatures, resulting in reduced crystallite size of 3.8 nm and revealing its distinct surface chemistry and layered structure with interlayer spacing of 1.13 nm, as confirmed by different characterization techniques. Photoluminescence studies demonstrated a broad emission spectrum ranging from ultraviolet to visible light, with notable blue–green emission attributed to the active -O termination groups. The MXene nanosheets also significantly enhance luminescence properties by increasing the photoluminescence intensity with varying excitation wavelength and improving the spectral stability. Overall, this research highlights that Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene possesses enhanced photoluminescence with broad light emission characteristics influenced by -O termination groups and demonstrates that pH plays a crucial role in modulating its optical properties. title: Defect passivation and transformation of Ti3C2Tx MXene hollow microsphere for superior electrochemical performance and sodium-ions storage
authors: Ningning Liu, Xiaochen Zhang, Jinfeng Chen, Fei Yu, Jie Ma
conclusion: In summary, 3D porous Ti3 C2 Tx MXene hollow microsphere doped with N, S and V atoms (N, S, V-MHM) has been rationally designed and used as the cathode material for electrochemical Na+ capture in CDI. DFT calculation and characterizations revealed that N and S atom doping can replace the unstable end groups of Ti3 C2 Tx (−F and −OH) and cap the oxidizable edge, and the Ti vacancy defects can be passivated through V atom doping. The vacancy defect passivation and heteroatomic doping defect transformation leads to the regulation of electronic structure and generation of active sites in the lattice structure, improving of chemical stability and electrochemical capacity of N, S, V-MHM. The 3D hollow structure accelerates the charge/mass transfer and mitigates volume expansion during ion insertion/expulsion of MXene, which further modifies the intercalation pseudocapacitance kinetics and structure stability. The obtained N, S, V-MHM electrode displays high ions adsorption capacity (141.77 mg g−1 at 1.2 V for 60 min) and long-term cycling stability (≈94.6% capacitance retention after 215 salt adsorption/desorption cycles). The in situ EQCM-D test indicates that hydrated Na+ dominated counter-ion adsorption play a key role during the charge and discharge process. This study contributes to the development of electrochemically stable MXene-based electrode with balanced high-capacity performance by passivating defects and transforming strategy through heteroatom doping. title: Flexible electrode based on multi-scaled MXene (Ti3C2Tx) for supercapacitors
authors: Xuefeng Zhang, Yong Liu, Shangli Dong, Jianqun Yang, Xudong Liu
conclusion: In this contribution, we synthesized a flexible electrode based on multi-scaled Ti3 C2 Tx through vacuum filtration of the mixture of Ti3 C2 Tx nanoparticles prepared by HF etching and the Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets obtained by a HCl + LiF method. The Ti3 C2 Tx nanoparticles existing between Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets can play an effective role in preventing the self-restacking of nanosheets, providing more unimpeded channels for electrolyte ions access, and ensuring high-rate performance. On the other hand, the Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets act as conducting “bridges” and connect the Ti3 C2 Tx nanoparticles, facilitating electron transfer during the charge-discharge process. Although the specific capacitance of the prepared flexible electrode based on multi-scaled MXene is higher than that of the reported MXenes composites, and graphenes composites, but it is still slightly lower than that of the surface modified MXene films and N-doped MXene electrodes [6 ,34 ,35 ]. However, this work provides a new strategy for design and development of other MXenes-based materials with high specific capacitance performance for the flexible and highly integrated supercapacitors. title: Hydrothermal synthesis of MoS2/MXene composites for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Jung-Jie Huang, Yu-Wu Wang, Yu-Jie Lin, Yu-Xuan Zhang
conclusion: This study used an MXene framework to mitigate the restacking and agglomeration of MoS2 in the electrodes of capacitors. Through hydrothermal synthesis, MoS2 was grown on MXene base to create MoS2 /MXene heterostructure materials. Ultrasonic spray coating was employed to fabricate MoS2 /MXene electrodes, thereby ensuring the uniformity and quality of the materials. The structural advantages of MXene effectively prevented the restacking of MoS2 , which enabled the electrodes to maintain favorable dispersion and high overall capacitive performance. The electrochemical performance and stability of MoS2 /MXene were investigated under different (NH4 )6 Mo7 O24 ·4H2 O:C2 H5 NS concentration ratios. Among MoS2 /MXene electrodes prepared under different (NH4 )6 Mo7 O24 ·4H2 O:C2 H5 NS concentration ratios, the electrode prepared under a concentration ratio of 0.04:0.4 M exhibited the optimal electrochemical performance and stability. Therefore, the capacitive performance of MoS2 /MXene electrodes prepared under the aforementioned concentration ratio and subjected to different annealing temperatures was examined. Among the MoS2 /MXene electrodes annealed at various temperatures, that annealed at 850 °C had the optimal performance. At 850 °C, MoS2 transitioned from a 1 T/2H mixed phase to a more stable 2H phase; thus, the electrode annealed at this temperature exhibited higher crystallinity than did the electrodes annealed at different temperatures. Moreover, it exhibited the highest specific capacitance among the electrodes. The specific capacitance of the MoS2 /MXene electrode annealed at 850 °C (88.00 F/g) was approximately 1.46 times higher than that of an unannealed MoS2 /MXene electrode (60.41 F/g). Thus, the MoS2 /MXene electrode annealed at 850 °C had high charge storage capacity and excellent electrochemical performance. Furthermore, after 15000 charge–discharge cycles at a high current density of 20 A/g, the capacitance retention of the aforementioned electrode remained 100 %, which indicated its exceptional long-term cycling stability, durability, and reliability. In summary, the results of this study confirmed that thermally annealed MoS2 /MXene composites are promising high-performance electrode materials for supercapacitors. journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: the studied HSC device exhibits good flexible electrochemical performance, with minimal changes in specific capacitance at different bending angles, indicating high mechanical stability. This makes the device highly promising for potential integration into flexible energy storage solutions and wearable electronic applications. 4 Conclusion In this study, a dual innovation in the flexible energy storage field was achieved through the development of CoNi-OH/3D Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid electrodes and sulfonated lignin (SL)-based double crosslinked gel electrolytes, addressing a key challenge in supercapacitor performance and scalability. By using polystyrene (PS) nanospheres as templates, Ti3 C2 Tx was transformed from a two-dimensional lamellar structure into a hollow spherical three-dimensional network, leading to a several-fold increase in specific surface area, suppression of self-stacking, accelerated ionic diffusion, and enhanced electrochemical active sites. The specific capacitance of the CoNi-OH/3D Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid electrode reaches an astonishing 2020 ± 50 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 . The SL-doped PEDOT/SL/PAM/ KOH gel electrolyte exhibits high ionic conductivity (2.83 ± 0.2 S m−1 ), mechanical flexibility (elongation at break: 995 % ± 60 %), and uniform cross-linking. HSC devices assembled with these components demonstrate a favorable energy density (87 Wh kg−1 ) and power density (750 W kg−1 ) with excellent stability, 99.5 % ± 0.1 % coulombic efficiency and 83.7 % ± 0.2 % capacity retention after 7000 cycles at 3 A g−1 . The material also exhibits excellent flexibility and maintains stable electrochemical performance under various bending angles. The great potential of CoNi-OH/3D Ti3 C2 Tx electrodes and PEDOT/SL gel electrolytes for flexible energy storage applications provides valuable insights into the future development of this field. This study not only achieved a breakthrough in the performance of flexible supercapacitors, but also provided a biomass-derived electrolyte design strategy and MXene morphology engineering paradigm that can be generalized to other energy storage systems. title: High-performance Zn-ion hybrid supercapacitor based on 3D K+-intercalated Ti3C2TX hydrogel cathode
authors: Haiping Wang, Xingyu Wang, Xinmiao Liu, Shuwei Zhang, Shutong Meng, Wenjie Yan, Xin Zhang, Zhansheng Lu, Zenghui Qiu, Haijun Xu, Jiaqi He
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  K + intercalation of Ti 3 C 2 T X inhibits the self-stacking of MXene material due to interlayer van der Waals forces, thus enlarging the layer spacing and achieving fast zinc ion diffusion kinetics; and the reduction of the intercalated Ti 3 C 2 T X with GO by ascorbic acid generates a RGO hydrogel in a composite 3D system, which further contributes to the fast zinc ion diffusion kinetics. Furthermore, our research findings address the inherent limitations of MXene and offer valuable insights that could inspire novel avenues for exploring the energy storage applications of MXene.

title: Review: 2D MXenes based electrochemical sensors and supercapacitors for biomedical and energy storage applications
authors: Sourav Karmakar, Anuprava Mandal, Naresh Kumar Mani, Rinky Sha
conclusion: 6  Conclusion & future outlook  MXenes similar to graphene have recently attracted a significant attention among research communities because of their promising physico-chemical, and electronic characteristics, which position them as a possible substitute for graphene. With a focus on sensing performances, including sensitivity, LOD, selectivity, stability, linearity, dynamic range, and their viability in real samples, this review provides a comprehensive analysis of the various methods that MXenes are synthesized as well as the latest advancements in electrochemical biosensors that are designed to detect a variety of biomarkers. The impressive metallic conductivities, vast surface area, diverse composition, and remarkable hydrophilicity make these materials useful for developing electrochemical sensing devices. Consequently, there is a promising outlook for their use as sensitive electrochemical sensors in detecting a wide range of analytes. Although there has been notable advancement, the domain still faces numerous obstacles to overcome for the successful commercialization of MXene-based electrochemical biosensors, which can be outlined as follows:   (1)  Limited resistance to oxidation: the process of MXenes oxidizing in oxygen-rich solvents. (2) Scalability in synthesis presents challenges, particularly in achieving commercial-scale production. The environmental hazards associated with HF necessitate the exploration of alternative, milder etchants such as LiF/HCl. In recent years, less harmful and environmentally friendly etching techniques such as H 3 PO 4 , DES, and TBAOH have been introduced to alleviate the problem.    (3)  Irregular surface termination and absence of fluorine: it is essential to steer clear of random functionalization of the MXene surface by employing a different approach than the traditional HF-based etching method. Additionally, the presence of fluorine on the MXenes' surface hinders their use in biomedical applications and the immobilization of biomarkers.    (4)  Surface imperfections: the process of delaminating MXene through ultrasonication can lead to the formation of surface imperfections that may alter the distinctive physiochemical properties of MXenes. Moreover, addressing the technological hurdles is crucial for the successful advancement of electrochemical biosensors into commercial applications.     The upcoming sensors must prioritize the followings:   (1)  broadening of sensing devices to encompass a diverse array of biomarkers through simultaneous non-invasive immunoassays, enabling the monitoring of individuals' health at the molecular level.    (2)  the development of secure and dependable biosensing diagnostic platforms that leverage valuable insights from population studies and their correlation to blood-based clinical assays. This area is anticipated to evolve over time with significant advancements in production, processing, electrochemical conversion, and integration.     Further, this review highlights the various MXenes based electrodes, including pristine MXenes, doped MXene, MXenes/carbonaceous nanocomposites, MXenes/transition metal oxide composites, MXenes/transition metal-dichalcogenides composites for the application of supercapacitors. The heteroatom doped MXenes and various MXenes composites exhibit better electrochemical performance and much suitable for practical applications due to its high specific surface area, high ionic and electronic conductivity, modified electronic structure, rich of active sites, enhanced inter-planar spacing, better chemical stability, improved operating voltage window, and prevention of the restacking problems of MXene nanosheets. As a result, the modified electrodes offered high specific capacitance, excellent cycling stability, and excellent rate capability. Despite the fact, that MXene-based electrodes showed remarkable progress as an energy storage device for supercapacitor applications they also faced various challenges. Therefore, further research in the field of sustainable energy storage should be done to overcome those challenges. Hereby, some future recommendations for supercapacitor applications are shortlisted.   1.  To enhance the electrochemical performance of pristine-MXenes, the surface chemistry of MXenes should be modified using appropriate synthesis process.    2.  Researchers should focus on the novel composite based MXenes to increase the energy density with high power density and prevent the restacking problem of MXene nanosheets and the electrodes should be engineered with defects and heteroatom doping to enhance the electrochemical performances.    3.  To explore the various properties of MXenes researchers should focus on the combined experimental and theoretical studies.    4.  Exploration of non-Ti-based MXenes, double-M MXenes, and double-X MXenes for the application of supercapacitors are also highly demanded.    5.  For better cycling stability, the degradation of material properties at the time of cycling should be carefully observed by material characterization techniques like in-situ XRD and Raman studies and should find out the root cause of capacitance degradation. Therefore, we can get an idea about the changes of the material properties during cycling and it can be resolved by modifying the synthesis techniques and other modifications.    6.  MXenes show promising performance in aqueous electrolytes but the limited potential window for aqueous electrolyte limits the electrode to achieve high energy density and the leakage of aqueous electrolyte restrict the practical applications of the devices. Therefore, the use of non-aqueous electrolytes and solid electrolytes are preferable.     Overall, the rigorous research in this area will enable 2D MXenes to overcome these obstacles for the practical applications. Therefore, this review is anticipated to have a significant influence on the investigation and development of 2D MXenes-based electrochemical sensors for use in supercapacitors and biomedical applications.

title: MnOx/Ti3C2Tx MXene/Carbon Nanofibers composite fiber film electrode with good flexibility derived by combining electrospinning technique with carbonization treatment

Hence, the as-derived MMC/CNFs film electrode delivers an excellent specific capacitance of 211.57 F·g−1 at the scan rate of 2 mV·s−1 , cycling stability and mechanical property. This work provides a feasible approach for preparing MXene-based flexible fiber film electrode with good electrochemical performance. title: Supercapacitor featuring Ti3C2Tx MXene electrode: Nanoarchitectonics and electrochemical performances in aqueous and non-aqueous electrolytes
authors: Anu M A, Merin Tomy, Manimehala U, Xavier T S
conclusion: In this study, we effectively synthesised Ti3 C2 Tx MXene by the HCl+LiF etching method. The successful synthesis is confirmed by XRD, FESEM, FTIR, and XPS. The Brunauer-Emmett Teller (BET) method is used to analyse the synthesised material's surface area and pore size, which were found to be 42.53 m2 /g and 37.37 nm respectively. As a result, there are more active reaction sites and improved ion and electron transport, boosting electrochemical performance. A deeper comprehension of the electrode's electrochemical behaviour is provided by the Dunns technique, which aids to determine capacitive contributions to the overall charge storage. At a scan rate of 5 mV/s, the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrode shows a specific capacitance of 212 F/g in an aqueous H2 SO4 electrolyte and 299 F/g in an aqueous H3 PO4 electrolyte. The predominant charge storage method for Ti3 C2 Tx MXene is still cation intercalation without redox peaks. The specific capacitance of a symmetric device with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrodes in a 1 M H3 PO4 and H2 SO4 electrolyte is 151 F/g and 81 F/g, respectively, when operated at a current density of 0.8 A/g. A very reversible charge-discharge process and significant coulomb efficiency are indicated by nearly similar charge-discharge cycles. The SC prototype exhibits cyclic stability of 94% and 95% in H2 SO4 and H3 PO4 aqueous electrolyte respectively showing the exceptional stability of the electrodes and electrolyte. Its ability to maintain mass-specific capacitance over time signifies its maturity and effectiveness, facilitating its widespread adoption and accelerating the transition towards a sustainable energy future. The specific capacitance of a symmetric device with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrodes was measured as 203 F/g in a 1 M H₃PO₄ gel electrolyte and 141 F/g in a 1 M H₂SO₄ gel electrolyte, both at a current density of 1 A/g. The power density and energy density of a SC device using H3 PO4 gel electrolyte are 800 W/Kg and 72 Wh/kg, respectively. Therefore, symmetric SC devices with gel electrolytes have the potential to provide a large operational voltage window offering affordable solutions for dealing with upcoming energy challenges. title: MXene/carboxymethylcellulose-polyaniline (Ti3C2Tx/CMC-PANI) film as flexible electrode for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Hanping Xu, Linlin Cui, Zijie Lei, Mincai Xu, Xiaojuan Jin
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, an ultrathin, porous and flexible Ti 3 C 2 T x /CMC-PANI film was successfully synthesized via a facile vacuum filtration process. Particularly, the introduction of CMC-PANI as the intercalator into the Ti 3 C 2 T x interlayer for conditioning Ti 3 C 2 T x flakes effectively alleviated the self-restacking problem of Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets, thus facilitating the diffusion and transport of ions. Moreover, the interwoven CMC-PANI connects horizontally adjacent Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets to establish interconnected electrical conductivity and ion channels, making the TCP film internal structure more uniformly and orderly, thereby achieving a high mechanical strength (≈ 35.6 MPa). The TCP-0.75 film electrode has a mass loading of about 5 mg cm −2 and can be used directly as an electrode for supercapacitors without any additives. Consequently, the TCP-0.75 film exhibits the largest area specific capacitance of 1161.4 mF cm −2 (812.9 mC cm −2 ) at 1 mA cm −2 , and a superior rate performance (maintains 58.4% of the initial value at 50 mA cm −2 ). Moreover, the fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device presents a high area energy density of 158.7 µW h cm −2 at a power density of 700.1 µW cm −2 , and good cycles stability (retention of 89.6% after 15,000 charging/discharging cycles). This rational design that balances flexibility and electrochemical performance provides a novel insight to address the inherent defects of MXene and further develop high-performance energy storage devices.

title: Mg2+ induced Ti3C2Tx MXene@microfibrillated cellulose into composite aerogels in a framework of melamine sponge for high-rate performance supercapacitors
authors: Debin Cai, Shuai Wu, Li Guo, Yanzhong Wang
conclusion: In summary, a series of three-dimensional porous Mg-MFMX@MS composite aerogels were successfully prepared via the induced gelation of MXene@MFC in the framework of melamine sponge with Mg2+ as a cross-linking agent and microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) as an additive to regulate their structures. Three-dimensional porous MS is an ideal support to enhance the mechanical strength of Mg-MFMX@MS aerogels. The inserted Mg2+ not only induces the formation of MXene/MFC composite hydrogels, but also improves the interlayer spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets. As an additive, MFC can combine with Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets to form hydrogen bonds, which can impede the restacking of MXene nanosheets and improve the mechanical stability of composite aerogels. The experimental results show that the Mg-MFMX composite aerogels are uniformly distributed in the framework of MS with high porosity and mass loading. At a scan rate of 10 mV s−1 , the prepared Mg-10%MFMX@MS aerogel showed the largest area capacitance of 685.77 m F cm−2 . Thanks to its three-dimensional structure, the areal capacitance is still 497.41 mF cm−2 at a high scan rate of 1000 mV s−1 , and the capacitance retention rate is 72.5 %, which is better than the previously reported MXene-based aerogels [19 ,42 ,45 ,63–65 ]. Furthermore, the energy density of the asymmetric supercapacitor assembled with activated carbon reaches up to 101.15 μWh cm−2 at a power density of 17,000 μW cm−2 , and the capacitance retention is up to 115 % after 10,000 cycles, indicating the superior stability. This article provides a simple approach for preparing MXene-based aerogels with 3D porous interconnected structure and high mechanical strength for high-rate performance supercapacitors. title: Construction of high-performance solid-state asymmetric supercapacitor based on Ti3C2Tx MXene/CuS positive electrode and Fe2O3@rGO negative electrode
authors: Xiaobo Chen, Huiran Ge, Wen Yang, Jianli Liu, Peizhi Yang
conclusion: In summary, we have successfully fabricated asymmetrical supercapacitor devices composed of few-layered Ti3 C2 Tx MXene wrapped CuS nanosparticles as the positive electrode and Fe2 O3 @rGO electrode as the negative electrode by a cost-effective method. For as-synthesized MXene/CuS nanohybrids, the high conductivity few-layered Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheets can construct a successive conductive network, while the CuS nanosparticles have abundant redox-active sites, ensuring the superb electrochemical performance of electrodes. As a result, an optimized MXene/CuS electrode exhibits a remarkable capacity/capacitance of 1541.6C g−1 (2569.3 F g−1 ) at 1 A g−1 with prominent stability (93.5 %) over 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . To improve the energy density of the asymmetrical supercapacitor, Fe2 O3 @rGO based negative electrode with excellent performance was fabricated. The Fe2 O3 @rGO negative electrode exhibits an excellent specific capacity of 255.6C g−1 at 1 A g−1 and long operational life retaining 92.8 % of the initial capacity after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . Further, the assembled solid-state supercapacitor of MXene/CuS//Fe2 O3 @rGO yielded an operating voltage window of 1.7 V, a specific capacity of 313.7C g−1 (184.5 F g−1 ) at 1 A g−1 , an extraordinary energy density of 74.1 Wh kg−1 at the power density of 849.8 W kg−1 , and stable cyclic life (91.3 % capacity retention) up to 10,000 cycles at 8 A g−1 . The demonstration of results not only demonstrate MXene/CuS and Fe2 O3 @rGO composites have great potential for electrodes in asymmetric supercapacitor but provides a novel perspective for rational design for 2D material-based composite for asymmetric supercapacitor applications. title: Protective hydrothermal treatment to improve ion pathway in Ti3C2Tx MXene for high-performance flexible supercapacitors
authors: M. Lai, K. Chen, D. Wang, P. Cai, L. Sun, K. Zhang, B. Li, C. Yuan, Y. Zou, Z. Wang, H. Peng
conclusion: In conclusion, the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx dispersion is treated by protective hydrothermal method to effectively improve ion pathway in Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. The protective hydrothermal treatment is simply conducted in the hydrothermal kettle (filled with N2 atmosphere) placed in vacuum oven. The optimal Ti3 C2 Tx is achieved by the hydrothermal treatment at 150 °C for 12h and thus recorded as h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h. The hydrothermal treatment contributes to the larger lattice spacing and decreased flake size for the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h nanosheets, and thus enables the significantly increased interlayer spacing and pores with obviously larger specific surface area for the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film, which can effectively improve ion transport pathways and enhance ions accessibility with more pseudocapacitive active sites. According to DFT calculations, a small number of oxides (TiO2 nanoparticles) produced during the hydrothermal treatment also facilitate to increase the capacitive performance of h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h. Therefore, the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode offers significantly increased capacitance and rate performance. Compared with the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode (324.7 F g−1 /581 F cm−3 at 1 A g−1 ), the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode shows significantly higher capacitance (498 F g−1 /1911 F cm−3 at 1 A g−1 ) with excellent rate performance (63 % retention from 1 to 20 A g−1 ) and cycling stability (98.2 % retention after 20 000 cycles), which are among the best electrochemical performances of undoped Ti3 C2 Tx based film electrodes reported so far. An ultra-high capacitance of 3.23 F cm−2 at 1 A g−1 is achieved for thick h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode of 33.1 μm thickness. The flexible supercapacitor device with symmetric h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrodes and PVA-H2 SO4 gel electrolyte enables excellent energy storage performance (117 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and 23.4 Wh kg−1 at 299.8 W kg−1 ) with high cycling stability (84 % retention after 3000 cycles) and bending stability, outperforming most of previously reported Ti3 C2 Tx -based flexible supercapacitor devices. The impressive results indicate that the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode possesses great application potential in flexible energy storage devices and the simply protective hydrothermal treatment could be also applicable to other MXenes. title: Ti3AlC2 MAX phase and Ti3C2TX MXene-based composites towards supercapacitor applications: A comprehensive review of synthesis, recent progress, and challenges
authors: Onkar Jaywant Kewate, Sathyanarayanan Punniyakoti
conclusion: 7  Conclusion  Due to the exhaustion of energy sources like fossil fuels and growing energy needs, it is essential to find an alternative energy source. Recent decades have seen a surge in attention for supercapacitors owing to their distinctive properties like good power density, quick charging/discharging time, and longer cycle life. From the last decade, MXenes are emerging as a two-dimensional material in academic and industrial sectors for next-generation applications, especially for energy storage. Among from different types of MXenes, Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes are widely attracted towards the supercapacitor due to their noteworthy benefits such as excellent conductivity, rapid surface terminations, hydrophilicity, unique surface chemistry, thermal conductivity, and structural diversity. The study of Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes as an electrode for supercapacitors has witnessed significant growth within the last decade.  This review focuses on the latest research developments pertaining to MXenes and supercapacitors. In the recent period, various types of MXenes and their composites are synthesized and studied. Among the different MXenes. Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene is widely studied and still research is going on. In the current review, various synthesis methods for the MAX phase are well discussed. Among all approaches, the high-temperature method is the most efficient and widely used technique for making MAX phases. For preparing MXenes, the etching methods widely used are HF acid etching, fluoride-based etching, and f-free etching methods. Normally, fluoride-based compounds were used as an etchant. Till now HF etching and LiF-HCl etching approaches are used widely. Here, it is essential to keep in mind that the etching conditions would result in MXenes with a variety of distinctive morphologies and tunability surfaces. As a result, it is critical to choose a suitable approach for the objectives of the research. Delamination and intercalation using various acid-salt combinations as etchants are well described. When different acid-salt combinations were intercalated, it is observed that the c-LP considerably increased and changed depending on the functional groups. The interlayer distance of sheets is important along with this it improves the performance of supercapacitors by applying intercalation.  Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene is largely researched for supercapacitor electrodes due to its distinctive surface chemistry, significant surface area, electrical conductivity, and Young's modulus. It was found that the combination of these other materials, such as carbon/polymer/transition metal oxide materials, with Pure Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes for supercapacitor electrode material, improved the overall mechanical strength and enhanced electrochemical performance. Activated carbon, CNTs, and 2D graphene have all been studied with Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene as an interlayer spacer in recent research to reduce restacking. Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene has strong pseudocapacitance, significant electrical conductivity, and extended cycle life as a result of the presence of transition metal oxides. However, the mechanical property possessed by Ti 3 C 2 T X /transition metal oxide composites are often observed to be low. The low temperature and environmentally friendly fabrication of the MAX phase is still found to be difficult. The less harmful and effective etching method to prepare Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene with improved oxidation stability and less restacking of MXenes sheets is a challenging task. Above mentioned factors which will directly affects the power density, energy density, and cycling stability of supercapacitor performance with notable advancements in supercapacitor electrodes in recent years, Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene shows exceptional promise for energy storage applications.  Thus, the current review gives an understanding of various synthesis of Ti 3 AlC 2 MAX phase and Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes, there their electrochemical behaviour with other composites which will throw some light on the field of MXenes-based supercapacitors.

title: Synergistic Ti3C2Tx MXene quantum dot/nanosheet Hybrid: Elevating supercapacitor performance
authors: Bheem Kumar, Avinash Rundla,  Priyanka, Mahaveer Singh, Divya Rani, Pushpendra Kumar, Kedar Singh
conclusion: This study demonstrates the successful synthesis and characterization of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx , Water@Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol@Ti3 C2 Tx , highlighting their synergistic improvements in electrochemical performance. Ti3 C2 Tx was synthesized via the etching of MAX-phase precursors in an acidic solution to remove the Al layer, forming a combination of nanosheets and MQDs that enhance the surface area for charge and ion transport. The materials were characterized via XRD for their crystal structure, FTIR for their functional groups, TEM for their morphological analysis, and UV–vis and PL spectroscopy for their optical properties. Electrochemical studies were performed in a three-electrode system with 1 M H2 SO4 as the electrolyte, with the materials coated on nickel foil used as working electrodes. CV, GCD, and EIS analyses demonstrated significant enhancements in the specific capacitance and charge transfer properties of Water@Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol@Ti3 C2 Tx compared with those of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . Both materials exhibited higher specific capacitances across varying current densities (1–5 Ag-1 ) and scan rates (10-200 mVs−1 ). The EIS results further revealed a reduced Rct and Rs in Water@Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol@Ti3 C2 Tx , indicating superior electrochemical kinetics. These findings underscore the potential of functionalized Ti3 C2 Tx materials for advanced energy storage applications. title: Hierarchical MOF-derived Selenide/Ti3C2Tx hybrids for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Yuhan Cui, Jing Sun, Yining Wang, Lijie Zhao, Jiawei Wang, Yunpeng Wu, Wenxi Zhang, Zengyuan Fan, Yuzhe Tang, Yue Song, Zhongmin Su
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this study, 2D/2D composites were fabricated utilizing 2D MXene as the substrate and 2D MOF as a precursor. Subsequently, MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se-5 wavy bimetallic selenide materials were synthesized through a hydrothermal selenization method employing MOF as a sacrificial template. The macroporous structure of 2D-MXene in combination with the wave-like microstructure of Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se constitutes a multi-layered architecture with enhanced conductivity and accelerated electron transfer rate. At the same time, MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se composites as electrode materials have high specific surface area and synergistic effect on binary metal selenides, significantly improving supercapacitors’ storage performance. Therefore, the specific capacitance of the MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se electrode can reach 1126 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 current density, and the capacitance retention can reach 70.98 % after 10,000 charge-discharge cycles at 10 A g −1 . After assembling the asymmetric supercapacitor (BC//MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se-5), when the power density is 750 W kg −1 , the energy density of 46.18 Wh kg −1 can be provided, and the specific capacitance of the device after 10,000 charge and discharge cycles is 79.06 % of the initial value. The excellent long-cycle stability indicates that the device has a practical application prospect. In conclusion, our work not only provides an efficient approach to enhance the specific capacitance performance of selenide supercapacitor electrode materials but also reveals the significance of topography engineering optimization and furnishes valuable perspectives for the rational design of more two-dimensional structures with excellent electrochemical properties for energy storage configuration.

title: Synergistic in-situ intercalation and surface modification strategy for Ti3C2Tx MXene-based supercapacitors with enhanced electrochemical energy storage
authors: Zhiyu Li, Mingyue Jiang, Fangfei Wu, Lili Wu, Xitian Zhang, Lu Li
conclusion: In summary, a synergistic in-situ intercalation and surface modification strategy for enhancing the electrochemical performance of Ti3 C2 Tx is demonstrated. Ag nanoparticles were intercalated into the interlayers of Ti3 C2 Tx using an in-situ reduction method to open ion diffusion channels and expose active sites, followed by annealing treatment to remove the deleterious termination. Benefitting from the structural modification, the obtained a-Ag/Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode possess an enhanced specific capacitance of 471 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 with a 2-fold increase in intercalation pseudocapacitance compared to the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . The enlarged interlayer space was able to transport ions rapidly and stably through the support of Ag NPs, giving the a-Ag/Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode process an exceptional rate performance of 88.3 % capacitance retention as the current density increase to 15 A g−1 and a stability of 100 % capacitance retention after 20,000 cycles. In addition, the asymmetric supercapacitor with a negative electrode of a-Ag/Ti3 C2 Tx and a positive electrode of RuO2 @CC delivers a high energy density of 24.6 Wh kg−1 . The present study demonstrates an effective strategy to improve the electrochemical energy storage of the Ti3 C2 Tx negative electrode by designing the intercalation and termination. title: Tag paper substrate enhanced self-assembled graphene oxide-Ti3C2Tx MXene composites for supercapacitors applications via laser processing
authors: Xiu-Yan Fu, Hua-Rui Li, Ruo-Yu Shu, Hao-Bo Jiang, Meng-Nan Yao, Jia-Nan Ma
conclusion: In conclusion, we proposed a new strategy to fabricate LIRGO-based supercapacitors, in which self-assembled GO-M composites and paper substrates collaborate. On the one hand, the self-assembled GO-M not only hinders the restacking of GO sheets to some degree but also renders the LIRGO high conductivity after the DLW of GO. Conversely, the numerous cellulose network structures offered by the paper substrates enabled LIRGO to exhibit better capacity and flexibility. Therefore, R-GO-M-P-based supercapacitors show good electrochemical performance, including a significantly higher specific capacitance value of 15.5 mF/cm2 compared to that of RGO-G (4.05 mF/cm2 ) and a good stability of 93.35 % retention of specific capacitance after 1000 cycles of charge-discharge tests. Moreover, R-GO-M-P-based supercapacitors also exhibited excellent flexibility, where after 1000 cycles of bending tests, the specific capacitance retention was as high as 142 %. Notably, in-series R-GO-M-P supercapacitors can be obtained using a programmable DLW process, that extends the working potential extension for powering an LED. We believe that this study will enhance the applications of LIRGO-based supercapacitors in future electronics. title: Probing the synergistic effect of MXene (Ti3C2Tx) and MWCNTs on NiWO4 for superior water-splitting and supercapacitor studies
authors: Amna Irshad, Mirza Mahmood Baig, Seung Goo Lee, Imran Shakir, Zeid A. ALOthman, Muhammad Farooq Warsi, Muhammad Shahid
conclusion: A simple approach is used to fabricate NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs. The fabricated samples are analyzed via different physio-chemical characterizations. The prepared materials are used to study water splitting and supercapacitors. The cyclic voltammetry experiment in non-Faradaic regions finds the electrochemical active surface area. NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs exhibits more ECSA (216 cm2 ) as compared to NiWO4 and NiWO4 /MXene. Tafel slope is explored to evaluate the kinetics of the catalyst for HER and OER performance. NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs shows Tafel slope of 77 and 91 mV/dec for HER and OER, respectively. The CNTs-based composite shows good response for oxidation and reduction reactions during cyclic voltammetric measurements. The prepared samples show pseudocapacitive behaviour during the electrochemical study. NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs composite exhibits more discharge time of 500 s compared to NiWO4 (276 s) and NiWO4 /MXene (390 s). NiWO4 , NiWO4 /MXene, and NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs show specific capacitance of 690, 975, and 1250F/g, respectively. The efficient performance of NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs for both water splitting and supercapacitor study is attributed to the increased surface area, more exposed active sites, and less charge transfer resistance. These attributes make it an excellent candidate for advanced electrochemical study. CRediT authorship contribution statement Amna Irshad: Writing – original draft, Methodology. title: Human-friendly flexible solid-state biodegradable supercapacitor based on Ti3C2Tx MXene film without adhesive structure
authors: Xiaofeng Zhang, Muhammad Sufyan Javed, Hongjia Ren, Xinze Zhang, Salamat Ali, Kaiming Han, Awais Ahmad, Ammar M. Tighezza, Weihua Han, Kui-Qing Peng
conclusion: In this study, Ti3 C2 Tx films were prepared by vacuum filtration, which showed superior electrochemical performance in FSBSCs. The adhesive-free structure of Ti3 C2 Tx film reduces the internal resistance of the electrode material and promotes the transport of electrons. In addition, the larger crystal plane spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx film provides more active sites for electrolyte ions, improving electrochemical performance. The Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode shows a remarkable electrochemical performance, including a peak capacitance of 768 F/g at 1 A/g, impressive rate capability (65.1% at 20 A/g), and notable capacitance retention (98.9%) after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles at 10 A/g. The assembled Ti3 C2 Tx //NaCl-PVA//Ti3 C2 Tx -FSBSC exhibited a high capacitance of 112 F/g at 1 A/g and a high energy density of 62.3 Wh/kg at 1,000.8 W/kg, coupled with exceptional cycle stability, retaining 98.9% after 5,000 cycles. We carried out biodegradation experiments, Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode and assembled solid-state biodegradable supercapacitor (SBSC) devices showed good degradability in a H2 O2 solution and could be completely degraded within 30 h. In addition, the DFT calculations proved the excellent performance of the Ti3 C2 Tx electrode material through excellent electronic properties, higher E ads, and lower diffusion energy barrier of the Na+ ions. This work provides a new direction for the development of safer and more effective implantable biodegradable bioenergy storage devices. title: Sandwich-like high-performance Ti3C2Tx MXene/NiCo2O4 nanosphere composites for asymmetric supercapacitor application
authors: Wei Wang, Guohui Chen, Weiqi Kong, Junshu Chen, Linyu Pu, Jiaxu Gong, Huan Zhang, Yatang Dai
conclusion: In general, Ti3 C2 Tx MXene/NiCo2 O4 composites were prepared by electrostatic self-assembly of modified NiCo2 O4 nanoparticles. The Ti3 C2 Tx MXene/NiCo2 O4 composites showed excellent electrochemical properties, and their capacities were much higher than that of the NiCo2 O4 microspheres. Moreover, the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene/NiCo2 O4 (M2-N1) composite showed excellent rate performance (10 A g−1 and 81 % initial capacity) and cycling stability (82.2 % after 5000 cycles). In addition, an asymmetric M2-N1 supercapacitor showed excellent electrochemical performance and cycling stability (88.2 % capacity retention after 5000 cycles) and a high energy density of 36.67 Wh kg−1 at a 800 W kg−1 power density. This work provides a strategy for the preparation of composite materials with high stabilities and high energy densities, and it has good application prospects. title: Ammonia-assisted heterocyclic amine exerts soft delamination and interlayer engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene for fabricating stable supercapacitors
authors: Arumugam Sangili, Binesh Unnikrishnan, Shun Ruei Hu, Han-Wei Chu, Hung-Lung Chou, Ren-Siang Wu, Chih-Ching Huang, Huan-Tsung Chang
conclusion: Highly stable Ti3 C2 Tx modified with heterocyclic aromatic amines were prepared from the multilayer-MXene without sonication. Our study provides a significant understanding of 5-Az for assisting the soft delamination, enhancing the chemical stability of Ti3 C2 Tx against air oxidation, and enhancing its electrochemical activities by increasing the active sites and interlayer spacing of adjacent Ti3 C2 Tx sheets. The 5-Az-protected Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited high oxidation resistance in aqueous medium and was stable for up to 500 days. 5-Az acted as the active species for intercalation and assisted in the soft delamination of the m -Ti3 C2 Tx layers into single-layer Ti3 C2 Tx . Based on our experimental and computational explorations, we concluded that the NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited excellent chemical oxidation stability over 150 days at room temperature, over 24 days at 70 °C, and over 24 h in 10 mM H2 O2 solution due to surface passivation by 5-Az via covalent and hydrogen bonding with the surface Ti-atoms. NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx enables an increased electrolyte-accessible area, enhanced charge-transport properties, and improved charge storage and discharge performance. In a three-electrode system, the NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited a specific capacitance of 631 F g−1 at a current density of 2 A g–1 and capacitance retention of 90 % even after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . Our NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx SSC displays energy and power densities of 59.1 Wh kg–1 and 1440 W kg–1 , respectively, showing their great potential in various energy applications. title: Hybrid nano-architectural engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructures for supercapacitor applications: A review
authors: Mojtaba Rostami, Parisa Rezvaninia, Ahmad Amiri, Ghodsi Mohammadi Ziarani, Mohammad Reza Ganjali, Alireza Badiei
conclusion: 3  Conclusions and future outlook  Despite the challenges in the architectural engineering of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene, these materials remain a promising candidate for SC devices. By addressing these challenges and working towards future goals, we can develop more efficient and effective Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based SC devices to alleviate the current energy crisis and shortcomings of existing energy storage devices. SCs, in particular, are crucial for meeting high-energy peak power demands over short periods in certain areas. They possess desirable properties such as long cycling stability, good safety and high power density. The electrical double-layer method, however, places a cap on the capacitance of conventional SCs that use Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based nanomaterials. As a result, researchers have turned to pseudo capacitive materials, like transition metal phosphides/oxides/sulfides/hydroxides, layered double hydroxides/oxide/phosphides/sulfides, MOFs, MOF-derived hybrid NAs, COFs and Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene, for the creation of SCs with excellent performance and secondary rechargeable batteries. This field has received significant attention in the past several years.  To enhance the effectiveness of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based SC devices and mitigate restacking resulting from excessive functional groups, we propose the utilization of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based hybrid NAs with materials such as COFs, LDH, TMC, MOFs, and MOF derivatives. Furthermore, we will delve into their capacitive performance. It is a potential strategy to improve the active sites and encourage rapid ion diffusion speeds in MOFs to use pseudocapacitive redox centers. However, MOFs' weak conductivity, which is insufficient for several fields, prevents their practical implementation. To address this challenge, a viable solution involves creating an aerogel structure with hierarchical porosity by growing MOFs within a two- and 3D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene framework that exhibits high conductivity (MOFs@Ti 3 C 2 T  x  aerogel). This hybrid material combines the advantageous functional properties of both MOFs and Ti 3 C 2 T  x  , providing high surface areas and is expected to demonstrate brilliant electrochemical energy storage behavior.  The bimetallic sulfide LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T  x  nanocomposite, with its unique 2D hierarchical structure and large S BET , can potentially expand the electrochemical performance of SCs. This is because it can make the entire electrode material more electronically conductive and structurally stable, which speeds up electron transport and reduces the length of ion diffusion routes during charge/discharge operations. Furthermore, because of their in-plane charge delocalization, extensive π-conjugation, broad ion-accessible surface, and adequate redox active sites, which help to boost Pseudocapacitance, 2D MOFs are interesting electrode materials. It is indeed evident that Ti 3 C 2 T  x  has the potential to become a superior electrode material for energy storage devices. However, there are still numerous areas that need to be explored to fully realize its potential. Some primary future goals highlighted via recent studies include: (i) Developing new synthesis methods to improve the scalability and cost-effectiveness of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene production. (ii) Increasing the electrical conductivity of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene via techniques like doping or surface alterations. (iii) To improve the electrochemical activity of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene, novel nanocomposite materials based on MXene are being investigated. (iv) Investigating the long-term stability and reliability of energy storage technologies based on Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene. (v) Constructing useable Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based energy storage (SCs) technology, Examples include in electric vehicles or renewable energy systems. (vi) Conducting advanced scientific research to better understand tunability, the surface chemistry and interlayer structure of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene for optimal device fabrication. (vii) Developing extra heterostructure and hybrid materials NAs based on other MXene family members, particularly non-Ti-based MXene, to enhance performance and improve the applications available. (viii) Fabrication of transparent, flexible and miniaturized Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene based SCs could greatly expand their practical applications. (ix)The generation of magnetic Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes and the creation of conductivity in Ti 3 C 2 T  x  could also create a new possibilities for energy storage and other applications. (x) Standardization and cost reduction of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based electrodes for device manufacturing would make them more accessible to a wider range of users. Finally, the presence of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based electrodes in the international energy market would guarantee that their potential advantages are felt globally. Addressing these goals will require continued research and innovation within the domain of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based SCs. Nevertheless, Ti 3 C 2 T  x  will undoubtedly remain to have a significant role in the advancement of storing energy technology with extremely effective performance given the encouraging outcomes so far.  The quest for cost-effective, versatile, and durable energy storage solutions has been a driving force behind advancements in electronics and related fields amidst the current era of industrialization. Among the myriad options 2D stratified nanomaterials have emerged as promising contenders for high-efficiency energy storage devices, owing to their Chemical, structural, and physical properties. Notably, 2D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes, a class of transition metal carbides/nitrides characterized by thin thickness, tunable electrochemical properties, high conductivity, and abundant active edge sites, have garnered significant attention in material science circles.  In the realm of electrochemical energy storage technologies, particularly SCs, Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes stand out as excellent electrode materials. However, the practical utilization of MXenes has encountered challenges stemming from issues such as aggregation, oxidation, and restacking within their layers. To surmount these hurdles, this study investigates various categories of 2D nanomaterials exhibiting noteworthy electrochemical activity. These encompass COFs, TMCs, LDHs, MOFs, and MOF derivatives, which hold promise for synergistic integration with Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes. Nanoarchitectural engineering techniques are employed to enhance the performance of these 2D nanomaterials, both individually and in composite configurations with the metallic conductive 2D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes, within SCs.  Core Findings: (I) The investigation highlights the potential of diverse 2D nanomaterials and their composite nanoarchitectures (NAs) for improving the performance of supercapacitors. (ii) Notable electrochemical activity is observed in various 2D nanomaterials, including COFs, TMCs, LDHs, and MOFs, suggesting their suitability for energy storage applications. (iii) Integration of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes with these 2D nanomaterials enhances the electrochemical performance of supercapacitors, indicating the feasibility of composite approaches for energy storage device optimization.  Problems Addressed: (I) Challenges associated with MXenes, such as aggregation, oxidation, and restacking, are acknowledged and addressed through the exploration of alternative 2D nanomaterials and composite strategies. (ii) By diversifying the range of materials considered for energy storage applications, the study seeks to mitigate the limitations imposed by MXene-related issues.  Results Achieved: (i) The investigation demonstrates the feasibility of enhancing supercapacitor performance through the strategic integration of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes with various 2D nanomaterials. (ii) Improved electrochemical activity and stability are observed in composite nanoarchitectures, indicating the potential for overcoming MXene-related challenges and advancing energy storage technologies.  Limitations of the Advantages Studies: (I) While the study explores the potential of diverse 2D nanomaterials and composite approaches, it may not comprehensively address all possible challenges or solutions in the field of energy storage. (ii) Practical implementation and scalability of the proposed nanoarchitectures may require further investigation and validation.  In conclusion, this review contributes to the ongoing efforts to develop high-performance energy storage solutions tailored to the demands of the contemporary industrial revolution. By examining a range of 2D nanomaterials and their composite configurations, the study offers insights into promising avenues for advancing supercapacitor technology.

title: Enhanced performance of Fe2O3/MXene based supercapacitors with redox-electrolyte strategy
authors: Jing Xu, Xinye Xu, Xiaoqing Bin, Yingyi Liao, Xuedong He, Wenxiu Que
conclusion: We propose a dual-optimization strategy: (1) the Fe2 O3 /MXene composite electrodes were fabricated via filtration process and annealing treatment, where Fe2 O3 nanoparticles are uniformly anchored on MXene nanosheets to both mitigate re-stacking of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene and provide additional redox-active sites; (2) A hybrid redox electrolyte (3 M H₂SO₄ + 30 mM CuSO4 ) was introduced to synergistically enhance charge storage via Cu2+ /Cu+ redox reactions. Thus, the optimized Fe2 O3 /MXene-5 composite electrode achieves a specific capacitance of 643.8 F g−1 at 2 A g−1 , which is attributed to reconstructed interfacial charge distribution that facilitates rapid ion adsorption and electron transfer. title: Boosting electrochemical activity via manipulating the d-band center of CoNi2Se4/MXene heterostructure for supercapacitor application
authors: Minmin Hu, Lihong Chen, Yu Wang, Jun Dai, Yifan Bi, Yuanming Li, Jian Zhao, Guicun Li, Lei Wang, Alan Meng, Zhenjiang Li
conclusion: 3  Conclusions  In summary, we have successfully fabricated a P-doped CoNi 2 Se 4 /Ti 3 C 2 T x heterostructure with abundant Se vacancies as battery-type cathode for supercapacitor application through a one-step hydrothermal method followed by the phosphating treatment. The homogeneous dispersion of CoNi 2 Se 4 on MXene effectively mitigates the issue of nanosheet aggregation, thereby diminishing the ion diffusion barrier to the redox reaction sites. The incorporation of P leads to a decrease in the valence state of the metallic Ni/Co and the inoization energy of P is higher than that of Se, resulting in an upshift of the d-band center of Ni/Co. Consequently, the occupancy of the antibonding state decreases when the metal active sites react with the electrolyte ion OH − , fostering accelerated electron mobility and enhanced Ni/Co 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization. Additionally, the reduction in the valence state of Ni/Co facilitates the formation of Se vacancies, generating numerous exposed unsaturated dangling bonds carrying positive charges, which serve as robust adsorption sites for foreign anions OH − and facilitate the ion diffusion. Collectively, these advancements culminate in a higher capacitance of 1520 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 , with a mere 20% capacitance decay after 5000 cycles. Furthermore, by pairing this cathode with an AC anode, an HSC achieves a desirable energy density of 37.4 Wh kg −1 at the power density of 0.8 kW kg −1 . This work provides an effective method to heighten the electrochemical performance of transition metal compounds via the synergy of favorable architectures and electronic effect.

title: Facile synthesis of MnO2@Ti3C2Tx composite electrodes for superior performance supercapacitor
authors: Yinghao Lv, Jiaqi He, Yajie Yang, Meilin Huang, Dawei He, Yongsheng Wang
conclusion: Overall, the composite material of 1, 3, 6, and 9-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx is effectively deposited onto the current collector (Ni foam) surface via a facile solution immersion method, culminating in the successful fabrication of the MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx electrodes. Varying the immersion cycles influences the deposition state of MnO2 , which significantly affects the electrochemical performance. Notably, the nanoflower-shaped 6-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx demonstrates the highest electrochemical activity. This self-assembly synthesis approach eliminates the need for binders and conductive agents, allowing for precise characterization of the electrochemical behavior of the Ti3 C2 Tx and MnO2 composite. Importantly, 6-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx exhibits a C s of 324.1 F g−1 , representing a 407.2 % improvement over 6-MnO2 in the identical three-electrode configuration with 0.5 M Na2 SO4 . This enhancement is attributed to Ti3 C2 Tx , which not only functions as a nucleation substrate for the deposition of MnO2 but also enhances the electrical conductivity of the composite material. Furthermore, the asymmetric supercapacitor, which combines 6-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx and Ti3 C2 Tx , has an energy density of 30.8 W h kg−1 . This facile synthesis method for the large-scale self-assembly of MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx composite electrodes holds great promise for practical applications in the energy storage field. Furthermore, our study focused on a single synthesis condition, namely the number of impregnation cycles in the solution-immersion technique, and we investigated the electrochemical behavior of this self-assembled electrode in a low-concentration neutral electrolyte. It is anticipated that, in the future, the energy storage performance of such self-assembled electrodes can be further optimized and their application scope expanded by exploring alternative synthesis parameters, selecting compatible electrolytes, and optimizing anode materials. title: MXene/Biomass-derived activated carbon composite for supercapacitor applications
authors: Rohit Sinha, P. Sai Kiran, K. Vijay Kumar, Niranjan Pandit, Chintham Satish, Saurav Keshri, Anup Kumar Keshri
conclusion: In this work, we have successfully synthesized the biomass-activated carbon incorporated in the Mxene composite. In this, biomass-activated carbon was prepared by utilizing the two-stage activation process with the help of KOH in different weight ratios. The KOH-activated carbon addition has attributed superior characteristics like induced defects and hierarchal porous structure in synthesized Mxene composite. In particular, the MxACK3 composite exhibited superior properties in terms of higher surface area (SSA) 2080.55 m2 g−1 with the coexistence of meso and micropores, hydrophilic nature (CA = 13.46°), increased interlayer spacing (d = ∼1.1 nm). This improved electrochemical behavior can be ascribed to reduced restacking issues, the formation of a 3D open structure with incorporated activated carbon, and increased active sites for ion storage and transport. Our findings delve into a new pathway for utilizing biomass-activated carbon's capability to improve Mxene-based composites and nanomaterials in different electrolyte environments for energy storage applications.
