Compared to conventional IMSCs, the optimized FMSCs, achieved by adjusting the width and thickness of microelectrodes, showed a maximum areal specific capacitance of 615.3 μF cm−2 , a cutoff frequency (f 0 ) of 1.21 kHz, and a high-power characteristic at an ultrahigh scan rate of 2000 V s−1 . These improvements can be attributed to the fractal structure design, which creates a superior electric field, accelerating the motion of ions in the electrolyte and facilitating greater ion absorption around these sites. Moreover, the integrated FMSCs exhibit excellent uniformity, meeting the customized requirements for operating voltage windows and capacity across various frequency ranges. Notably, they played a crucial role in the AC line-filtering circuit, effectively filtering various waveforms and high-frequency (20 kHz) AC signals to produce DC signals. This study provides novel guidance for designing MSC structures to meet the AC-DC conversion demands in micro/nano energy power management systems.

title: Multilayered MXene electrodes in deep eutectic solvent ionic liquid electrolyte for supercapacitor applications
authors: Derya Kapusuz Yavuz, Abdulcabbar Yavuz
conclusion: This work examined the electrochemical performance of ml-Ti3 C2 Tx , a MXene family member, in several electrolytes, focusing on the cost-effective ionic liquid Ethaline. ml-Ti3 C2 Tx attained a capacitance of 356 mF/cm2 in Ethaline at a scan rate of 5 mV/s which increased to 640 mF/cm2 at 1 mV/s. This performance was observed throughout a large potential window of 1.7 V, exceeding several MXene capacitance values reported in the literature. The electrochemical performance of ml-Ti3 C2 Tx is markedly affected by the characteristics of the electrolyte. Alkaline (KOH) and neutral (Na2 SO4 ) aqueous electrolytes are unsuitable for MXene-based energy storage due to degradation and negligible electrochemical activity, respectively, within the 1.7 V potential window. The wider potential window noted in Ethaline was ascribed to improved ion intercalation and enhanced electrostatic interactions between the ionic liquid species and the Ti3 C2 Tx layers. The broadest potential range of 1.7 V, including both positive and negative voltages, resulted in the greatest capacitance of MXene in Ethaline. Narrower windows of 0.6 V (positive) and 1.2 V (negative) resulted in lower capacitance values. These findings underscore the importance of a higher potential window in increasing energy density, as it allows for the use of fewer or smaller supercapacitor units to obtain the same storage capacity. The contribution of this work is essential for advancing high-performance, durable supercapacitors that can satisfy the requirements of modern energy applications, such as renewable energy systems and electric vehicles.

title: MXene mastery: Transforming supercapacitors through solid-solution innovations
authors: Yedluri Anil Kumar, Reddi Mohan Naidu Kalla, Tholkappiyan Ramachandran, Ahmed M. Fouda, H.H. Hegazy, Md Moniruzzaman, Jaewoong Lee
journal: Journal of Industrial and Engineering Chemistry
conclusion: Conclusions and future prospects  Researchers have increasingly focused on MXene solid-solution materials for advancing supercapacitor technology, driven by the distinctive properties of MXenes that make them highly effective for energy storage applications. Among the most notable advantages are their large specific surface area, high electrical conductivity, and the unique two-dimensional (2D) structure that enables fast ion diffusion and charge transport. In particular, titanium carbide-based MXenes like Ti 3 C 2 T x have emerged as strong candidates for supercapacitors due to their ability to achieve high capacitance, quick charge–discharge rates, and superior power and energy densities when compared to traditional carbon-based supercapacitors. One of the key advantages of MXenes is their tunable surface chemistry, which allows for precise control over their electrochemical properties. By modifying surface terminations (e.g., −O, –OH, −F), researchers can adjust the interaction of MXenes with different electrolytes, enabling the design of application-specific supercapacitors. This flexibility opens up opportunities to improve energy and power density simultaneously, something that has historically been difficult to achieve with conventional supercapacitors, which tend to favor either high power or high energy storage, but not both. Moreover, MXenes' intrinsic pseudocapacitive behavior contributes significantly to their outstanding performance. Unlike electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), which store energy through physical adsorption of ions at the electrode–electrolyte interface, pseudocapacitive MXenes can undergo fast surface redox reactions. This results in higher charge storage capabilities and better overall electrochemical performance. Recent studies have demonstrated that MXene-based supercapacitors can achieve specific capacitance values exceeding 1,500 F/g, positioning them as frontrunners for next-generation energy storage devices.  Additionally, MXenes' 2D layered structure allows for easy fabrication of flexible and lightweight electrodes, making them ideal for applications in portable electronics and wearable devices. The combination of flexibility, mechanical robustness, and high conductivity ensures that MXene-based supercapacitors can deliver consistent performance even under mechanical stress, such as bending or stretching. This makes them particularly attractive for use in emerging technologies, such as flexible and stretchable electronics, where traditional rigid materials are unsuitable. Despite these advantages, several challenges remain in the practical deployment of MXene-based supercapacitors. One major issue is restacking, where the 2D MXene layers tend to reassemble during electrode fabrication, leading to reduced surface area and limited ion accessibility. This negatively impacts the overall performance of the supercapacitor, especially in terms of ion transport and capacitance retention at high charging rates. To address this, researchers have explored various strategies, such as intercalating larger ions or molecules between MXene layers to increase interlayer spacing, thus preventing restacking and enhancing ion diffusion. Another significant challenge is the long-term stability and cycling performance of supercapacitors based on MXene in real-world scenarios. For real-world applications, it is essential to understand the causes of deterioration and discover solutions to improve durability. To guarantee the viability of large-scale manufacturing for commercial deployment, more research into the cost-effectiveness and scalability of MXene production is necessary. To fully realize the potential of MXene solid-solution materials as supercapacitors, which are currently at the crossroads of exciting advances and established obstacles, researchers must keep digging and working together across fields if we want to build high-performance supercapacitors of the future.  There is tremendous hope for the future of energy storage technology in the realm of supercapacitor research with MXene solid-solution materials. To satisfy the increasing need for effective, high-performance energy storage devices, researchers want to optimize MXene-based supercapacitors further and overcome existing restrictions. Investigating the reasons for deterioration and creating ways to make the materials more resilient are two possible ways to solve the problems with cycle performance and long-term stability. Materials with enhanced structural integrity and electrochemical performance might be the goal of future research into MXene synthesis processes, which could lead to materials with longer operational lives and maintain functioning. Continuous efforts are being made to optimize production processes and minimize costs related to MXene manufacture, with an eye on ensuring commercial viability and scalability. Supercapacitors based on MXene would be more widely available for use in a variety of applications if large-scale manufacture were possible due to developments in scalable synthesis processes. Furthermore, to discover new combinations of characteristics that might further improve energy storage capability, researchers will likely investigate newer MXene compositions and hybrid materials. To drive innovation and put laboratory results into practical applications, multidisciplinary research including material scientists, electrochemists, and engineers must be prioritized. Supercapacitor research with MXene solid-solution materials has exciting prospects as we tackle present obstacles, discover new possibilities, and finally realize their promise as a game-changing technology in the ever-changing energy storage landscape. Better and more efficient energy storage solutions for many uses, from handheld devices to grid-level power storage, may be possible with the further development of the field and the incorporation of MXenes into supercapacitors.

title: Functional integrated electromagnetic interference shielding in flexible micro-supercapacitors by cation-intercalation typed Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Xin Feng, Jing Ning, Boyu Wang, Haibin Guo, Maoyang Xia, Dong Wang, Jincheng Zhang, Zhong-Shuai Wu, Yue Hao
conclusion: 3  Conclusion  In summary, a highly conductive Mn ions introduced Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene was developed as a promising material for MSCs functional EMI shielding. The cation intercalation mechanism of Ti 3 C 2 T x was explored as that Mn ions were inclined to be bonding with interfacial oxygen-contained terminal, performed as the orbital hybridization of Mn 3d and O 2p. Cation intercalation enabled to expand the d-space and improve the electrical conductivity of Ti 3 C 2 T x . With the unrivaled features of Mn ions-introduced Ti 3 C 2 T x , the as-prepared MSCs delivered excellent energy storage ability and outstanding EMI shielding efficiency. This study can provide powerful information on the surface structure and the intercalation mechanism of Ti 3 C 2 T x at the atomic level, enrich the understanding of interlayer engineering of the MXenes. More importantly, this work also can propose new views of functional MSCs with EMI shielding for special on-chip application in microelectronics, endowing great significance for the stability of integrated circuits and micro-systems.

title: Insights into the synergistic effect of V3S4 decorated Ti3C2 MXene as an electrode for asymmetric supercapacitor
authors: Sandra Mathew, Kalathiparambil Rajendra Pai Sunajadevi, Arun Varghese, Dephan Pinheiro, B. Saravanakumar
journal: Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  A novel MXene-based binary composite material was synthesized by incorporating V 3 S 4 through hydrothermal method and evaluated for its electrochemical supercapacitance performance. The innovative approach has resulted in a composite that leverages the unique properties of both Ti 3 C 2 MXene and V 3 S 4 , leading to reduced self-stacking of Ti 3 C 2 , increased accessible surface area, and exposure of more active sites for charge transport, thereby enhancing conductivity. The Ti 3 C 2 /V 3 S 4 electrode exhibits an enhanced C sp of 1323.7 Fg -1 at 1 Ag -1 , with a remarkable capacitance retention rate of 90.5 % over 2000 cycles. It also maintains a lower R ct value of 4.6 Ω, that is significantly less than that of pristine Ti 3 C 2 and V 3 S 4 . The fabricated device, Ti 3 C 2 /V 3 S 4 //AC exhibited a high energy density of 60.6 Whkg −1 at a power density of 649.2 Wkg -1 . Our findings underscore the promise of MXene-based materials for advancing next-generation energy storage solutions, highlighting their potential to deliver high performance and reliability.

title: Optimizing ZnSe microspheres through 2D MXene for asymmetric pseudocapacitive supercapacitors and efficient hydrogen production via water splitting
authors: Inaam Ullah, Ayesha Irfan, Mai Li, Samira Saddique, Tiantian Yang, Hanxue Zhao, Nimra Irshad, Kaishuai Yang, Chunrui Wang, Paul K. Chu
conclusion: In this study, the morphological and crystallographic properties of hydrothermally synthesized ZnSe microspheres are optimized. The synergistic effects rendered by the 2D-MXene nanosheets enhance the electrochemical performance in the APSC device as well as the water-splitting setup. The ZnSe electrode shows good electrochemical performance, but self-aggregation and side reactions of Zn restrict the performance of the cathode and applications. The Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets function as a physical barrier to alleviate agglomeration and impeding side reactions of Zn, thereby enabling ZnSe to expose more sites in addition to a consistent supply of Zn2+ , ultimately augmenting the reversibility, enhancing the cyclic stability, and diminishing the overpotential. The composite electrode demonstrates superior integrity and dispersion, resulting in a longer discharging time than the ZnSe electrode. The ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx electrode shows outstanding cyclic stability (98.81 % capacity retention for 10,000 cycles), high specific capacitance of 1673.8 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , and remarkable pseudocapacitive behavior of 88 % at 60 mV s−1 . DFT results confirm the higher adsorption energy, high electron density, and stable structure of the composite electrodes. The AC//ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx -APSC device demonstrates remarkable cyclic stability, energy density, and high specific capacitance boding well for energy storage applications. LSV reveals that the ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx electrode has a remarkable tafel slope in OER (∼51.3 mV dec−1 ) compared to ZnSe (68.7 mV dec−1 ) besides outstanding properties of ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx in HER. This innovative approach effectively mitigates the inherent limitations of ZnSe and significantly enhances the overall electrochemical performance, positioning the ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx as a promising candidate for energy storage and water splitting applications. title: Construction of proton channels in POMCPs@MXene electrodes for flexible all-solid-state symmetrical supercapacitors
authors: Xiaoyi Li, Yifu Wu, Tingting Chen, Qian wang, Cuiwen Lu, Hongru Hao, Bo Wei, Haolin wang, Chengbao Yao, Feng Zhang, Haijun Pang, Guangning Wang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, this study demonstrates notable advancements in the development of POMCPs-based flexible supercapacitor materials. We successfully fabricated a 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ-based FSS device, showcasing a combination of favorable electrochemical performance and mechanical flexibility. Through structural design, we fine-tuned the arrangement of water molecules to customize a novel Ni(itmb) 4 [H 2 SiW 12 O 40 ]·5H 2 O (Compound 1 ) with proton-conductive channels. The Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene nanosheets and the customized POMCPs are combined through a simple composite method to produce the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ composite material, which exhibits an ultrahigh proton conductivity of 0.16 S cm −1 . This represents a promising advancement in ion-conductive materials for supercapacitors. This work also innovatively presents a comprehensive study of the influence mechanisms governing the relationships among wettability, impedance, composition ratio, and capacitance within the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ material system. Results indicate that optimizing the composition ratio of POMCPs to Ti₃C₂Tₓ effectively enhances material hydrophilicity, as evidenced by a contact angle of 83.4° with 2 M H₃PO₄. This improvement subsequently reduces impedance and increases C s. As expected, the supercapacitor performance of the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ composite significantly outperforms that of individual POMCP and MXene components: at 5 A g −1 , its C s reaches 892.3 F g −1 , four times that of 1 -GCE; its rate capability is 81.6 %, 1.56 times that of 1 -GCE; and its cycle stability is 96.8 % (vs. 60.3 % for 1 -GCE). Additionally, the FSS device assembled with 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ demonstrates satisfactory energy and power densities, capable of powering a red LED. Notably, it retains 90 % of its C s under significant bending, highlighting its potential for flexible energy storage applications. Overall, the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ composite offers new perspectives for supercapacitor material development, contributing to efforts to meet the demands of high-performance, flexible energy storage in modern electronics. title: Revealing the ionic storage mechanisms of Mo2VC2Tz (MXene) in multiple aqueous electrolytes for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Xiaodie Xuan, Yangyang Xie, Yi Tang, Jianghong Zhou, Zhao Bi, Junhui Zou, Yu-ang Lei, Jiahang Gao, Lu Li, Aibo Zhang, Chenhui Yang
conclusion: To sum up, 2D few-layer bimetallic Mo2 VC2 Tz MXene nanomaterials have been successfully prepared by introducing high electrochemical activity V atoms into the precursor MAX. The unique bimetallic solid-solution structure of Mo2 VC2 Tz has an enlarged layer spacing and oxygen-dominated surface termini, which together enhance ion accessibility and redox active site density. The electrochemical results indicate that at a current density of 0.1 A g−1 , the Mo2 VC2 Tz electrodes in 1M H2 SO4 , 1M Al2 (SO4 )3 , and 1M KOH have a top three high specific capacitances in 257.6, 143.4, and 134.4 F g−1 , respectively. In an acidic electrolyte, the oxidation-reduction reaction is effectively promoted by the strong interaction between hydrated hydrogen ions (protons) and oxygen-containing functional groups on the surface of the electrode materials, so that the specific capacitance of the system is significantly higher than that of other electrolytic liquid systems. After 20,000 cycles, the Mo2 VC2 Tz film electrode retains a capacity retention rate of 95.71% in the 1M H2 SO4 electrolyte and the Coulomb efficiency is close to 100%. Confirmed by DFT calculations showing increased density of states near the Fermi level and reduced H+ adsorption energy. These structural and electronic modifications synergistically promote rapid proton diffusion and reversible multivalent redox reactions, establishing Mo2 VC2 Tz as a high-performance electrode material for acidic electrolyte-based supercapacitors. In general, this study not only provides theoretical guidance for the application of bimetallic solid-solution MXene materials in the field of energy storage, but also establish an innovative research foundation for the development of high-performance electrochemical energy storage devices by combining experiment and theory. title: Electromagnetic interference shielding, mechanical, and flame retardant behaviors of Ti3C2Tx-MXene/glass fabric epoxy hybrid composites
authors: Ayten Nur Yuksel Yilmaz, Ayse Celik Bedeloglu, Doruk Erdem Yunus
conclusion: In this study, fiber-reinforced composites consisting of six layers with different configurations were produced using both MXene-coated and uncoated glass fabrics. The MXene-coated fabrics received 5 and 10 layers of coating. The effect of the number of coatings and various fabric configurations on EMI-SE in the X-band range was investigated. It was observed that increasing the number of conductive layers in the composites led to higher SET . Compared to the pure composite (C1), the composites with 5 and 10 layers of MXene coating (5MXC5 and 10MXC5) showed total shielding effectiveness values that were 147.05 % and 205.80 % higher, respectively. Among the 5MX and 10MX composite groups, the samples 5MXC5 and 10MXC5, which demonstrated the highest shielding effectiveness, underwent bending, ILSS, hardness, and flammability tests. The MXene coating on glass fabric was found to reduce the burning rate of the composites, with 5MXC5 and 10MXC5 showing 15.25 % and 26.31 % lower burning rate than C1, respectively. Moreover, the addition of MXene, a two-dimensional ceramic material with high hardness, increased the hardness of the composites. The hardness values of 5MXC5 and 10MXC5 were 133.29 and 145.05 HV, respectively, representing increases of 10.03 % and 19.74 % over C1. According to the results from bending and ILSS tests, a decrease in composite strength was observed with MXene reinforcement. The increased presence of MXene flakes on the glass fabric surfaces hindered the epoxy's ability to sufficiently impregnate in the thickness direction, weakening the interfacial bond between the fiber and the matrix, which led to a reduction in strength. After the bending test, the fractured surfaces of the composites were examined under a microscope, revealing tensile, compression, and delamination damages were observed. Compared to the neat composite, 10MXC5 showed reductions of 23.88 % and 24.37 % in flexural and ILSS strength, respectively. This study demonstrates that MXene can provide high electromagnetic shielding efficiency to insulating glass fiber-epoxy composites due to its high electrical conductivity. It is anticipated that the total electromagnetic efficiency in the X band range can be further improved through different configurations and increased the amount of fillers. Moreover, this research lays the groundwork for developing glass fiber-reinforced composite materials with electromagnetic shielding and radar-absorbing properties, particularly for aerospace applications. title: MXene (Ti3C2Tx) anodes for asymmetric supercapacitors with high active mass loading
authors: Xuelin Li, Jianfeng Zhu, Wenyu Liang, Igor Zhitomirsky
conclusion: We developed a high-performance Ti3 C2 Tx -CNT composite electrode containing 20% CNT with a 40 mg cm−2 high AML, which can deliver excellent rate performance, a 2.26 F cm−2 high areal capacitance, and long-term cyclic stability in a negative potential range. The enhanced capacitive behavior benefits from the synergy between Ti3 C2 Tx layers and a proper amount of CNT to form more interconnected nanopores for efficient electrolyte ions transfer, improved electronic conductivity, and build more accessible nanostructure for effective reactions. The high mass loadings benefit from an advanced PMMA binder, in which solution multilayered Ti3 C2 Tx and multiwalled carbon nanotube can be well dispersed and mixed. A MnO2 -CNT composite electrode with a 20% carbon nanotube was also fabricated by the same procedure and tested in a positive potential window. Asymmetric devices operating in a cell voltage of 1.6 V consisted of Ti3 C2 Tx -CNT-20 anodes and MnO2 -CNT-20 cathodes, possessing a 1.24 F cm−2 maximum areal capacitance, good cyclic stability after 1000 cycles, as well as a 0.44 mWh cm−2 maximum energy density. The proposed approach in this study provides an idea to design and fabricate advanced electrodes for asymmetric devices in industrial energy-storage applications, which can be operated in large voltage windows with enhanced energy-power characteristics. title: Nickel-infused cobalt ferrite/MXene nanocomposites: Structural insights and electrochemical properties for high performance supercapacitors
authors: W. Trinisha Infancy, T. Jaqulin Jenila, R. Rathikha, S. Maruthasalamoorthy, Belina Xavier, R. Navamathavan, Manikandan Ayyar, V. Mohanavel, M. Santhamoorthy, S. Santhoshkumar, Saravanan Rajendran
conclusion: The slick coprecipitation approach was used to produce nickel doped cobalt ferrite with incorporation of MXene nanocomposite. The clustering of the nanoparticles was revealed by FESEM pictures. HRTEM micrographs demonstrate the formation of nanosized particles, the elements Ni, Co, Fe, Ti, and O were confirmed to be present in the EDX patterns without any impurities. The elemental composition has been examined using XPS. Bands lower than 1000 cm−1 in the FTIR spectra have been induced due to the ferrite groups' vibrations. For each individual sample, the tetrahedral metal–oxygen stretching vibration was the cause of the band (ν 1 ) that was seen at about 550 cm-1. The band (ν 2 ) 420 cm-1 emerged by the metal‑oxygen stretching vibration at the octahedral sites in the produced samples. Saturation magnetization increased when Co1−x Nix Fe2 O4 doped with MXene. Electrochemical characteristics derived from GCD plots showed pre-eminent capacitance values, 96.33 Cg−1 , 121.63 Cg−1 , 210.15 Cg−1 , 361.2 Cg−1 and 367.2 Cg−1 for Co1-x Nix Fe2 O4 (x = 0.03, 0.05, 0.07, 0.10 and 0.10/MXene) at a precise scan rate 10 mV /s and thereby intending it to be a strong contender for applications involving supercapacitors. title: Ionic liquid induced gelation of Mo1.33C i-MXene for enhanced supercapacitor and Li-Ion storage performance
authors: Zhaohui Chen, He Chong, Peng Hei, Hongyun Guo, Zhen Ma, Qiang Wang, Yu Song, Weibin Cui
conclusion: In conclusion, the introduction of ionic liquids (ILs), specifically [Bmim]Cl and [Omim]Cl, effectively induces rapid gelation in Mo1.33 C i -MXene aqueous solutions. A three-dimensional network is formed and extended d spacing is realized by the ion exchange of TBA+ by [Bmim]+ and [Omim]+ . Additionally, a significant increase in surface −O functional group is also observed. These modifications lead into significant enhanced supercapacitance of 552.6 F·g−1 at 1 A·g−1 and Li-ion storage capacity of 1056 mAh·g−1 at 50 mA g−1 along with the long-term cyclic stability. The computational results reveal that the increased content of −O functional groups on the surface of Mo1.33 C enhances Li adsorption capacity. In addition, the expanded layer spacing enhances both the Li-ion storage capacity and diffusion kinetics. Through interlayer and surface engineering, the Li-ion adsorption capacity of Mo1.33 C is enhanced, and Li-ion diffusion during lithiation is accelerated, enabling Mo1.33 C to exhibit superior Li-ion storage performance. These results suggest that the Mo1.33 C i -MXene can be applied as the promising electrode in the supercapacitor and Li-ion batteries through our efficient and easy strategy. conclusion: In summary, our study successfully synthesized MNCS-0.02 composites via a one-step hydrothermal method, integrating NCS into exfoliated Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets. title: Tunable interlayer spacings Ti3C2Tx MXene/Ni/C for enhanced electromagnetic microwave absorption
authors: Jingyu Song, Yongqian Shen, Guibin Zhang, Mingxuan Sun, Mengyao Han, Xueyan Du
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this study, xDA-Ti 3 C 2 with controllable layer spacing was prepared via a dehydration condensation reaction between xDA and –NH 2 functionalized Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene layers. Subsequently, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/Ni/C composites with unique layered structures were prepared using a simple mechanical stirring and carbonization strategy. Compared to traditional MAs, the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/Ni/C composites retained the accordion structure of pure Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene. The increase in layer spacing exposes the material to a wider interface, preventing agglomeration and providing a favorable interface for subsequent nickel metal doping. Moreover, the electromagnetic parameters could be accurately controlled by changing the doping amount of Ni metal. Several highly dispersed magnetic particles are doped into the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheet layer or attached to its surface, imparting the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheet with magnetic characteristics and significantly improving its magnetic loss capability. Finally, the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/Ni/C composites exhibit excellent EMWs absorption performance (RL = −42.3 dB) owing to the synergistic effect of multicomponent complementary effects, conduction loss, interfacial polarization, and dielectric loss. Molecular welding offers an inimitable method for controlling the interlayer spacing between the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene layers and other two-dimensional materials, providing theoretical guidance for designing high-performance, two-dimensional wave-absorbing materials.

title: Enhanced electrochemical performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene film based supercapacitors in H2SO4/KI redox additive electrolyte
authors: Jianjian Fu, Lei Li, Damin Lee, Je Moon Yun, Bong Ki Ryu, Kwang Ho Kim
conclusion: In summary, freestanding Ti3 C2 Tx film was prepared through vacuum filtration process. The electrochemical performance of the Ti3 C2 Tx //Ti3 C2 Tx RAESs was systematically studied in H2 SO4 /KI electrolyte. Owing to the combinational effect of the pseudocapacitance performance of the MXene and reversible redox reaction of KI additive, the Ti3 C2 Tx //H2 SO4 /KI//Ti3 C2 Tx RAESs exhibits an optimized volumetric specific capacitance of 601 F cm−3 (gravimetric specific capacitance of 166 F g−1 ) at current density of 1 A g−1 . Moreover, the device delivered a volumetric energy density of 83.5 Wh L–1 at a volumetric power density of 1800 W L–1 . This excellent electrochemical performance of the RAES device suggests the importance of KI additive with enhanced redox reactions for high performance Ti3 C2 Tx based energy storage devices. title: Blade-coated Ti3C2Tx MXene films for pseudocapacitive energy storage and infrared stealth
authors: Haoxiang Ma, Junqi Wang, Jingfeng Wang, Kun Shang, Yang Yang, Zhimin Fan
conclusion: In this work, a free-standing MXene film was prepared using the blade coating method, and the electrochemical capacitance and infrared stealth behavior of the blade-coated MXene film was investigated. Since the blade-coated MXene film had a more regular interlayer lamellar arrangement and denser structure than the traditional MXene film prepared by vacuum-assisted filtration, the density and conductivity reached 3.95 g cm−3 and 8000 S cm−1 , respectively. In addition, the blade-coated MXene film exhibited superior mechanical properties to the filtered MXene film. At a scan rate of 5 mV s−1 , the blade-coated MXene film had a gravimetric capacitance of 347 F g−1 and a volumetric capacitance of 1353 F cm−3 . Meanwhile, the capacitance retention rate at a scan rate of 100 mV s−1 was almost consistent with that of the vacuum-assisted filtered MXene film. Furthermore, the blade-coated MXene film exhibited outstanding infrared stealth performance because of its low mid-infrared emissivity. Therefore, it has the potential for infrared camouflage applications in the military field. Besides, the size of the blade-coated MXene film is scalable, rendering such film more suitable for industrial-scale production. This work is of considerable significance for promoting the practical applications of MXene film in the field of electrochemical energy storage and infrared stealth. title: Influence of natural organic matter on ecotoxicity, ingestion and depuration of MXenes (Ti3C2Tx) in D. magna and R. subcapitata
authors: M. Ahl, M.B. Nielsen, A. Baun, L.M. Skjolding
conclusion: This study found no acute immobilization of D. magna after the exposure to MXenes at concentrations up to 100 mg/L and no changes in response after aging or addition of NOM. Conversely, growth rate inhibition was shown for freshwater green algae (R. subcapitata) with EC50 -values of 41 and 81 mg/L for freshly prepared and aged suspensions of MXenes, respectively. Conversely, EC10 -values for the aged and freshly prepared suspensions was 5.6 and 0.55 mg/L respectively. Marked differences was also observed after the addition of NOM resulting in a decrease in growth inhibition for both the freshly prepared (EC50 190 mg/L) and the aged (EC50 282 mg/L) MXenes suspensions. Exposure to a mixture of PCP and MXenes did not significantly affect the response of algae, but significantly lowered the acute immobilization of D. magna . In ingestion experiments, addition of NOM increased the content of MXenes in daphnia. However, a rapid depuration was observed both with and without NOM present and depuration was further acceleration in the presence of a food source. MXenes were depurated to levels below the quantification limit when presented to a food source for >1 h, thus the potential for trophic transfer from daphnia to higher level organisms was found to be minimal. It was concluded that the presence of NOM influenced neither the stability nor the ecotoxicological response of both lower tier organisms tested herein. Consequently, it is expected that testing without NOM could represent a conservative estimate of effects in an environmental setting. CRediT authorship contribution statement M. title: Improving the electrochemical properties of MXene through intercalation of WC and TiC nanoparticles for supercapacitors application
authors: Sayed Zafar Abbas, Dhanasekaran Vikraman, Zulfqar Ali Sheikh, Shahzaib Ali, Iftikhar Hussain, Jeung Choon Goak, Hyun-Seok Kim, Doyoung Byun, Jongwan Jung, Sajjad Hussain, Naesung Lee
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: Increasing environmental concerns and the energy crisis have highlighted the need for renewable energy solutions, with SCs gaining attention owing to their efficiency, low cost, and long cycle life. This study addressed the challenges of using MXenes as supercapacitor electrodes by intercalating TiC and WC nanoparticles into MXene sheets to form TiC@MXene and WC@MXene hybrid composites. These composites leverage the high conductivity and hydrophilicity of MXenes while enhancing their stability and reducing restacking issues. The TiC@MXene and WC@MXene hybrid composites exhibit a specific capacitance of 481 and 478 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and maintain 95.5 and 96.3 % of their initial capacitance after 5,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 , showcasing superior electrochemical performance and cycling stability. The WC@MXene //AC ASC device, demonstrating an energy density of 53 Wh kg− 1 at 2.25 kW kg−1 with 97.7 % retention after 5,000 cycles, further emphasizes the potential of these composites for high-performance supercapacitors. title: A compressible asymmetric supercapacitor based on carbon Felt/MWCNT@PANI and MXene
authors: Elif Vargun, Haojie Fei, Ulku Anik, Qilin Cheng, Petr Saha
conclusion: An effective compressible asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated using a-CF/MWCNT@PANI positive electrode and a Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene negative electrode. Both XPS and FTIR spectroscopy confirm that the first MWCNTs were loaded into a-CF, and then PANI functionalization of a-CF/MWCNT was performed successfully. With MWCNTs and PANI coatings, the electric conductivity and specific capacitance of the positive electrode were significantly increased. For the MXene negative electrode, a successful etching of aluminum from MAX phase was verified by XRD analysis. Moreover, SEM analysis demonstrated flake-like morphologies of 2D MXene nanosheets. By the asymmetric configuration, the cell voltage of the assembled supercapacitor was extended to 1.3 V. The specific capacitance was found as 1.6 F cm−2 at 5 mA cm−2 , the corresponding energy density and power density were 262 μWh cm−2 and 2.7 mW cm−2 , respectively. The asymmetric cell exhibited an excellent retention rate of 92.4 % after 1000 GCD cycles. Moreover, the asymmetric cell became compressible due to the compressibility of CF, and the capacitance retention retained more than 90 % over 200 compression-recovery cycles. Considering the preparation procedure, it is possible to conclude that, as a result, a practical, economical, and robust compressible asymmetric supercapacitor was developed. title: Synergistically coupling of 3D FeNi-LDH arrays with Ti3C2Tx-MXene nanosheets toward superior symmetric supercapacitor
authors: Renjie Zhang, Jidong Dong, Wei Zhang, Lina Ma, Zaixing Jiang, Jiajun Wang, Yudong Huang
conclusion: In summary, 3D FeNi-LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanohybrids were successfully prepared via an electrostatic attraction connection of negatively charged 2D Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets with positively charged FeNi-LDH arrays. In this architecture, the high conductivity Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets not only can construct a successive conductive network but also act as the platform for the growth of FeNi-LDH arrays, ensuring the superb electrical conductivity of the whole energy materials. As a result, the optimized battery-type electrode Fe1 Ni3 -LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene indicates remarkable rate capability, the outstanding gravimetric capacitance for 922.6 F g-1 , and retains for 88% after 10,000 cycles. Moreover, the symmetric supercapacitor based on Fe1 Ni3 -LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene electrodes can exhibit excellent electrochemical performance with a high energy density of 94.1 Wh kg-1 at a power density of 802.4 W kg-1 . These superior electrochemical performances are benefited from the high capacity of Fe1 Ni3 -LDH arrays, excellent conductivity of the Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets and their synergistically interactive effect in the heterostructure. This strategy not only proves the feasibility of the development of the desirable Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene, but also paves the way for the fabrication of the hybrids electrodes with a stable interface for high-performance supercapacitors. title: In situ synthesis of M (Fe, Cu, Co and Ni)-MOF@MXene composites for enhanced specific capacitance and cyclic stability in supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Yaxiong Ji, Weibin Li, Yang You, Guihong Xu
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, a series of MOF@MXene composite materials were synthesized by a one-step in situ method. Intercalation of the MXene into the Co-MOF, Ni-MOF, Cu-MOF and Fe-MOF materials contributes to four types of surfaces: “ flower-like ”, “ rock ”, “ pomegranate seed ” and “ sponge ” surfaces, respectively, which contribute to different electrochemical performances. During the composite process, both Co and Ni ions are initially fixed on the surface of MXene through electrostatic interactions and serve as the centers for in-situ growth of MOFs, whereas Co ions offer stronger interaction with the suitable dosage of MXene layers. Uniform distribution of MXene on the surface of Co-MOF and Ni-MOF facilitates efficient ion transport channels and high charge transfer rates for supercapacitor applications. Among the various MOF@MXene-based materials, Ni-MOF@MX 2 shows outstanding properties with a high specific capacitance of 1160.5 F g −1 at a current density of 1 A/g, and moreover maintains significant cyclic stability after 10,000 cycles at 20 A/g. The Ni-MOF@MX 2//AC ASC exhibits a maximum energy density of 48.2 Wh kg −1 at 750 W kg −1 and retains 94 % of the initial capacity after 10,000 cycles. Both experimental and theoretical calculations have demonstrated that these excellent electrochemical performances are due to the synergistic effect between MXene nanosheets and unique structure of MOFs. Such prepared materials possibly shed a light on solving the key issues of MXene layer stacking, poor conductivity of MOFs, and the development of high-performance energy storage devices for their practical applications.

title: Ti3C2Tx MXene decorated with CoMnO3 / CoMn2O4 nanoparticles as electrocatalysts for anion exchange membrane water electrolysis

conclusion: The electrostatic self-assembly method was used to prepare CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 –Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanocomposites. The XRD analysis confirmed the rhombohedral/cubic structure of CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 in the nanocomposites. The SEM and TEM morphology show the CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 nanoparticles decorated into the multilayer Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheets. The developed a novel CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 –Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanocomposites as the OER/HER electrocatalyst in AEM water electrolyzer. The Ti3 C2 Tx enhances the OER activity of CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 by altering its electronic structure and enhancing the electrical conductivity. Therefore, the interface between CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 and the Ti3 C2 Tx results in synergistic effects, that reduce the ohmic loss and electrode loss, leading to remarkable AEM electrolyzer, utilizing performance. The AEM electrolyzer by CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 –Ti3 C2 Tx (20 wt%) achieves a current density of 520 mA cm− 2 at 1.8 V outperforming the electrolyzer. The CoMnO3 /CoMn2 O4 –Ti3 C2 Tx couple possesses long-term cyclic durability over 3000 cycles. title: Ti3C2Tx MXene and Vanadium nitride/Porous carbon as electrodes for asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Sandhya Venkateshalu, Andrews Nirmala Grace
conclusion: In summary, this work reports on the testing of Ti3 C2 Tx as the negative electrode and VN/PC as the positive electrode in an asymmetric cell. Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes were synthesized by etching the Al layers by immersing them in aqueous HF solutions and further delaminating them with DMSO. It is well known that the synthesis of Vanadium nitride is very difficult without the use of the dangerous ammonia gas. Herein, we have synthesized Vanadium nitride/porous carbon through a simple and safe method using the data available in literature with modifications. In a 3-electrode system, Ti3 C2 Tx MXene and VN/PC electrode exhibits specific capacitances of 283 F/g and 52 F/g at 0.5 A/g respectively. VN/PC//Ti3 C2 Tx asymmetric 2-electrode cell exhibits a superior capcitance of 105 F/g at 1 A/g with energy density and power density of 12.81 Wh/kg and 985.8 W/kg respectively. title: 3D ZnO hexagonal prism-decorated 2D MXene-based high-performance flexible symmetric supercapacitor
authors: Sahil Jangra, Shilpi Sengupta, Azam Raza, Aadil Rashid Lone, Bhushan Kumar, Manab Kundu, Iftikhar Hussain, Kavita Pandey, Subhankar Das, M.S. Goyat
conclusion: For the first time, ZnO hexagonal prism decorated MXene sheets were synthesized via a hydrothermal technique to address the restacking issue of d-Ti3 C2 Tx and improve ion transport for enhanced electrochemical performance. The distribution of ZnO hexagonal prism on the surface and between the MXene layers improved the accessibility of active sites, significantly boosting the electrode's specific capacitance and extended cycling stability. This study not only demonstrates a novel method to mitigate MXene's inherent limitations but also establishes a controlled strategy to tailor the structural and electrochemical properties of hybrid materials through precise morphology-engineering of ZnO. The ZnO hexagonal prism decorated MXene achieved an impressive specific capacitance of 140 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 , nearly twice the capacitance of MXene. It also exhibited impressive cycling stability, retaining 97.2 % of its specific capacitance following 12,000 cycles at 3 A g−1 . Additionally, a flexible symmetric supercapacitor device fabricated from this material demonstrated remarkable mechanical flexibility, maintaining stable performance even after bending at different angles such as 0°, 60°, 90°, and 180°. The flexible symmetric supercapacitor device demonstrated an energy density of 6.33 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 600 W kg−1 , highlighting the potential of ZnO hexagonal prism decorated MXene for flexible, high-performance energy storage systems. This work underscores the synergistic effect of integrating ZnO hexagonal prism with MXene, overcoming key limitations, and advancing the development of next-generation supercapacitors. title: Optimizing the electron spin state of hierarchical NiCo2O4@MXene@LDH 3D composite electrode by heterointerface engineering to enhance energy density and excellent cyclic stability of supercapacitor
authors: Jianghong You, Yiming Yuan, Chen Zhang, Haoming Xu, Mingyao Chen, Ying Wang, Dongsheng Chen
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: In this work, we proposed and successfully constructed a three-dimensional hierarchical NiCo2 O4 @MXene@LDH (LDH: layered double hydroxide) composite electrode through rational heterointerface engineering to overcome the intrinsic limitations of NiCo2 O4 -based materials in supercapacitor applications. The strategy effectively integrates the advantages of NiCo2 O4 nanorods, conductive MXene nanosheets, and electrochemically active NiCo-LDH nanoparticles into a unified architecture, thereby achieving a well-interconnected structure with enhanced electron/ion transport pathways and expanded electrochemical active surfaces. One of the key innovations of this study lies in the modulation of the electronic spin states and the redistribution of electronic states within the composite. DFT calculations, along with XPS, UV–Vis, PL, and EPR characterizations, demonstrated that the introduction of MXene and NiCo-LDH triggered significant changes in the local electronic structure of Ni and Co atoms. This led to a considerable narrowing of the bandgap from 4.00 eV (pristine NiCo2 O4 ) to 2.58 eV (NiCo2 O4 @MXene@LDH), which facilitated improved electrical conductivity and charge transfer kinetics across the heterointerface. The in situ Raman analysis reveals that the enhanced energy storage performance originates from the accelerated formation and increased exposure of NiCoOOH active species during electrochemical cycling. Electrochemical measurements further confirmed the remarkable performance of the as-prepared composite. The NiCo2 O4 @MXene@LDH electrode exhibited an ultrahigh specific capacitance of 5066 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , with excellent rate capability and long-term cycling stability (97.82 % retention after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 ). Moreover, the asymmetric supercapacitor device assembled with this composite delivered a superior energy density of 70.22 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 850.11 W kg−1 , outperforming many previously reported systems. This study not only demonstrates a successful pathway for optimizing transition metal oxide-based electrodes via electronic and interfacial engineering but also highlights the crucial role of spin state regulation and synergistic component design in improving electrochemical storage performance. The results suggest that the NiCo2 O4 @MXene@LDH composite holds significant promise for the development of high-performance, durable, and scalable supercapacitor devices. More broadly, the design principles and insights obtained herein can be extended to other functional materials and energy storage platforms. title: Polydopamine-bridged MXene/graphene composite aerogel for bifunctional applications in supercapacitors and piezoresistive sensors
authors: Yunfeng Wang, Zejiang Deng, Haiyun Ou, Shi Feng, Xu Xiang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this study, we successfully fabricated MXene@PDGA aerogels, significantly enhancing their electrochemical energy storage and sensing capabilities through a synergistic modification strategy. By utilizing PDA as a bridge, we successfully incorporated MXene into graphene aerogels, constructing a three-dimensional network composite structure with outstanding properties. This design approach not only strengthened the mechanical stability of the material but also introduced abundant functional groups, supplementing active adsorption sites and thereby achieving an overall improvement in material performance. In particular, the hydrophilic and strong adhesive properties of PDA not only prevented the curling and agglomeration of rGO and MXene nanosheets during the aerogel formation process but also enhanced the framework strength of the composite aerogel by bridging the two-dimensional nanosheets, thus providing a guarantee for its mechanical and electrochemical energy storage performance. Experimental results indicate that the MXene@PDGA-3 aerogel exhibits high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability in supercapacitors, while also demonstrating high sensitivity and rapid response characteristics in piezoresistive sensors. These superior performances validate the promising potential of MXene@PDGA aerogels in the fields of energy storage and sensing. The excellent energy storage performance of MXene@PDGA aerogels makes them ideal electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors, while their high sensitivity and rapid response characteristics render them competitive candidates in the field of flexible sensing.

title: Unleashing the potential of vanadium based MXenes for supercapacitors
authors: Onkar Jaywant Kewate, Jeng-Yu Lin, Sathyanarayanan Punniyakoti
conclusion: 6  Conclusion  In recent decades, supercapacitor have gained significant attraction owing to their excellent characteristics such as cycle stability, power density, rapid charge and discharge, low maintenance, and less sensitivity to high temperature. For the fabrication of high performance supercapacitor, the electrode materials found play a very vital role. Among various electrode materials, Vanadium based MXenes also represent a new and promising frontier in Supercapacitors due to their unique structural and electronic attributes, and break new ground in the energy storage sector. Their layered morphology, high conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, and redox-active vanadium centres yield supercapacitor with enhanced energy storage, and robust cyclic stability. These attributes also open up avenues for novel charge storage mechanisms, thereby positioning them as an interesting candidate for next-generation supercapacitors. This thorough review highlights the recent progress in the vanadium MXenes (V 2 CT  x  , V 2 NT  x  , and V 4 C 3 T  x  ) as electrode materials for supercapacitors. This article overview the ESS system, especially V-MXenes-based supercapacitors, V-MXenes properties and various synthesis approaches are discussed. Vanadium MXene composited with various materials proved to be a promising electrode material for supercapacitors as they have exceptional properties such as high electrical conductivity, hydrophilicity, thermal stability, increased surface area, and many more. These properties can be enhanced using the various composition of MAX phases and etching methods during its synthesis. In this article, various synthesis processes are mentioned like HF, MILD, electrochemcial, hydrothermal, and molten salts. From the above-mentioned synthesis routes, minimum F-based etching are widely utilized for the MXenes due to their effectiveness, and controlled terminations. Nevertheless, there are a requirement for F-free etching approaches to avoid potential hazards.  To improve performance, MXene-based heterojunction/heterostructures is employed in supercapacitors, hybrid capacitors, and micro-supercapacitors. Their unique characteristics like high conductivity, adjustable surface chemistry, and mechanical flexibility, render them suitable for next-generation energy storage technologies. Ongoing research and advancements in this field are anticipated to reveal even higher performance levels and wider applications in the future. Nevertheless, there is a requirement for extensive research on V-MXene and its composites/heterostructures/heterojunction for high performance storage devices. title: Multifunctional Co3O4/Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposites for integrated all solid-state asymmetric supercapacitors and energy-saving electrochemical systems of H2 production by urea and alcohols electrolysis
authors: Shidong Li, Jincheng Fan, Guocai Xiao, Shanqiang Gao, Kexin Cui, Zisheng Chao
conclusion: In summary, Co3 O4 /Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanocomposites have been prepared by vacuum filtration and hydrothermal-annealing methods and their structural and electrochemical performances were investigated, systematically, for energy storage and conversion. Co3 O4 nanomaterials (nanoparticles and nanorods) randomly distributed on the surfaces or between the layers of Ti3 C2 Tx . As the electrode materials for supercapacitors, Co3 O4 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites presented the outstanding specific capacitances and cyclic stability. Further, the constructed solid-state supercapacitor of S–NaOH-025//AC achieves an operating potential window of 1.4 V, a specific capacitance of 97.9 F g−1 at 0.25 A g−1 , an energy density of 95.9 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 630.4 W kg−1 , and excellent long-term durability. The ASCs can be easily connected into series or parallel for high voltage and current, demonstrating excellent electrochemical properties of energy storage for practical applications. Besides, Co3 O4 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites presented outstanding catalytic behaviors for H2 generation in various electrolytes and the introductions of urea or alcohols, replacing OER by the UOR and MOR, are the ideal energy-saving methods for H2 production from water. Remarkably, the electrolyzer with S–NaOH-05 in KOH + CH3 CH2 OH electrolyte required only 1.33 V potential to deliver the current density of 0.5 A g−1 . Especially, the electrolyzer with Co3 O4 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites as electrochemical electrode and powered Co3 O4 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites//AC ACS can be assembled electrochemical system in for H2 production. Therefore, this study not only shows enormous potential of Co3 O4 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites as a portable power supply, but also indicates its great opportunities in energy-saving H2 production in practical applications.

title: Bimetallic synergy in CoZnOHF/Ti3C2Tx MXene composites enables enhanced high-rate lithium-ion storage
authors: Yicen Liu, Zekun Wang, Bing Zhu, Yan-gai Liu, Xiaowen Wu
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, Ti₃C₂ MXene was obtained using LiF/HCl etching. Subsequently, a novel CoZnOHF/MXene composite electrode was constructed by directly growing needle-like CoZnOHF nanostructures onto the MXene surface via a simple one-step hydrothermal method. This unique structure delivers a high specific capacity of 1018 mAh g −1 at a specific current of 2 A g −1 and maintains stable cycling for 1000 cycles, demonstrating significantly superior electrochemical performance compared to single-metal composite electrodes. Electrochemical kinetic analysis reveals that the bimetallic synergy between Co and Zn significantly enhances Li + migration kinetics, contributing to excellent rate capability. Full-cell performance tests assembled with LFP further demonstrate the practical application value of the CoZnOHF/MXene electrode. The LFP||CoZnOHF/MXene full cell delivers a specific capacity of 105.67 mAh g −1 at 0.1C. Ex situ characterization techniques confirmed the reversible Li + intercalation/deintercalation behavior of the CoZnOHF/MXene electrode material during charging/discharging, as well as the built-in electric field effect formed between the Co/Zn bimetal, synergistically optimizing charge transfer efficiency.

title: Engineering MXene/nickel‑silver sulfide composites for high-performance hybrid supercapacitors: Synthesis and electrochemical insights
authors: Luxmi Rani, Jeong In Han
conclusion: In the present work, Ag2 S microcorals and NiAg2 S hexagonal microstructures were synthesized using hydrothermal method and characterized using various techniques. The bimetallic NiAg2 S electrode exhibited a higher specific capacitance of 837 F·g−1 from Ag2 S (383 F·g−1 ) at 1 A·g−1 . To enhance electrochemical performance of NiAg2 S and mitigate the restacking tendency of MXene sheets, MXene/NiAg2 S hybrid composite was engineered by incorporating a small amount of MXene into NiAg2 S. The resulting MXene/NiAg2 S hybrid electrode achieved higher specific capacitance of 1255 F·g−1 at 1 A·g−1 . Furthermore, a hybrid supercapacitor (HSC) device was assembled using MXene/NiAg2 S as +ve electrode and AC as -ve electrode, delivered a high energy density of 50.38 Wh·kg−1 at 775 W·kg−1 . title: In-situ electrochemical XRD and raman probing of ion transport dynamics in ionic liquid-etched Ti3C2Tx MXene for energy storage applications
authors: Jeremiah Hao Ran Huang, Shih-Wen Tseng, I-Wen Peter Chen
conclusion: In this study, in-situ Raman spectroscopy reveals that during the discharge process, Ti3 C2 (OH)2 gradually loses H+ ions, leading to the formation of Ti3 C2 O2 . Conversely, during charging, the reappearance of H+ ions gradually convert Ti3 C2 O2 back to Ti3 C2 (OH)2 . By analyzing these H+ interactions between MXene layers, we can infer the overall charge–discharge mechanism. For further validation, in-situ XRD was employed to monitor these structural changes in real time. However, due to the small size of H+ ions, direct observation was challenging, so we introduced TMA+ ions to simulate the process. During discharge, as Ti3 C2 O2 forms, we observe a shift of the MXene (002) plane to lower 2θ value, indicating expansion of the interlayer spacing like the cation release seen with H+ ions. This observation suggests that TMA+ ions intercalate in a similar manner to H+ ions, which enhances the activation of Ti3 C2 O2 sites and increases Ti3 C2 O2 formation. This mechanism aligns with previous findings, where the presence of oxygen functional groups on the MXene surface facilitates water molecule insertion, increasing the D-spacing of the MXene (002) plane. Together, these results support our proposed charge storage mechanism, highlighting the role of oxygen surface groups and interlayer spacing changes as key factors in MXene’s electrochemical behavior. In conclusion, this study successfully demonstrates the etching of Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase using TMATFB, resulting in the formation of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene with oxygen-containing functional groups. The characterization results from Raman spectroscopy, FTIR, and XPS consistently indicate the presence of these functional groups, which significantly enhance the specific capacitance of MXene. The electrochemical analyses reveal that the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene exhibits a high specific capacitance of 417.4F/g at a scan rate of 1 mV/s in 1 M H2 SO4 . In situ Raman observations confirm the reversible transportation of H+ ions, leading to the conversion between Ti3 C2 O2 and Ti3 C2 (OH)2 . In situ XRD measurements further validate the interlayer spacing changes due to cation intercalation. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene in high-performance energy storage systems and provide a foundation for further exploration of different etching mechanisms to optimize MXene properties for various applications. title: Synthesis and properties of 2D MXenes and their composite electrodes for supercapacitors
authors: Mengbin Li, Lizhong He
conclusion: 5  Conclusion and outlook  In summary, MXene is considered extremely promising for energy storage. Compared with carbon materials, conductive polymers, and conventional electrode materials, MXene has the advantages of high electrical conductivity, great specific surface area, and unique surface chemistry. Future investigation on MXene materials may focus on the effect of various precursor materials on the multiple performance, the design and construction of functionality MXenes, and synthesis approaches to optimize the bottom-up and top-down strategies by selectively etching the layered parent MAX precursors. Furthermore, the energy storage mechanism of the MXene-based composite electrodes is the main focus in the further because a deep understanding of the mechanism is prerequisite for design and construction of MXene-based electrode towards high performance supercapacitors. Also, some intrinsic properties such as chemical and thermal stability, and electronic properties is also the utmost importance to energy storage performance. Thus, the aim of this review is to present the intrinsic properties and fabrication methods of MXenes, as well as the latest achievements and progress in the MXene-based composite electrodes for supercapacitors.  Even though MXene was discovered by Yury's group in 2011 and several researchers have conducted extensive investigations in a variety of sectors throughout the past 13 years, certain shortcomings in synthesis and application still exist, which have an impact on the future development of MXene in commercialization: (1) MXene still needs to be further investigated in terms of antioxidant. Although cryogenic/inert gas modification and storage is the current approach to solve this problem, much efforts are still needed in this area; (2) As well all know, the energy storage performance of MXene is largely affected by the surface functional groups. In terms of surface functionalization, current investigations mainly focus on the random modification/regulation of the surface chemistries. Therefore, deep studies on the integration of specific functional groups in a controlled manner on the surface of MXene materials are important. (3) MXene has a certain advantage in weight capacitance because it belongs to two-dimensional materials, but there is a certain lack in volume-specific capacitance. Therefore, it is important to design special structures such as delamination or pleating to reduce the void space for a purpose of preventing capacitance loss. (4) Introducing defects into the MXene is an effective way to regulate its electrochemical performance, but the corresponding mechanism is unclear. Thus, it is necessary to delve into the defect-dominant mechanism for improving of electrochemical performance of MXene-based electrode. (5) MXene self-stacking is still a significant problem, which is closely related to the electrical capacity of the electrodes used in MXene-based supercapacitors. It is crucial to explore effective ways to add supports between MXene sheet layers to prepare the MXene-based composite electrode with hierarchical morphology to prevent nanosheets from self-stacking. Although MXene has advanced significantly in the field of supercapacitors just 13 years after its discovery, supercapacitors based on MXene are still in the beginning stage, and industrial production is also not realized. Nevertheless, as an emerging 2D material with many merits, we believe that MXene and its derivatives will shine in the field of energy storage.

title: Multi-electron redox asymmetric supercapacitors based on quinone-coupled viologen derivatives and Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: M. Boota, M. Rajesh, M. Bécuwe
conclusion: In summary, we have synthesized quinone-functionalized viologen molecules by simple mixing at room temperature for pseudocapacitive applications. When coated on rGO sheets and tested in a three-electrode setup, these hybrids exhibited distinct redox peaks and showed improved capacitance than their pristine counterpart under positive potentials. Optimized hybrids were paired with the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene as negative electrodes to manufacture all-pseudocapacitive asymmetric devices, which exhibited expanded voltage window of 1.5 V in 3 M H2 SO4 , high-rate electrochemical behavior (64 F/g (10 mV/s), 16 F/g (5000 mV/s)), good energy density (~20 Wh/kg), and capacitance retention of 80% after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles. We also found that the charge storage mechanism of single electrodes as well as asymmetric devices is predominantly capacitive at lowest tested scan rates where diffusion current dominates electrode performance. We stress that further performance of the electrodes can be achieved by designing electrode architectures, confining organic molecules within defined pores and by pairing optimized electrodes with other reported MXenes and conductive metal organic frameworks. title: Multiscale porous structured MXene: Synthesis, design and applications in batteries and supercapacitors
authors: Chen Chen, Xincao Tang, Mengjie Wang, Yanan Ma, Siliang Wang, Yang Yue
conclusion: Summary and outlook   Summary   Research advances in multiscale pore structures of 2D MXene provide important opportunities to regulate the diffusion behavior and chemical kinetics of active materials, thereby significantly advancing the development of energy storage devices. By scientifically designing and controlling pore parameters (such as pore size, pore orientation, shape and porosity), can effectively enhance the efficiency of ion/electron transport and promote the permeation of different electrolytes through various pores, thus optimizing the electrochemical performance of MXene. Particularly, the synergistic effects across multiple pore scales, the quantitative regulation of pore sizes from micropores, mesopores and macropores, and the precise control of pore geometries have been proven to be key strategies in achieving high-performance MXene electrode. Therefore, fully utilizing interdisciplinary knowledge in materials science, chemistry, and physics to precisely design and control pore parameters further advances the application of multiscale pore MXene, which will offer a more comprehensive solution to improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage devices.   Outlook   Multiscale porous MXene have demonstrated impressive performance in laboratory-scale energy storage applications, but still faces several unresolved issues. To bridge the gap between academic innovation and industrial translation, key scientific and engineering challenges must be addressed.   1.  Fluoride-dependent synthesis methods: Currently, large-scale fabrication of MXene still relies heavily on fluorinated etchants (e.g., HF, LiF/HCl), which raise environmental, safety, and cost issues, limiting industrial scalability.    2.  Lack of electrolyte-pore matching principles: How different pore sizes (and their hierarchical combinations) interact with various electrolytes, including differing in ionic size, solvation shell, or charge has not been systematically established, leading to deteriorated electrochemical performance.    3.  Unclear structure-performance relationship of multiscale pores: The optimal electrochemical performance and spatial distribution of micropores, mesopores, and macropores remain poorly understood, particularly regarding their integrated effect onion transport, mechanical integrity, and volumetric energy density.     To address these challenges, we make several recommendations:   1.  Green and scalable synthesis: Fluoride-free routes (e.g., molten salt etching [ 34 ] and electrochemical exfoliation) should be developed to enable safer, environmentally friendly, and industrially viable MXene production.    2.  Systematic electrolyte–pore compatibility studies: Future research should explore how pore size and hierarchy affect ion accessibility in electrolytes with different ionic radius, solvation shells, and charges. Understanding these interactions is crucial for tailoring MXene structures to diverse electrolyte systems and maximizing charge transport efficiency [ 339 ].    3.  Apply bio-inspired and data-driven design strategies ( Fig. 11  ): Principles derived from biological systems, such as Murray's Law and Fibonacci sequence-based distributions [ 340–342 ], can offer useful guidance for optimizing hierarchical pore design. In parallel, deep learning algorithms and data-driven models should be applied to predict ideal pore configurations and accelerate the design of high-performance MXene-based electrodes [ 343–347 ].

title: Self-standing porous MXene film via in situ formed microgel induced by 2- methylimidazole for high rate supercapacitor
authors: Sai Yan, Chenjing Shi, Zhen Tian, Dan Li, Yanjun Chen, Li Guo, Yanzhong Wang
conclusion: In summary, we purpose a new strategy to prepare the self-standing porous MXene film via the in-situ formation MXene microgel induced by 2-MeIM and vacuum filtration. The hydrogen ion released from the deprotonation of 2-MeIM and hydron bonding interaction between 2-MeIM and MXene nanosheets break the electrostatic balance of MXene nanosheets, resulting in the assembly of MXene nanosheets into 3D MXene microgel. The formed MXene microgel in MXene suspension not only reduces the time of vacuum filtration to prepare the porous M-MXene-5 film but also facilitates the electrolyte ions transport. Meanwhile, 2-methylimidazole acts as an intercalated agent to increase the layer spacing of MXene. As a result, the M-MXene film has an excellent rate performance, demonstrating the specific capacitance of 223.4 F g−1 even at a scan rate of 1000 mV s−1 . Moreover, the assembled M-MXene-5//AC ASC device displays 16.88 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 799 W kg−1 , and maintains 13.11 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 8 kW kg−1 . Meanwhile, the ASC device shows the exceptional cycling stability with the capacitance retention of 90.4 % after 10 000 cycles. This work opens a new way to prepare the porous MXene film with excellent electrochemical properties for high rate supercapacitors.

title: High-performance aqueous zinc-ion hybrid micro-supercapacitors enabled by surface-modified Ti3C2 MXene anode and polar organic molecule intercalated AlxV2O5 cathode
authors: Weifeng Liu, Jixuan Zhang, Jitao Li, Zhuang Ma, Lingling Sun, Yamin Feng, Long Zhang
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In this study, a high-performance, low-cost, and stable AZHMSCs (summarized in Table S3–S4 ) was engineered through rational material design and structural optimization. The key breakthrough of this study is the synergistic modification of anode and cathode materials to effectively address critical challenges such as sluggish ion kinetics, structural instability, and low energy density observed in conventional AZHMSCs. A deep alkali treatment was employed to synthesize the m-Ti 3 C 2 MXene anode material, wherein inactive –F functional groups were replaced with O-rich surface terminal functional groups. This modification not only alleviated the stacking effect of MXene layers but also enhanced the Zn 2+ adsorption capacity of the material, as confirmed by DFT calculations. The resulting 3D interconnected network generated rapid ion-diffusion paths, achieving a remarkable specific capacitance of 1231.8 mF cm −2 at 1.0 mA cm −2 and excellent rate performance. Further, Al  x  V 2 O 5 -NMP used as the cathode material to stabilize the layered structure and accelerate Zn 2+ migration. The strong electrostatic interaction between NMP and pre-intercalated Al 3+ minimized structural collapse of the cathode during cycling, and its weak binding with Zn 2+ ensured efficient ion mobility. The cathode exhibited a high specific capacity of 327.78 μAh cm −2 at 0.5 mA cm −2 and retained its structural integrity for 5000 cycles. By integrating the optimized m-Ti 3 C 2 MXene anode and Al  x  V 2 O 5 -NMP cathode, the assembled AZHMSCs exhibited exceptional performance: an energy density of 105.15 μWh cm −2 at 0.475 mW cm −2 , power density of 9.5 mW cm −2 at 39.53 μWh cm −2 , and 89.29 % capacity retention after 3000 cycles. In addition, the device demonstrated excellent mechanical flexibility, maintaining 93.27 % of its capacity under 90° bending, showing its potential for wearable electronics. This study highlights the significance of optimizing material properties and their synergies in enhancing Zn 2+ storage, and outlines a pathway for developing advanced micro-energy storage devices, with future work aiming to scale up production and explore hybrid designs for widespread use in portable and flexible electronics (summarized in Table S5 ).

title: Advancements and approaches in developing MXene-based hybrid composites for improved supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Thibeorchews Prasankumar, Kaaviah Manoharan, N.K. Farhana, Shahid Bashir,  K. Ramesh, S. Ramesh, Vigna K. Ramachandaramurthy
conclusion: 8  Conclusion  This review examines supercapacitors in detail, including their specifications, applications, development of electrode materials, and principles of operation. It was briefly mentioned how supercapacitors are categorized based on their mechanisms. The review centers on the most recent advancements in MXenes and supercapacitor research. MXenes of various kinds are synthesized and their combinations are investigated. The most thoroughly studied material is Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene, and research is currently underway. Several synthesis techniques used during the MAX phase are briefly reviewed in the current review. There are many different etching procedures available for creating MXenes, including F-free, fluoride-based, and HF acid etching. It is crucial to remember that the range of unique morphologies and adjustable surfaces could be primarily attributed to the etching circumstances. It was discovered that combining MXenes with other materials, like carbon, polymers, transition metal oxides, and MOF, for the supercapacitor electrode material improved both the electrochemical and overall mechanical performance. Non-etheless, it is frequently noted that MXene/transition metal oxide composites have poor mechanical characteristics. As a result, we hope that our analysis will help researchers identify suitable MXene and activated carbon composite energy storage systems to help them overcome obstacles. Furthermore, the summary offered in this review will help future investigators to carry out their research on MXene dispersal and denudation techniques in order to produce MXene hybrids with enhanced electrochemical performance.

title: Enhanced charge storage using in-situ grown NiGa-layered double hydroxide on V4C3Tx MXene for supercapacitor applications
authors: Dana Susan Abraham, Mari Vinoba, Margandan Bhagiyalakshmi
conclusion: In summary, NiGa-LDH was in situ grown on the surface of delaminated V4 C3 Tx MXene nanosheets via a facile hydrothermal procedure leveraging the electrostatic interactions between LDH and MXene. Various ratios of nickel and gallium were explored to optimize capacity performance, resulting in the Ni-Ga (1:1) LDH/V4 C3 Tx MXene (NGV-11) nanocomposite demonstrating a notable increase in specific capacity to 268.85 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1 . This enhanced capacity can be attributed to the synergistic interaction between NiGa-LDH and V4 C3 Tx MXene, where the abundant active sites of NiGa-LDH are complemented by the superior electrical conductivity and structural stability of V4 C3 Tx MXene. NGV-11//AC supercapacitor device attained a remarkable energy density of 56.41 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 800 W kg−1 , an impressive cycling stability with 93.24 % capacitance retention, and a coulombic efficiency of 96.96 % after 5000 cycles. Thus, the integration of NiGa-LDH with V4 C3 Tx MXene addresses common challenges in LDH-based materials, such as low conductivity and limited cycling stability, positioning the NGV-11 nanocomposite as a competitive candidate for next-generation energy storage systems. Hence, the study shows that NiGa-LDH/V4 C3 Tx MXene nanocomposite confers notable prospects as electrode material in the field of energy storage applications. Moreover, this study lays a strong foundation for advancing vanadium-based MXene-LDH hybrids in future energy storage research. title: Fungus-modified wood anchor MXene constructs high-performance wood-based carbon electrodes for supercapacitor
authors: Shengzhang Deng, Jian Zhang, Lin Lin, Ziqi Li, Qingping Wang, Peng Li
conclusion: In this study, a self-supporting wood-derived carbon electrode has successfully been engineered with high energy density through a combination of fungus (Phanerochaete chrysosporium) treatment, low concentration KOH solution treatment and MXene anchoring. Fungi and KOH solution treatment induce the formation of layered porous structures in wood and generate many oxygen-containing functional groups, thereby improving the self-stacking problem of MXene in wood-derived carbon. Simultaneously, the integration of MXene into the wood-derived carbon enhanced its electrical conductivity, surface wettability, ion accessibility and provided abundant active sites. With a current density of 1 mA cm−2 , the ACW2 @WR-M3 has a capacitance of 10.5 F cm−2 (232.8 F g−1 ) and a retention of almost 97 % at 50 mA cm−2 after 10,000 cycles. Symmetric supercapacitor with two identical ACW2 @WR-M3 electrodes has high energy density (0.705 mWh cm−2 /3.53 mWh cm−3 ) and power density (54200 mW cm−2 /271000 mW cm−3 ). This work proposes a novel technique for increasing the electrochemical performance of wood-derived carbon electrodes, emphasizing their potential for high-performance supercapacitor applications. title: Sandwich-like MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9S8 with rich pores and high charge transfer capability for boosted supercapacitor capability
authors: Ye Qu, Yanzi Zhang, Yali Zhang, Jun Song, Zhaoen Liu, Weixing Rao, Yu Liu
conclusion: In summary, this work successfully synthesized the sandwich structure MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 ternary nanocomposite. The high capacity of NiCo-LDH and Co9 S8 , and the exceptional electrical conductivity of MXene make the MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 composite a potential electrode material for a high-performance battery-type supercapacitor. The obtained hybrid structure generates a large number of channels, promoting the rapid transfer of ions and electrons, significantly improves electrochemical efficiency through synergistic effects. The obtained MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 composites showed a high specific capacity of 808.0 F g−1 . In addition, the assembled device (MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 //AC) achieved a superior energy density of 96.4 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1 . Therefore, it can be concluded from the results that combining battery type and double-layer capacitive electrode materials to form a heterojunction is an excellent strategy for enhancing electrochemical performance. title: Exploring the potential of MXene-based aerogels and hybrid nanocomposites for supercapacitor applications
authors: Suresh Sagadevan, Is Fatimah, J. Anita Lett, Babak Kakavandi, Tetsuo Soga, Won-Chun Oh, Hyacinthe Randriamahazaka
conclusion: The growing demand for energy storage with enhanced performance has driven the research toward innovative supercapacitor electrode materials. MXene aerogels, with their unique combination of properties, emerge as a promising candidate to address limitations that are faced by conventional electrodes. This review highlights the potential of MXene aerogels in supercapacitors, emphasizing their key advantages. Their strong and good conductivity, large surface area, and inherent MXene properties lead to remarkable capacitance values, enabling the efficient energy storage. Furthermore, MXene aerogels exhibit excellent cycling stability, demonstrating minimal performance degradation during extended charge-discharge cycles. This translates to long-lasting supercapacitors with reliable energy storage capabilities. The porous aerogel structure facilitates fast ion diffusion within the electrode, leading to fast charging and discharging rates thereby influencing the MXene aerogels suitable for the applications which are demanding high-power energy systems. Future research focused on optimizing fabrication methods and exploring composite structures with other conductive materials holds immense promise for delivering the full potential of MXene aerogels in the next-generation supercapacitors. This material has the advantage like cost-effective, high-capacity energy storage devices, which are beneficial for both industries and individuals. By enabling more efficient energy storage, MXene aerogels can revolutionize various productions. As research progresses, this technology development will play a major role in the viable and ecologically approachable for energy storage supercapacitor applications.
