title: Electrostatic self-assembly assisted construction of MXene/MoO3 hybrid aerogel for free-standing supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Feitian Ran, Bowen Tan, Meijie Hu, Shulin Deng, Kai Wang, Wanjun Sun, Jifei Liu, Xiaobin Yang
conclusion: In summary, MXene/MoO3 hybrid aerogels were synthesized through electrostatic self-assembly and freeze-drying techniques. The incorporation of Ti3 C2 Tx establishes an efficient conductive network within MoO3 , significantly enhancing its intrinsic conductivity and facilitating rapid electron transport. Additionally, MoO3 nanobelts mitigate the restacking of Ti3 C2 Tx layers, thereby exposing more active sites for electrochemical reactions and resulting in a superior synergistic effect. The hybrid aerogels exhibit a larger pore size, providing accelerated ion diffusion pathways and improving electrochemical reaction kinetics. First-principles calculations reveal a marked enhancement in H+ adsorption and conductivity within the MXene/MoO3 hybrid aerogel. Consequently, the TM-50 hybrid aerogel achieves a specific capacity of 418.2 C g−1 at 1 A g−1 and maintains 92.3% of its capacity after 10000 cycles at 3 A g−1 . Furthermore, the assembled TM-50//AC asymmetric supercapacitors deliver an energy density of 20.9 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 491.5 W kg−1 This simple and controllable strategy for developing hybrid aerogels can be extended to other MXene-based functional materials. title: From 2D to 3D: Green synthesis of wrinkled MXene thin-film electrodes for ultra-high specific capacitance and structural resilience combination of supercapacitors
authors: Lanyun Di, Xuehua Yan, Chu Chu, Feng Zhang, Jamile Mohammadi Moradian, Zohreh Shahnavaz
conclusion: 2D MXene nanosheets are prone to self-stacking, which significantly hinders their application in supercapacitors. This study investigated a new path to synthesize a novel 3D porous MXene thin-film electrode. By leveraging the high-temperature pyrolysis of NaHCO3 , an annealing process was used to develop a 3D cavity structure and modify the surface end groups, reducing the harmful -F end groups. Additionally, the gas generated by the pyrolysis of NaHCO3 was used for in situ bubbling, inducing micron-scale 3D cavities combined with the remaining pores of CMC carbonization. This approach addresses the issue of self-stacking in 2D MXene nanosheets, which has hindered their application in supercapacitors. The abundant water molecule channels effectively accelerate the insertion and extraction of electrolyte ions. In addition, carbonized CMC improves the conductivity of the composite film and provides an additional double electric-layer contribution. Similarly, it acts as an interlayer spacer to inhibit the self-stacking of MXene nanosheets. Thanks to its favorable 3D structural design, the synthesized film electrode exhibits a mass-specific capacitance of up to 565 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , and the area-specific capacitance reaches 1582 mF cm−2 . After high-temperature annealing, the film still showed surprising mechanical flexibility, with a tensile strength of up to 34.2 MPa. When used as the positive and negative electrodes to assemble a symmetrical supercapacitor, at 1 A g−1 , the mass-specific capacitance could reach 71.25 F g−1 . Even under a power density of 400 W kg−1 , the energy density remained at 6.3 Wh kg−1 . The device also exhibited extremely high cycle stability, maintaining a capacity retention rate of 99.6 % after 20000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . This remarkable electrochemical performance opens up a novel avenue for the advancement of porous electrodes and high-efficiency flexible energy storage devices utilizing 2D nanomaterials. title: High-performance asymmetric supercapacitors based on 2D MXene/NiCoP hybrid and ZIF derived porous nanocarbon
authors: Erdenebayar Baasanjav, K.A. Sree Raj, Hafis Hakkeem, Chandra Sekhar Rout, Sang Mun Jeong
conclusion: In summary, a 2D MXene-based NiCoP hybrid structure was successfully synthesized via a cost-effective hydrothermal reaction and phosphorization process. The designed and well-developed 2D MXene/NCP composite exhibits large porous active sites, abundant redox-active sites and exceptional electrical conductivity, which collectively promote enhanced Faradaic redox reactions, efficient electrolyte diffusion, and fast electron transport. The synergistic interaction between the MXene sheets and NCP nanorods leads to remarkable electrochemical performance, achieving a high specific capacitance of 1754.0 F g−1 at 3 mA cm−2 , along with good rate capability and higher stability, with minimal loss in activity after 5000 charge/discharge cycles. Additionally, a hybrid ASC device constructed using MX-3/NCP as the positive electrode and PNC as the negative electrode, delivered a high specific energy of 54.3 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 565.6 W kg−1 and maintained 32.6 Wh kg−1 at a high-power density of 6270 W kg−1 . The device also demonstrated exceptional cyclic stability by retaining 93.8 % of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles and excellent adaptability in practical applications. Moreover, TMP/MXene composites can be promising electrodes for the development of hybrid supercapacitor technologies. title: Synergistically coupling of ternary hydrotalcite and Ti3C2Tx-MXene nanosheets boosting electronic transmission in energy storage
authors: Lu Luo, Qiuyan Kong, Qianqian Zhang, Jing Zhang, Mizi Fan, Weigang Zhao
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, the LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T x nanohybrids with intriguing “lace-like” structure were successfully developed via synergistically coupling Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene with ternary hydrotalcite (NiCoMn-LDH). The disordered crisscross arrangement of the NiCoMn-LDH arrays have enabled a high porosity and abundant active sites. Coupled with Ti 3 C 2 T x serving as an electronic transmission bridge, the LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T x nanohybrid exhibits outstanding electrical conductivity, showcasing a remarkable specific capacitance of 1102.9 F g −1 and demonstrating a rate capability of 66.87 % at 20 A g −1 . Further assembly of the LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T x -2//AC hybrid supercapacitor (HSC) yields a maximum energy density of 47.3 Wh kg −1 (at 800 W kg −1 ), maintaining a considerable energy density of 35.7 Wh kg −1 even at 8000 W kg −1 . Moreover, the HSC device demonstrates distinguished durability (91.7 %) and Coulombic efficiency (99 %) after 5000 cycles. This work highlights the rational combination of 2D Ti 3 C 2 T x with highly active transition metal compounds, showcasing their synergistic effects in enhancing the performance of nanohybrids. This presents thrilling possibilities for the design of devices for electrochemical energy harvesting and storage.

title: Enhanced electron conductivity, stability, and electrochemical performance of MXene-coated manganese and iron oxides as negative electrode of supercapacitors
authors: Moo Young Jung, Yongsuk Oh, Subin Eom, Jihye Park, Chanyong Lee, Sudeshana Pandey, Taemin Kim, Hae-Seok Lee, Ji-Won Son, Yong Ju Yun, Yongseok Jun
conclusion: In this study, a novel MXene/MnO2 /Fe2 O3 composite was developed and optimized as a negative electrode material for supercapacitors. The MXMFO-1.0 exhibited the best performance, achieving a high charging and discharging specific capacity of 1226.30 and 595.74 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 and retaining 78 % of its discharging capacity after 4000 cycles at 4 A g–1 . An asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) using this composite as the negative electrode demonstrated an energy density and power density of 61.70 Wh kg–1 at 426.21 W kg–1 and 17.88 Wh kg–1 at 2824.63 W kg–1 and excellent cycling stability, retaining 92.92 % of its initial capacitance after 25,000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1 . These findings highlight the potential of MXene/MnO2 /Fe2 O3 composites for high-performance supercapacitors, particularly in energy storage applications such as electric vehicles and grid systems. title: A novel MnO2/Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposite as high performance electrode materials for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Hanmei Jiang, Zegao Wang, Qian Yang, Muhammad Hanif, Zhiming Wang, Lichun Dong, Mingdong Dong
conclusion: In summary, we have developed a novel MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite for flexible supercapacitor, which is synthesized by synergistically coupling one-dimensional (1D) MnO2 nanoneedles with two-dimensional (2D) Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheet. In the as-prepared materials, MnO2 nanoneedles, growing along the (001) direction, are anchored on Ti3 C2 Tx sheets with diameters of around 10–20 nm and length of around 200–300 nm. XPS characterization demonstrated the chemical interaction between Ti3 C2 Tx and MnO2 in the composites, which can improve the electrochemical performance of the MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite material by promoting the electron transfer between MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx . The synergistic effect between MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx is significantly affected by the MnO2 content, the 1 MT sample with the mass ratio between MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx = 1 exhibits the best electrochemical performance due to the maximizing electron transfer and ion diffusion. The flexible supercapacitor device fabricated by using the 1 MT nanocomposites as electrode materials can be freely bended and exhibits excellent capacitive behavior. The energy density of the device can reach 0.7 μWh cm−2 at the power density of 80.0 μW cm−2 , which is better than many of the reported MnO2 -based and carbon–basted flexible supercapacitor device. Moreover, the MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite flexible supercapacitor shows superior electrochemical stability (more than 100% capacitance retention after 1000 cycles at 0.2 mA cm−2 ). On the basis of these features, the good electrochemical behavior of the MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites makes it a promising electrode material for flexible supercapacitor. However, to close the theoretical specific capacitance of MnO2 , further optimizing the structure of this flexible supercapacitor device with higher capacitance and energy density are desired. Furthermore, this work provides a general route for preparing MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites and sheds light on the exploitation of MnO2 -based materials for advanced flexible energy storage devices. title: Simultaneously addressing self-stacking and oxidative degradation issues of Ti3C2Tx MXene through biothermochemistry induced 3D crosslinking
authors: Haitao Zhang, Hanyu He, Yongxiang Huang, Shi Pu, Yanting Xie, Junfeng Huang, Xinling Jiang, Yongbin Wang, Shenglong Wang, Hongzhi Peng, Yuanxiao Qu, Weiqing Yang
conclusion: In conclusion, a variety of Ti3 C2 Tx with 3D crosslinking structure are constructed by a novel biothermochemistry method, in which bioagents are combined with Ti3 C2 Tx through electrostatic and/or the formation of Ti-N and S-S chemical bonds. On the one hand, 3D crosslinking effect expands the interlayer spacing and reduces self-stacking issue; On the other hand, bioagents reduce the number of exposed Ti atoms and effectively prevent the oxidation of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Impressively, 3D-MX exhibits extraordinary antioxidant capacity as revealed by extremely-long on-shelf stability up to 550 days. In practical, as used as an electrode material for supercapacitors, 3D-MX-G exhibits high specific capacitance and excellent stability. This work solves the problems of self-stacking and oxidative degradation of Ti3 C2 Tx and provides an excellent solution for exploring the further application and long-term preservation of Ti3 C2 Tx .

title: Biomimetic and electrostatic self-assembled nanocellulose/MXene films constructed with sequential bridging strategy for flexible supercapacitor
authors: Shaowei Wang, Yuanyuan Ma, Sailing Zhu, Haoyu Ma, Yiying Yue, Qinglin Wu, Huining Xiao, Jingquan Han
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, biomimetic and hierarchical flexible CM-Al composite films with distinguished mechanical toughness, electrical conductivity and electrochemical energy storage capabilities were developed via the facile electrostatic self-assembly and vacuum filtration processes. The introduced CNFs enriched with hydroxyl and carboxyl groups served as an intercalation layer to connect the adjacent MXene nanosheets through hydrogen bonding interactions, which not only imparted the enhanced mechanical strength and flexibility to the composite film through constructing a “soft-hard” biomimetic microstructure, but also effectively suppressed the undesirable self-stacking of the MXene nanosheets, allowing the exposure of more active sites on MXene surface. The positively charged Al 3+ induced the self-assembly of the negatively charged CNFs and MXene via electrostatic attraction, resulting in the establishment of ionic bonds with oxygen-containing functional groups via charge transfer. The strong and rigid ionic bonds interlocked the adjacent CNFs and MXene, facilitating a denser internal structure and enhanced mechanical toughness of CM-Al. Furthermore, additional electron transport pathways acted by ionic bonds boosted the fast electron transfer, improving the electroconductivity of the composite films. Benefiting from the biomimetic structure with sequentially bridged hydrogen and ionic bonds, the robust and flexible CM-Al displayed optimal mechanical properties (tensile strength of 163.88 MPa, Young ' s modulus of 2.18 GPa and toughness of 8.64 MJ m −3 ), electrical conductivity (82.63 S cm −1 ) and extraordinary capacitive capability (762 mF cm −2 ), proving a remarkable dominance in electrochemical energy storage. The assembled symmetric quasi-solid-state supercapacitor with CM-Al as electrode material integrated the superior areal capacitance (679 mF cm −2 at 0.8 mA cm −2 current density), cycling stability (85.3 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles) and high energy density (16.2 μWh cm −2 ). Additionally, the basically constant electrochemical performance of the flexible supercapacitor was detected even after experiencing repeated non-stretching deformations due to the stable internal structure of CM-Al, indicating the noteworthy reliability in practical applications. This work delivered a simple and feasible strategy for the fabrication of flexible composite films combined with impressive mechanical toughness, electrical conductivity and brilliant electrochemical energy storage, facilitating the development of MXene-based flexible electronics in high-performance wearable energy storage devices.

title: Nanoengineering of novel MXene (Ti3C2Tx) based MgCr2O4 nanocomposite with detailed synthesis, morphology and characterization for enhanced energy storage application
authors: Rubia Shafique, Malika Rani, Kiran Batool, Aqeel Ahmad Shah, Aboud Ahmed Awadh Bahajjaj, Mika Sillanpää, Hessa A. Alsalmah, Naveed Kausar Janjua, Maryam Arshad
conclusion: that MXene/MgCr2 O4 based electrode materials is most suitable for energy storage applications such as supercapacitors. 4 Conclusion A novel nanocomposite combining MXene and magnesiochromite has been investigated in the realm of energy storage particularly as electrode material for supercapacitors. The X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis distinctly reveals the characteristic peaks corresponding to both MXene and MgCr2 O4 phases within the nanocomposite spectrum. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) micrographs exhibit the attachment of magnesiochromite particles onto MXene nanosheets. Raman and photoluminescence spectra provide insights into the presence of functional groups and enhanced electron-hole recombination, resulting in a bandgap of 1.8 eV as determined from UV spectra. The Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra exhibit prominent peaks corresponding to C-F, C–H, and MgCr2 O4 at wavenumbers of 940 cm−1 , 2880 cm−1 and 505 cm−1 respectively. Notably, a tailored increase in electrostatic repulsion has been achieved for the colloidal solution, as evidenced by the measured Zeta potential of −19.9 mV. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) spectra demonstrate the remarkable electron transfer rate constants of 4.097 × 10−9 (S/cm) in 1 M KOH and 2.66 × 10−9 (S/cm) in 0.1 M H2 SO4 underlining the material efficient charge transport properties. Notably in 1 M KOH electrolyte solution at 20 mV/s, a maximum capacitance value of 542.6F/g is achieved. Maximum power density increases from 104.99 to 271.2 kW/kg while energy density value reduces from 37.68 to 14.58 kWh/kg emphasizing the potential utility of this nanocomposite as an energy storage material particularly in the context of supercapacitor applications.

title: Binder-free Ti3C2Tx MXene electrode film for supercapacitor produced by electrophoretic deposition method
authors: Shuaikai Xu, Guodong Wei, Junzhi Li, Yuan Ji, Nickolai Klyui, Vladimir Izotov, Wei Han
conclusion: In summary, a general, simple MEPD strategy has been developed for preparing binder-free Ti3 C2 Tx -based supercapacitor electrodes with excellent electrochemical performances. The key novelty in this study is the use of a facile, time-saving method to produce layered self-assembled binder-free Ti3 C2 Tx films with adjustable mass loading and reduced agglomeration on different conductive substrates at room temperature by using organic colloidal solution containing well-dispersed few-layer d-Ti3 C2 Tx nanoflakes. The MEPD method facilitates the formation of a layered and interconnected self-assembled framework with a broad pore size distribution and reduced agglomeration, ensuring the high electrical conductivity and improved accessibility of electrolyte to the electrode. The film electrodes demonstrated good rate performance and long cyclic life with capacity retention close to 100% after 10,000 cycles. Moreover, the proposed MEPD as a universal method could also open a door to design high performance MXene-based supercapacitor by using arbitrary conductive substrates, especially for manufacturing flexible or micro supercapacitor with complex shapes and greatly promoting the practical applications of Ti3 C2 Tx -based supercapacitor devices in the future. title: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis of Ti3C2Tx MXene: A sustainable and scalable approach using alkaline etchant
authors: Farah Ezzah Ab Latif, Mohammad Khalid, Arshid Numan, Norhuda Abdul Manaf, Nabisab Mujawar Mubarak, Haizum Aimi Zaharin, Ezzat Chan Abdullah
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  This study successfully demonstrates the synthesis of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene from the Ti 3 AlC 2 MAX phase using NaOH as the etching agent, with concentrations ranging from 5 to 30 M, through a microwave-assisted hydrothermal heating method. XRD analysis reveals slight shifts and a reduction in peak intensity at the (002) and (104) panes, suggesting effective structural modification caused by etching. The results confirm the successful alteration of the MXene structure. FTIR analysis highlights Ti-O, C=O, C-H, and O-H functional groups on the etched MXene surface, suggesting elemental substitution and introducing various functional groups. The findings align with the previously reported MXene compositions, demonstrating effective surface modification. Raman analysis confirms the formation of new bonds, such as Ti-C and Ti-O/Ti-OH, providing further evidence of Al removal from the precursor and validating the efficacy of the NaOH etching process through microwave-assisted hydrothermal heating.  FESEM analysis reveals the etched MXene's surface morphology, showing carved patterns and layered structures with increased interlayer spacing, especially at higher NaOH concentrations (27.5 and 30 M). Elemental analysis using FESEM-EDS demonstrates significant Al removal, with the remaining Al content as low as 2.19% and 0.46% for the 27.5 M and 30 M etched MXene, respectively. The combination of XRD and FESEM-EDS characterisation provides a comprehensive understanding of surface termination, elucidating the elemental composition and distribution. Furthermore, UV-Vis spectroscopy analysis using Tauc's plot reveals that the band gap energy changes after etching, likely due to surface functionalisation. Interestingly, the magnetic properties of etched MXene at lower NaOH concentrations (10 M and below) transition to semiconducting behaviour at higher concentrations (20 M and above), showcasing the material's electronic versatility and potential for various applications. Notably, Ti 3 C 2 T x etched MXene synthesised at 27.5 M NaOH concentration is a promising candidate for future MXene synthesis studies to optimise etching conditions. While this study has successfully reduced Al content and formed narrow interlayer spacing, future work should focus on refining etchant concentrations to maximise the etching process. In conclusion, this work demonstrates a fluorine-free, efficient NaOH etching approach for synthesising Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene, leveraging microwave-assisted hydrothermal processing to drastically reduce etching time to 45 min. The resulting etched MXene exhibits a unique, multilayered structure, modified surface features, and versatility in electronic properties, promoting its potential in a wide range of applications.

title: The Rise of Ti3C2Tx MXene synthesis strategies over the decades: A review
authors: Mohammed Askkar Deen, Harish Kumar Rajendran, Ragavan Chandrasekar, Debanjana Ghosh, Selvaraju Narayanasamy
conclusion: 6  Conclusion  Ti 3 C 2 T x has emerged as a robust 2D nanomaterial ascribed to its properties such as tunable conductivity, abundant surface functional groups, hydrophilicity, structural variations and mechanical pliability. However, there are challenges associated with Ti 3 C 2 T x in utilizing it effectively. One major obstacle is the need for safe and cost-effective synthesis techniques that can yield high quantities of Ti 3 C 2 T x . Although the chemical vapour deposition (CVD) method is considered safe and controllable, it is not explored for synthesizing Ti 3 C 2 T x . Currently, the only fabrication method available is wet chemical etching. An environmentally friendly process like molten salt substitution and halogen etching exist; nevertheless, etching based on HF and HCl-LiF is still the most sought-after approach because of their ease of synthesis. However, these approaches require hazardous etchants or harsher synthetic conditions to etch out the Al layers in Ti 3 C 2 T x successfully. For instance, HF etching allows synthesis at room temperature, while molten salts require a higher temperature of 700 ° C for successful synthesis. This demonstrates the demand to generate economically viable and efficient methods for etching and producing a large quantity of Ti 3 C 2 T x . Furthermore, complete control over the synthesis process of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene hasn't been achieved. It remains challenging to synthesis Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets with specific sizes, defects and surface terminations with desired spatial distribution. Being a material of active research interest, the list of synthesis routes of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene will get some add ons whereby there is a good scope on green solvent based Al etching and etching methods that require minimal energy to be developed in near future. In addition, facile exfoliation protocols must be developed to produce multi-layered Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene into single or fewer layers without any defects, resulting in a perfect crystal structure. This development will unveil detailed insights into the electronic, magnetic, mechanical, and photic properties of MXene. These insights help understand the interface properties between Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets and other substances, including surface functional groups, gas molecules, water molecules, and hybrid phases, through experimental and theoretical analyses (both in situ and ex-situ observations). Furthermore, a greater focus on the stability of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene in the form of nanosheets is needed, specifically in humid environments with oxygen and at high temperatures. The irreversible oxidation of MXenes is a significant obstacle that hinders their practical applications. The feasible ways to prevent this permanent degradation of MXenes must be unveiled to utilize their potential in practical applications fully. The preservation of Ti 3 C 2 T x 's properties over time remains challenging despite attempts to enhance its oxidation stability with antioxidizing agents. While this treatment improves stability, it does not entirely prevent oxidation. As a result, a method to improve the long-term storage of Ti 3 C 2 T x while keeping its properties intact is still elusive. Despite the challenges mentioned above, state-of-the-art research demonstrates that these challenges are expected to progress significantly soon. There is no doubt that Ti 3 C 2 T x  MXene has guaranteed the era of the next generation of 2D nanomaterials.  Some of the crucial state of the art challenges in Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene synthesis includes oxidation stability, environmental friendly synthesis procedure and scalability. The conversion of Ti in Ti 3 C 2 T x to TiO 2 is accelerated by the presence of dissolved oxygen during the etching process. Hence in many MXene synthetsis laboratory, the synthesis is accompanied by Argon purging or the etching is carried out in an inert atmosphere. One strategy used to reduce the dissolved oxygen levels in liquid is coating the liquid holding container with polymeric composites, which scavenges the oxygen present in liquid and reduced the oxygen level. This kind of polymer coatings are used in packagings that prevent the oxidation of food items [142] . Block copolymer made up of 1,6-hexanediol/tetrahydrophthalic anhydride polyester and polycaprolactone was found to scavenge 382 cc/m 2 oxygen [143] . Most of the etching protocol involves usage of direct HF or in situ generation of HF by reaction between metal fluorides and HCl and this demands the usage of polymeric containers rather than the glass material. Plastic containers made up of the above mentioned polymer or the inner walls coated using those polymers help to scavenge oxygen from the etching solution. Stability and purity of the MAX phase is anothern concern towards MXene synthesis. The purity of the MAX phase for etching process is not uniform and varies with suppliers and hence demands a reliable, simple synthesis protocol for high quanitity production, ensuring purity and minimal batch variations. The stability of MAX phase before it meets its end application is also a concern of discussion. The roughness of the surface and grain boundary diffusion of oxygen in MAX phase are to blame which compromises the stability of MAX phases. This was explained by Julian in terms of breakaway oxidation of Ti 2 AlC [144] . In MXene synthesizing laboratories, storage of MAX phase is carried out in glove boxes which is not offordable in many laboratories. In such cases researches can use anaerobic gas jars like GasPak jars to maintain oxygen free contidions while storing the MAX phases and the similar principle can be used for synthesizing and transportation of MAX phases. Few researchers have tried the strategy of increasing the concentration of aluminium during MAX phase synthesis, for example Roslyk et al. increased the molar ratio of Al 1.1 times to that of TiC, resulting in MAX phase of commendable stability against oxygen [145] . Also it has been found that utilization of Ti sponge for MAX synthesis could produce porous MAX phases helping in reducing the addition work for making MAX phase powders. These kind of strategies can be incorporated in large scale manufacturing of MAX phases which reduces the cost and also improves the stability of the material. Despite the challenges mentioned above, state-of-the-art research demonstrates that these challenges are expected to progress significantly soon. There is no doubt that Ti 3 C 2 T x  MXene has guaranteed the era of the next generation of 2D nanomaterials and synthesis of different nanohybrids of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene for various applications will takes place.

title: Nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) pillared Ta4C3Tx MXene as high-performance electrochemical supercapacitors
authors: Sabeen Fatima, M. Waqas Hakim, Xiaoxiao Zheng, Yu Sun, Ziheng Li, Nan Han, Muyang Li, Zeyuan Wang, Lei Han, Liang Wang, Safia Khan, Jiangwei Liu, Hu Li
conclusion: In this study, we have prepared Ta4 C3 Tx MXene and nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) using easy and cost-effective synthesis routes. Ta4 C3 Tx MXene sheets were surface engineered via NGQD by adopting a solvothermal synthesis approach. Various NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets were created by carefully regulating the surface engineering of Ta4 C3 Tx sheets with NGQD varying concentrations from 1.5% to 10%. For the assessment of working materials quality, shape, crystallinity, chemical structure, and elemental content, different supporting characterizations such as UV–vis, PL, Raman, XRD, TEM, FTIR, SEM and XPS were also performed. The effective synthesis and excellent quality of every material were explained by these characterizations. To test the charge storage capabilities NGQD, Ta4 C3 Tx , 1.5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx , 3%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx , 5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx , 7%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx, and 10%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets were employed as working electrodes in 1 M KOH electrolyte. With the attachment of nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots the charge storage of Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets was not only enhanced up to sevenfold but also displayed excellent stability for 20k repeated cycles. The performance evaluation of 5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx //AC capacitor device demonstrated charge storage characteristics in between pseudocapacitance and battery-like properties, along with long-term stability. Also, the increased specific capacity, power, and energy density of the device make 5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx a superior candidate for energy storage device applications. All things considered, this work offers guidance on how to modify dense MXene phases, such as tantalum carbide, to improve their electrochemical device performances relative to their plain forms. title: Oxygen vacancy enriched Na+ intercalated MnO2 for high-performance MXene (Ti3C2Tx)-based flexible supercapacitor and electrocatalysis
authors: B. Thanigai Vetrikarasan, Abhijith R. Nair, Surendra K. Shinde, Dae-Young Kim, Ji Man Kim, Ravindra N. Bulakhe, Shilpa N. Sawant, Ajay D. Jagadale

title: In situ oxygen doped Ti3C2Tx MXene flexible film as supercapacitor electrode
authors: Yapeng Tian, Maomao Ju, Yijia Luo, Xiaoqing Bin, Xiaojie Lou, Wenxiu Que
conclusion: The facile in situ oxygen doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanosheets have been successfully synthesized by etching the oxygen doped Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase with fluorinated acid salt, which avoids the complex post-treatment. The substitution of carbon atoms in the Titanium octahedron by the oxygen atoms has been also proved by the experimental results and density-functional theory (DFT). The results indicate that the introduction of oxygen atoms can effectively enhance the interlayer space of MXene and promote the conversion from –OH to the -O termination. Moreover, the introduction of appropriate oxygen atoms can improve the electronic conductivity of the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, interface charge transfer between the solid electrode materials and the electrolyte ions, and the interface capacitance, but with sluggish proton transfer within the oxygen doped MXene. Moreover, the electrochemical energy storage for the oxygen doped MXene firstly increases to 306.0C g−1 for the O-Ti3 C2 Tx -0.05 film electrode, then appears a downward trend due to the excessive oxygen doping origin from the formation TiO2- x Fx . The quantitative analysis results indicate that the enhanced capacitance is mainly attributed to the diffusion-controlled capacitance and interface capacitance, which result from the enhanced quantum capacitance due to the improvement of the density of state, the higher Ti active center, and the higher adsorption energy. In short, the oxygen heteroatom is in favor of the quantum capacitance and higher Ti active center, thus giving rise to the enhancement of electrochemical performance for 2D MXene electrode materials. This strategy is of great potential for the future optimization of the 2D MXene electrode material design.

title: Recent advances in MXene-polymer composites for high performance supercapacitor applications
authors: Sanam Bashir, Lala Gurbanova, Ibrahim A. Shaaban, Muhammad Sufyan Javed, Md Rezaul Karim, Syed Shoaib Ahmad Shah, Muhammad Altaf Nazir
conclusion: 7  Conclusion and outlook  Supercapacitors have made extensive use of conducting polymers because of their high theoretical capacity, cheap access to raw ingredients, inexpensive preparation costs, straightforward synthesis techniques, etc. In barely 10 years, MXene has generated a significant curiosity from scholars due to its exceptional conductivity comparable to that of metal and enormous graphene-like usable ion surface area. This paper examines the latest achievements in the research of MXene/conducting polymer composites and supercapacitors are conducted on electrode materials, composite material manufacture, SSCs, and ASCs. MXene and conducting polymers has been the subject of much research, but some obstacles still stand in the way of their widespread use. From the standpoint of material preparation, conductive polymers need careful control over the duration of polymerization and the design of preparation schemes since they have distinct morphologies and are prone to agglomeration. Strong, corrosive acids such concentrated HCl and HF are used to etch MXene compounds. It is clear from the papers previously cited in the text that MXene produced using various etching techniques differs in size, shape, and surface functional groups. More convenient and mild etching techniques must be investigated for the mass synthesis of MXene. Furthermore, the MXene precursor's MAX phase use rate is rather low, therefore when looking into more easy and gentle etching technique, it's important to think about ways to increase the MAX phase's utilization rate.  From the standpoint of material storage, low temperature can lessen MXene's oxidation, but they cannot stop converting MXene to TiO 2 containing molecules of water and oxygen. The researchers used end-group protection to lessen the interaction between oxygen and water molecules and functional groups on the surface of MXene to address the problem of improved MXene material utilization. For instance, Wu et al. [ 262 ] used sodium citrate for MXene's end-group protection; the outcomes shown that the end-base protection significantly extended MXene's storage period. However, MXene's storage mechanism remains a challenging issue that prevents its widespread use.  From the perspective of electrode material use, MXene is highly susceptible to self-stacking because, when the transition metal is removed away, there is no support material left. When charging and discharging, conducting polymers swell, this impairs their performance in electrochemistry. Along with fixing the problems of conducting polymer expansion when charging and discharging and MXene self-accumulation, the successful union of conductive polymers with MXene confers advantageous properties on the electrode material, such as enhanced stability and more adjustable usage conditions (such as pH and temperature).  Additionally, MXene has been progressively employed in numerous applications since its beginnings, such as adsorption, sensors, batteries, SCs, and electromagnetic shielding. Nonetheless, MXenes' component parts and surface functional groups differ, making them varied. The structure, chemistry, and form of conducting polymers also differ. Numerous elements of MXene's characteristics are yet unknown, and its potential has not been completely utilized. Along with the need to address the previously outlined outstanding concerns, theoretical simulation calculations and experiments may be combined in the future. In addition to increasing research efficiency and cutting down on needless exploration time, an efficient computer system should be able to create composite materials with various topologies based on various application scenarios. Because of its exceptional and distinctive qualities, MXene is anticipated to be used in a wider range of research domains as its study progresses.  MXene/conducting polymer composites have great potential in high-performing supercapacitors as a result of their synergic properties i.e. high conductivity of MXene and pseudocapacitance of polymers. However, some challenges of MXene oxidation, polymer swelling, restacking, and harsh etching techniques constrain real world application. Future work should entail the development of green, scalable etching processes, improvements on the stability of MXene through surface passivation, and the utilization of the control of morphology in polymerization. Counteracting self-stacking and agglomeration, on the one hand, with the help of 3D architectures and, on the other hand, with the spacer materials, is essential. Combination of computational modeling and machine learning could advance the design of optimized composites' design. Besides, in situ characterization and long-term device evaluation will be critical in transforming material-level progress to real energy storage systems. By using theoretical, experimental, and engineering methodologies, it is possible to tune these composites for flexible, effective, and scalable supercapacitor applications.  The main challenge is that numerous prior documented attempts have relied on polymer materials and MXene, as well as their composites with MOFs, phosphates, sulphides, oxides, and other chemicals. When researching ESDs for supercapacitor applications, researchers encounter a significant obstacle due to the limited availability of MXene/polymer material. Therefore, combining battery-grade polymers will boost the energy and power density of the devices. Furthermore, the composite of polymer-based materials with MXene (because to its remarkable hydrophilicity) would enhance the device's performance and spark the next generation's curiosity about ESDs, as polymer-based materials exhibit extraordinary EIS performance.  Chemical and thermodynamic stability are also important considerations for the materials being used. MXene is susceptible to oxidation when exposed to H 2 O and O 2 . Therefore, a detailed investigation into the preparation or regulation of MXene to ensure long-term stability is necessary. While sodium ascorbate has been employed as an antioxidant, there is an urgent need for a more efficient way to increase MXene's resistance to oxidation.  Additionally, for applications requiring temperatures greater than room temperature, it is necessary to design new polymer capacitors based on MXene. The current review discussed the various methods of producing MXene and its mechanical, electrical, thermal, optical, magnetic, dielectric, structural, compositional, and functional characteristics. It also highlighted recent advancements in the development of MXene and polymer-based composites-based high-performance supercapacitor devices. The mechanical, electrical, and thermal characteristics of MXene-polymer composites are further highlighted. Last but not least, the development and uses of the next-generation SCs take into account the difficulties and potential future developments associated with MXene/polymer nanocomposites. In numerous applications, MXene/polymer nanocomposites have shown their significant latent potential. Therefore, we hope that our analysis would help researchers identify suitable composite energy storage devices based on MXene and polymers to enhance desirable qualities. In order to create MXene/polymer composites with remarkable and all-encompassing electrochemical performance, future researchers will also find this review helpful as they continue to improve MXene stripping and dispersion techniques.

title: Recent advance in the construction of 3D porous structure Ti3C2Tx MXene and their multi-functional applications
authors: Wenke Hao, Sijia Ren, Xiaodong Wu, Xiaodong Shen, Sheng Cui
conclusion: 4  Summary and outlook  This review has summarized the definition and preparation of MXene-based fibers/whiskers and films/nanosheets, and emphasized on the different kinds of and MXene-based 3D macro aggregations for wide applications including supercapacitors, piezoresistive sensors, electromagnetic shielding, microwave absorption, seawater desalination and catalysis attributed to their rapid electron transfer rate, large specific surface area, contactable active sites, and stable porous channels. Many achievements have been made during the past few years in the construction of different kinds of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations using carbon-based materials, metal oxides, spinel, polymers, metal-based nanoparticles, etc., as the second phase, yet challenges and opportunities remain as follows:  (1) Further enhancement of the mechanical strength of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations. Many MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have been obtained so far, however, the weak interaction of the electrostatic interaction, hydrogen bonding, and van der Waals forces between MXene nanosheets and the other components, have induced the weak mechanical performance, which can be only used in the laboratory scale and have limited their further industrialization applications. Therefore, we should try to effectively control the abundant functional groups on the surface of MXene via the green chemical synthesis route, therefore to improve the interaction strength between the MXene and other components via the strong intermolecular forces and covalent bond, etc. Furthermore, the design of structures, such as the oriented structure and recrystallization texture, should be attracted more attention for the further enhancement of the mechanical strength of the 3D porous material, therefore to obtain more robust and stronger MXene-based 3D macro aggregations.  (2) Construction of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations with controllable pore structures. MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have been frequently prepared by sacrificial template and lyophilization methods, but the pore sizes prepared by these methods are mostly in the range of several tens of micrometers, therefore have limited their specific surface area and their wide applications as supercapacitor, catalysts, and adsorbents. Therefore, the design of controllable pore structures is in highly demand, and the control of building sub-micron-level structures should be explored by combining multiscale theoretical calculations via density functional theory, molecular dynamics, and mesoscopic dynamics, as well as the in-situ characterization techniques such as the in-situ FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy), TEM (Transmission Electron Microscope), XAS (X-ray Absorption Spectra), Raman (Raman spectra), etc to further achieve precise control of the pore structures.  (3) Decrease the fabrication cost and explore more applications of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations. As is reported in this work, the unique properties of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have led to their different application in certain fields, such as supercapacitors, electromagnetic interference shielding, pressure sensors, seawater desalination, and catalysis. However, industrial applications of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations are still in their infancy due to the single and expensive fabrication route of the MXene nanosheets, therefore, the cost-effective fabrication technique for MXene nanosheets with high performance should be developed in further study. In addition, the excellent thermal, electric, and mechanical properties of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations should be expanded to many other fields in the future, such as thermoelectric material, superconducting material, solar cell, biocompatibility, electrocommunication, anti-microbico, etc.

title: FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4 core-shell nanospheres intercalating into Ti3C2Tx for high-performance all-solid-state supercapacitors

title: Advances in MXene-based composites for next-generation flexible supercapacitors: From design and development to applications
authors: Priya Siwach, Latisha Gaba, Sajjan Dahiya, Rajesh Punia, A.S. Maan, Kuldeep Singh, Mohd. Shkir, Anil Ohlan
journal: Advances in Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: 7  Conclusion and future perspectives  The demand for flexible supercapacitors is an ongoing force driving researchers towards an exploration of suitable electrode materials. The quest concludes with MXenes, as its amazing attributes portray it as a potential candidate. Despite the intriguing features, MXenes encounter certain challenges when it comes to real-world applications. Prior to employing MXenes in FSCs, it is imperative to address factors such as agglomeration tendency, oxidation, degradation, and the need for synchronization of mechanical and electrochemical performance. In the Evaluation, this review provides a curtailed introduction of MXene and further encompasses the current advancement in the MXene-based electrode materials for flexible supercapacitors. This review gains significance by offering insights into the fundamentals of flexible supercapacitors, including a detailed discussion of flexibility aspects, variables affecting the performance of electrode materials, followed by an exploration of different flexible MXene electrodes. The discussion incorporates the diverse available substrates and their applications in MXene-based electrode materials, different configurations of flexible devices and gel-based electrolytes. The focused efforts of researchers have propelled MXene-based FSCs forward, resulting in substantial progress and significant advancements. However, reviewing the findings of the review, various important aspects and future prospectives emerge:   1)  The extraordinary attributes of MXenes, including surface chemistry, metallic conductivity, hydrophilicity and layered structure, are an outcome of their synthesis approach. In other words, the properties of MXenes are tunable according to different synthesis methods. Hence, significant research needs to be directed towards developing facile, scalable, cost-effective and environment-friendly synthesis routes. The traditional preparation methods of MXenes involve the use of hazardous etching agents. For instance, HF is the most commonly used acid, which not only pollutes the environment but also negatively impacts the yield and the electrochemical performance of the resulting material. Developing novel green synthesis approaches by varying different etching conditions results in distinct morphologies, modified surface chemistry and tunable properties of MXenes. In this context, initial efforts towards green synthesis of MXenes include examples such as the electrochemical etching method [ 183–186 ], Alkali etching method [ 187 ], Photo Fenton method [ 188 ], and the in-situ hydrothermal method [ 189 , 190 ].    2)  The most abundantly synthesized and commercially available MXenes are based on Titanium. However, depending on different elemental compositions and surface termination groups, various MXenes are predicted. Further exploration of the breadth of MAX phases and the development of new double M or double X MXenes may significantly impact the MXenes' properties, such as mechanical stability, structural diversity and electrical conductivity. Hence, diversification of the MAX phase is imperative since this will eventually lead to the commercialization of MXenes.    3)  Despite achieving milestones in energy storage applications, challenges such as the oxidation and agglomeration of MXene nanosheets continue to hinder their performance. Certainly, the abundance of surface functional groups enhances the capacitive performance, however, these groups adversely affect the physiochemical stability of MXene. Therefore, substantial efforts are needed to design novel and safer synthesis methods. Strategies such as encapsulating MXenes with organic solvents, forming effective composites, and maintaining proper storage conditions will effectively enhance their stability and extend their lifespan.    4)  To enable the transition of MXenes from bench to bedside, scalability must be prioritized. Currently, the conventional top-down etching approach limits large-scale production. Therefore, the development of high-yield, bottom-up, and cost-effective synthesis methods is essential. Advancing scalable fabrication techniques is crucial to fully harness the potential of MXene-based flexible supercapacitors for real-world energy storage solutions.    5)  Aqueous electrolytes are widely used due to their high ionic conductivity, ease of synthesis, and cost-effectiveness. However, their practical application is limited by several drawbacks, including a narrow electrochemical stability window that restricts energy density, as well as the risk of leakage, which raises safety concerns. Whereas, Gel electrolytes, with inherent flexibility, high conductivity, thermal and chemical stability, are ideal for FSCs. Therefore, progress in suitable and efficient solid-state and non-aqueous electrolytes will pave the way for the development of FSCs for the next generation.    6)  Device design—including configuration and substrate selection—is a crucial aspect in the engineering of flexible supercapacitors (FSCs). Common architectures such as bridge–island layouts, interdigital patterns, 3D-printed structures, twisted fibers, and origami designs are frequently employed. However, achieving high energy storage in flexible formats remains a key challenge, necessitating innovative design strategies. MXene stands out as a versatile material, utilized across various device components, with particular emphasis on its role as an electrode. Strategic selection of MXene morphologies (0D, 1D, 2D) based on specific application needs is essential, as the structure and dimensionality of the electrode directly influence device stability and performance.  An equally vital component of flexible devices is the substrate, which must be ultrathin, flexible, conductive, and lightweight. For next-generation devices, MXene-based substrates—such as yarns, fabrics, fibers, and ultrathin metal networks—offer significant potential to enhance performance and functionality. Moreover, the exceptional electrical conductivity of MXenes presents a major opportunity for device miniaturization, as highly conductive MXene films can eliminate the need for additional current collectors.    7)  Balancing flexibility with electrochemical performance remains a key challenge in flexible supercapacitors (FSCs). Variations in device configurations, shapes, and dimensions complicate direct comparisons of mechanical flexibility, even under similar deformation conditions. As flexibility is critical to mechanical stability, standardized quantitative evaluation methods are essential. Enhancing energy storage capacity is equally important, and advancing MXene-based hybrids offers a promising pathway to achieving optimal synergy between flexibility and performance.    8)  Integrating MXene-based flexible supercapacitors (FSCs) into the rapidly evolving landscape of wearable electronics has become imperative. When embedded in smart textiles, sensors, healthcare devices, and portable gadgets, MXene FSCs serve as reliable power sources for these systems. To align with advancing technologies, these devices must also exhibit multifunctional properties such as transparency, self-powering, sensing, photothermal response, electrochromic properties, and self-healing capabilities [ 191 , 192 ]. For instance, multifunctional AgNP@Ti 3 C 2 T  x  /PU composites have demonstrated self-healing/transparency/photothermal functionalities for wearable devices [ 193 ]. Realizing such multifunctional FSCs will pave the way for the next generation of smart energy storage devices.  Continued efforts in this field will revolutionize MXene-based flexible SCs, leading to their widespread commercial application and significantly improving our quality of life.

title: MXene-based ternary composites for supercapacitors: Advancements and challenges
authors: Kabir O. Otun, Azfarizal Mukhtar, Ismail Hossain, Jibril Abdulsalam
conclusion: 9  Conclusions  MXene, a two-dimensional material with high conductivity, surface functional groups, and intercalation capacitance properties, is promising for modifying supercapacitor electrode composition due to its potential to change electrode composition and advance supercapacitor technology. The electrical, mechanical, and electrochemical charge storage capabilities can be enhanced by modifying their surface chemistry; as a result, these materials are well suited for further investigation in supercapacitors. The developments in MXene-based nanocomposites for supercapacitor applications were mostly covered in this review. Additionally, charge storage mechanisms of MXenes stores in supercapacitor devices are also highlighted. The advantages of mixing MXene material with traditional active ingredients such metal sulfides, metal oxides, conductive polymers, and carbon-based compounds are discussed. The most recent advancements in those MXene-based nanocomposites and their uses in supercapacitors are presented in detail. We conclude that:   i.  Ternary MXene composites can be prepared by different methods including vacuum infiltration, solvent-assisted self-assembly, hydrothermal, ultrasonication, electrospinning, among others. However, the synthesis technique adopted influence the surface functional groups, sheet size and interlayer, and ultimately, the electrochemical performance.    ii.  Synthesis of ternary MXene composites prevents MXene materials from restacking, and allows the active surface area accessible to ions, leading to superior electrochemical performances.    iii.  The MXene-carbon/conducting polymer ternary composites have demonstrated superior electrochemical performance when compared with that of the pristine MXene and carbon/conducting polymer composite. The highly conductive two-dimensional MXene nanosheets with good electrical contact and the carbon/conducting polymer composite material together form an efficient conductive network, which provides sufficient electron supply for the Faradaic reaction of PANI.    iv.  A ternary composite of transition metal sulfide and oxide with MXene shows improved energy density than metal-oxide/MXene binary composites and pure MXenes. This enhancement is due to high theoretical capacitance of transition metal sulfides as compared to metal oxide.    v.  The incorporation of metal oxide into the ternary composite resulted in an improvement in its specific capacitance and energy density by creating a larger potential window. Comparing a binary composite electrode to a ternary composite electrode, the latter provided almost twice as much specific capacitance. Because of its improved conductivity and intercalative pseudocapacitive charge storage, the ternary composite demonstrated superior electrochemical performance.    vi.  The remarkable electrochemical stability of ternary MXene and MOF composites is key to delivering high hybrid supercapacitor performance since it guarantees steady performance under a variety of operating situations and increases the device's lifespan. This stability is essential to sustaining capacitance and efficiency throughout multiple cycles of charge and discharge.    vii.  The use of ternary composites in sophisticated microsupercapacitors with high energy and power densities has also demonstrated considerable promise. This was made possible by the strong pseudocapacitance, metallic conductivity, and simplicity in solution processing of MXenes with other flexible materials.     To sum up, ternary composites based on MXene have advanced tremendously and have a lot of potential applications in supercapacitors. The importance of research in pairing MXene with other potential materials is still quite high. Because of its comprehensive performance, flexible MXene-based composites are expected to become the next generation of supercapacitor electrode materials for advanced energy storage applications. Understanding surface chemistry, designing distinctive structures that support high-performance supercapacitors, and comprehending their capacitive energy storage process will all be crucial in this regard.

title: High-rate electrospun Ti3C2Tx MXene/carbon nanofiber electrodes for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Hyewon Hwang, Segi Byun, Seoyeon Yuk, Seulgi Kim, Sung Ho Song, Dongju Lee
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, free-standing Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/CNF electrodes with various MXene sizes were prepared by electrospinning for use in flexible supercapacitors. This versatile and simple technique provided a large surface area and aligned Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets for good dispersion in the fibers. These electrodes demonstrated good gravimetric capacitance up to 120 F/g at 2 mV/s, and maintained a higher capacitance value of 90 F/g at 300 mV/s in comparison to pure CNF electrodes. They also exhibited outstanding flexibility, as demonstrated by dynamic bending tests. Based on these results, MXene-based nanofibers have great potential for applications in flexible and versatile electronic devices beyond energy storage, including electrocatalysis, absorption, and filtration.

title: Synergistic effects in CuO/SnO2/Ti3C2Tx nanohybrids: Unveiling their potential as supercapacitor cathode material
authors: Tholkappiyan Ramachandran, M.P. Pachamuthu, G. Karthikeyan, Fathalla Hamed, Moh'd Rezeq
conclusion: Our studies concentrated on the synthesis and exploration of the synergistic effects of a novel nanosheet-like structure comprising copper oxide (CuO) and tin oxide (SnO2 ) dispersed MXene. Through a successful ultrasonicated coprecipitation method, we achieved the synthesis of CuO/SnO2 /MXene nanohybrids, which were thoroughly characterized using SEM, HRTEM, XRD, XPS, and BET methods, approving the presence of synergistic effects between MXene and CuO/SnO2 . Electrochemical investigations revealed that CuO/SnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx presented significant electrochemical performances, with a high capacitance of 683.5 Fg-1 at 1 Ag-1 in a 2 M H2 SO4 electrolyte and an impressive cycling stability of 85 % after 10,000 cycles. Importantly, this performance surpassed that of MXene-Ti3 C2 Tx and CuO/SnO2 alone. The remarkable results are attributed to the active site availability, synergistic effects, surface area and enhancing electrical conductivity. This research presents a promising avenue for advancing supercapacitor electrode materials, utilizing a novel nanosheet structure to harness synergistic effects for superior electrochemical performance. title: PANI-MnO2 and Ti3C2Tx (MXene) as electrodes for high-performance flexible asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Yudi Wei, Wenlong Luo, Xue Li, Zhongtai Lin, Chunping Hou, Mingliang Ma, Jianxu Ding, Tingxi Li, Yong Ma
conclusion: In summary, the fabrication of flexible asymmetric supercapacitor has been demonstrated by combining PANI-MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx − MXene electrode materials on CC in PVA/H2 SO4 electrolyte. CC/PANI-MnO2 presents improved electrochemical performances with a high specific capacitance of 634.0 F g−1 (380.4 C g−1 ) at 1 A g−1 . The device with good flexibility can successfully work in an extended 1.5 V potential window, which can be up to twice than that of a symmetrical device. Its capacitance can reach up to 21.1 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and the capacitance remains at 83% after 4000 charge-discharge cycles at 1 A g−1 . Moreover, two devices connected in series can power a 1.8 V LED. The device shows an energy density of 47.25 μWh cm−2 at a power density of 2.40 mW cm−2 . Therefore, the flexible asymmetric supercapacitor can be a promising candidate for exploiting next new generation flexible electrochemical energy storage devices. title: MXene material for supercapacitor applications: A comprehensive review on properties, synthesis and machine learning for supercapacitance performance prediction
authors: Daisy Maria Saju, R. Sapna, Utpal Deka, K. Hareesh
conclusion: 9  Summary & outlook  MXenes, a novel class of TMCN, has attracted immense interest in research field by their immense potential in SC applications aided by the exceptional electrical conductivity, rich surface functionality, high SSA, and hydrophilicity. In contrast to conventional electrode materials for SC, MXenes exhibit a unique combination of properties that enable better charge storage mechanism in SC. Nevertheless, the electrochemical properties of the material depends on the other factors including interlayer spacing, surface functional groups, and methods of synthesis. This article has reviewed the properties, methods of synthesis, composites and the studies done till date in the above arena. Different method of synthesis, influencing the structural integrity, morphology, and other properties of MXene have been explored. Attempts to enhance supercapacitive performance and to mitigate the limitations of MXenes including self-restacking and oxidation have driven extensive research into DTM MXenes and MXene-based composites. Industrial perspective of MXene-based SCs with a comparative market analysis is also included in the review. A crucial aspect of the review is the integration of ML methods to predict performance of SC. ML algorithms including ANN, RF, RT, RS, and SISSO have been widely used to explore materials for application in energy sector and also analyze datasets and then predict Csp, energy density, capacitance retention and such features with the help of data studied. This has opened new avenues to escalate the development of highly efficient SCs.  To unlock full potential of MXene-based SCs, several challenges need to be addressed. Developing environment-friendly, fluoride-free synthesis methods without compromising the yield or structural integrity that is important for large-scale synthesis must be focused on. Future research should explore methods to overcome restacking and improvising charge transport dynamics of the material. Although, significant progress has been achieved in MXene material for application in SC, further exploration is inevitable to broaden their application scope and optimize their supercapacitive performance. In-depth understanding of the charge storage mechanism of MXenes when subjected to varying operational conditions is also significant for enhancing performance of MXene. Key features like cyclic stability and environmental stability demands focus as it ensures long-term reliability in practical applications. Interweaving ML for accurate prediction of MXene based materials demands collaboration among the computational and experimental researchers. Addressing these challenges will enable MXenes to revolutionize energy storage industry.

title: Synergistically boosting the performance of asymmetric supercapacitors: in-situ construction of NiCo2S4 on amino-functionalized and Zn2+-predoped multilayer MXene
authors: Min Lu, Mingwu Chen, Xiaohui Xu, Xinyan Wang, Wenxiao Zhang, Xinyu Li
conclusion: Based on a two-step modification strategy, the Zn-N-MX was designed to solve the problems of low conductivity and reduced electron transport capacity caused by surface functionalization and agglomeration of multilayer MXene. Zn-N-MX/NCS was further synthesized. The optimized electrode has a high specific capacitance of 1546.76 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , which is significantly better than MX/NCS (1311.11 F g−1 ). The fabricated Zn1.0 -N-MX/NCS//AC ASC demonstrates remarkable electrochemical performance. It exhibits a high specific capacitance of 150 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 . Regarding its cycle stability, it retains 87.5 % of its initial capacitance after 5000 cycles. Moreover, at a power density of 800 W kg−1 , a high energy density of 53.3 Wh kg−1 is achieved. The multi-dimensional control strategy for the structure and electrical properties of MXene, proposed in this study, effectively promotes the practical application of supercapacitors. title: Interlayer-engineered MXene Nanosheets confining CoGa-LDH enable ultrafast charge transfer kinetics for high-energy potassium-ion supercapacitors
authors: Chenxi Li, Mai Li, Xiang Peng, Inaam Ullah, Haotian Hu, Jiayi Shen, Ayesha Irfan, Wendong Xu, Paul K. Chu
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: This work demonstrates a rational design strategy to synergistically integrate bimetallic CoGa-LDH with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, overcoming the inherent challenges of MXene restacking and limited active-site exposure in LDHs. Optimizing the Co/Ga atomic ratio enables structural refinement, where self-assembly suppresses MXene restacking and generates oxygen vacancies via competitive coordination between metastable metal ions and surface hydroxyl groups. The vacancies dynamically reconfigure the electronic environment to enhance the charge transfer kinetics and create abundant redox-active interfaces. The Co1 Ga1 -LDH/MXene composite delivers exceptional single-electrode performance, achieving a high specific capacitance of 1345.3 F/g at 1 A/g and 94.45 % Coulombic efficiency, significantly outperforming the Ga-deficient counterparts (Co1 Ga0 -LDH/MXene: 162.6 F/g; Co1 Ga0.5 -LDH/MXene: 644 F/g). DFT calculations reveal that Ga3+ incorporation modulates the electronic structure by shifting the Co d -band center from −1.84 eV to −1.67 eV and optimizing the K+ adsorption energy to −2.36 eV to collectively enhance the redox activity and ion diffusion. To demonstrate the commercial feasibility, the ASC device shows a high energy density (77.44 Wh/kg) at a power density (1125 W/kg) as well as excellent cycling stability. This study reveals a promising approach to overcome the technical challenges that have hampered the development of high-performance SCs. title: Highly durable and conductive Korea traditional paper (Hanji) embedded with Ti3C2Tx MXene for Hanji-based paper electronics
authors: Jaehoon Jeong, Hae-Jun Seok, Hak Shin, Su Bin Choi, Jong-Woong Kim, Han-Ki Kim
conclusion: Hanji, which is known for its exceptional mechanical strength and chemical stability, was integrated with highly conductive MXene using a spray-coating strategy to fabricate paper electrodes. As the spray-coating cycles increased, the higher Ti3 C2 Tx content covered the entangled fibers of the Hanji network, resulting in a sheet resistance as low as 0.62 Ohm square−1 after 5 spray-coating cycles. Dynamic bending, folding, rolling, and twisting fatigue tests were conducted to demonstrate the excellent robustness of MXene/Hanji electrodes. Regardless of the dynamic fatigue mode, there were noticeable electrical resistance changes and disconnections between the fibers and MXene. To evaluate its suitability for paper electronics, we applied MXene/Hanji composite electrodes to EMI shielding, heaters, supercapacitors, and temperature sensors. As observed, the Hanji electrodes achieved an EMI shielding efficiency of 43.3 dB, wherein that more than 99.99 % of incident waves could be shielded. Further, they exhibit a favorable thermal conductivity of 1.33 W m−1 K−1 , effectively releasing the heat generated from EMI shielding. In addition, the MXene/Hanji-based paper heater reached a high saturation temperature of 76.2 °C at a low input voltage of 3 V, exhibiting uniform and long-lasting heating performance due to the low resistivity of the MXene. Furthermore, the MXene/Hanji symmetric supercapacitors showed impressive electrochemical performances with a high areal capacitance of 139.6 mF cm−2 at a current density of 1 mA cm−2 and an initial capacitance retention of 79.3 % after 1000 charge-discharge cycles. The MXene/Hanji-based temperature sensor was also evaluated by measuring resistance changes as a function of temperature. In the range of the human body temperature, the resistance of the sensor decreased as the temperature increased, and displayed stable resistance changes with excellent TCR values for the accuracy of the sensor. In conclusion, the conductive MXene coated Hanji substrate presented herein could serve as an exceptional platform propelling the use of paper electrodes in next-generation electronics. title: The phosphorus doping modification of Ti3C2Tx MXene films assisted by tripolyphosphate-crosslinking for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Dan Lu, Yiwei Lu, Yongfang Liang, Jianghai Li, Jiaheng Xu, Jinyu Wu, Haifu Huang, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou
conclusion: In summary, a simple method for improving the electrochemical properties of Ti3 C2 Tx by hetero-atomic doping is reported. In this method, KTPP was used as phosphorus source and the Ti3 C2 Tx was doped by heat treatment. The effect of heat treatment time and temperature on the doping effect of phosphorus was investigated. It was found that the comprehensive electrochemical performance of Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300°C-3h was excellent. The P-doping ratio in Ti3 C2 Tx reaches 1.25 %, the interlayer spacing is regulated and the generation of P−O bond optimizes the redox reaction on the surface of Ti3 C2 Tx . The specific capacitance of Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300 °C-3 h as the electrode material of supercapacitor reaches 365.1 F g−1 , which is twice as high as the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx (183.1 F g−1 ). The study of the relationship between peak current and scanning rate shows that the surface capacitance contribution of all P-doped Ti3 C2 Tx was higher than that of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . When Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300°C-3h based flexible supercapacitor device is bent at 0°, 60°, 90° and 120°, its CV curves, GCD curves and the retention rates of specific capacitance have no obvious changed with angle change, showing the Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300°C-3h based flexible supercapacitor device has good flexibility. When the power density is 483.03 W kg−1 , the supercapacitor device has a high energy density of 10.76 Wh kg−1 . Therefore, the facile and cost-effective KTPP assistance strategy endows MXene film with P-doping, remarkable mechanical flexibility and pseudocapacitance performance, which provides a promising reference route for MXene doping modification, surface functional group regulation and performance improvement. title: 2D/3D Ti3C2Tx/HCl etched Ni-Mn Prussian blue analogue nanocomposite as advanced electrode material for flexible solid-state supercapacitors
authors: Selvadhas Nirmala Kanimozhi, Abdullah Mohammed Alswieleh, Andrea Sorrentino, Jegadesan Subbiah, Anandan Sambandam
conclusion: This study presents the successful design and application of a novel 2D/3D nanocomposite, Ti3 C2 @Ni-Mn PBA, which effectively addresses some of the key challenges associated with MXenes in energy storage applications. By employing a straightforward fabrication method involving the etching of the Ni-Mn PBA surface, the material was seamlessly anchored onto the conductive Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, resulting in a nanocomposite with significantly enhanced electrochemical performance. The Ti3 C2 @Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposite achieved a high specific capacitance of 900 F/g, outperforming its individual components and demonstrating its ability to compete with leading nanomaterials in the field. When incorporated into a two-electrode asymmetric supercapacitor, the device delivered a remarkable energy density of 44 Wh/kg and a power density of 2640 W/kg. Additionally, it successfully powered a multifunctional display for approximately 2 min, showcasing its practical utility in real-world applications. An innovative aspect of this work lies in the development of a flexible, binder-free electrode coupled with an ionic liquid-based gel electrolyte (PVA/KOH/EMP-TFSI). This design provides the device with enhanced mechanical stability, excellent ionic conductivity, and extended durability, paving the way for its integration into wearable and portable electronics, areas of rapidly growing interest. The robust device architecture maintained an outstanding 100 % capacitance retention and a 75 % coulombic efficiency over 1000 charge-discharge cycles, highlighting its reliability for long-term use. Moreover, the unique synergy between the 2D structure of Ti3 C2 Tx and the 3D open framework of Ni-Mn PBA-augmented by etched surface voids-facilitates rapid ion transport, reduced polarization, and improved charge transfer kinetics. This hybrid approach not only enhances the material's energy storage capacity but also contributes to its exceptional rate capability and reversibility. In light of these findings, the Ti3 C2 @Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposite represents a significant step forward in the development of high-performance, sustainable energy storage solutions. Future investigations should focus on further optimizing the material's synthesis, exploring its behaviour with other electrolytes, and scaling its production to meet industrial demands. title: Rationally constructed CeO2/Ti3C2Tx-MXene heterostructure for rapid and efficient visible light photocatalytic activity and enhanced supercapacitor performance
authors: Nagaraju Macherla, Govinda Dharmana, Manjula Nerella, Thirumala Rao Gurugubelli, Ravindranadh Koutavarapu, Jaesool Shim
journal: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, CeO 2 nanospheres were successfully compounded with Ti 3 C 2 MXene via solvothermal method. A smaller crystallite size is noticed from XRD for CeO 2 /MX5 resulted in reduced particle size of CeO 2 nanospheres (∼87 nm) which were uniformly dispersed over 2D nanosheets of MX. Consequently, a larger specific surface area is realized for CeO 2 /MX5 (114.20 m 2 g −1 ) with abundant mesoporosity. XPS surface analysis designates the dual oxidation states (Ce 4+ and Ce 3+ ) of Ceria owing to the rich abundance of reactive oxygen species. Optical study describes the reduced bandgap trend (red-shift) of composites with increasing MX and lower charge transfer resistance is obtained for CeO 2 /MX5. Improved TC photodegradation efficiency (96.05 % in 120 min) of the optimized composite was due to enhanced charge separation and nano-phased heterostructure. Holes and superoxide ions play a vibrant role in the degradation mechanism and the high stability of the optimized composite even after three consecutive cycles. The significant enhancement is electrochemical activity is realized by achieving enhanced specific capacitance (522 F g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 ) along with a capacitance retention of 92.01 % after 5000 cycles. Based on the above merits, the prepared heterostructure was found to be an efficient photocatalyst for degrading TC pollutant from water bodies upon light irradiation and Supercapacitor.

title: MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/cellulose nanofiber/polyaniline film as a highly conductive and flexible electrode material for supercapacitors
authors: Tao Yuan, Zhen Zhang, Qian Liu, Xiu-Tong Liu, Ya-Ning Miao, Chun-li Yao
conclusion: In conclusion, flexible MXene/CNF/PANI composite films with excellent electrical properties were successfully prepared in this study. MXene/CNF/PANI films show a high areal specific capacitance of 2935 mF cm−2 at 1 mA cm−2 , good rate capability with 90.2 % capacitance retention at 5 mA cm−2 , and excellent cycling stability (94 % capacitance retention after 2000 cycles), making it a promising electrode material for supercapacitor. The SC which used the PVA/H2 SO4 gel electrolyte and the MXene/CNF/PANI films as electrodes, possessed a significantly high areal capacitance of 522 mF cm−2 at 5 mA cm−2 , and the SCs also had good electrical stability. The SC provides 94.7 μWh∙cm−2 areal energy density at 573 μW∙cm−2 areal power density, and it has good cycles stability (81.5 % retention after 4000 cycles). This proves that the added CNF/PANI can not only enhance the mechanical properties of the film, but also improve the electrochemical properties of the film. It is also proved that the improved electrochemical performance of the composite conductive films is not only due to the high electrochemical activity of MXene and PANI, but also because CNF provides charge carriers with a path and improves electrolyte ion diffusion by increasing the MXene nanosheet interlayer spacing. The results of this research will facilitate the development of MXene-based hybrid films and high-performance SCs. title: Sulfur-tuned MoS2 quantum dot decorated Ti3C2Tx (MXene) electrode materials for high performance supercapacitor applications
authors: Sumanta Bera, Tapas Kumar Mondal, Yan-Kuin Su, Shyamal Kumar Saha
conclusion: In summary, the few layers of Ti3 C2 Tx 2D sheets have been successfully prepared by the chemical etching of the aluminum layer from the Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase. MoS2 quantum dots with tunning the sulfur ratio are grown on the Ti3 C2 Tx nano sheets to stave off the restacking. The low conductivity of the MoS2 quantum dots is overcome by using Ti3 C2 Tx 2D with superior electronic conductivity. The SCs of the composite samples are increased remarkably due to the combined effect of unsaturated sulfur S 2 2 − on the edge of MoS2 and the Ti3 C2 Tx highly conductive 2 D sheets and delivered the superior potential windows. The S-rich MSM composite has delivered the SC of 985 Fg−1 at a CD of 1 Ag−1 within the potential range from −0.5 V to 0.6 V. Also, S-rich MSM has retained 96.53% of its initial SC after 104 cycles at a CD of 10 Ag−1 . Additionally, over the potential ranges from −0.3/0.4 V to −0.7/0.8 V, it is also workable. Therefore, we eagerly considered that the MoS2 quantum dot and Ti3 C2 Tx composite will be promising electrode materials for supercapacitor application.
