title: Electrophoretic deposition of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheet N-carbon cloth as binder-free supercapacitor electrode material
authors: Zhichao Li, Xinyu Liu, Xuyun Wang, Hui Wang, Jianwei Ren, Rongfang Wang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this work, the binder-free Ti 3 C 2 T x(EPD) /ENCC was developed through the electrophoretic deposition of Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets onto the ENCC substrate as the flexible supercapacitor electrode material. It was found that the rich oxygen-containing functional groups resulted in the well-dispersed Ti 3 C 2 T x on the ENCC substrate via the hydrogen binding effect. The composite electrode displayed an area-specific capacitance of 2080.1 mF·cm −2 at 1 mA·cm −2 current density. In addition, a good rate performance was observed when the current density increased from 10 to 50 mA·cm −2 . The assembled EDLC achieved a long-term stability with a 91% retention after 10,000 GCD cycles at 20 mA·cm −2 .

title: Tailoring interlayer spacing of Ti3C2Tx MXene with organic acid doped polyaniline and polypyrrole for more stable supercapacitors
authors: João V.M. Lima, Hugo G. Lemos, Rafael A. Silva, Jéssica H.H. Rossato, Miguel H. Boratto, Carlos F.O. Graeff
journal: Journal of Alloys and Compounds Communications
conclusion: In this work, we fabricated aqueous inks by incorporating water-dispersible PANI and PPy doped with DBSA organic acid to Ti3 C2 Tx for SCs. XRD showed that the CPs were allocated among MXene sheets. XPS analysis indicated an increased protonation of the CPs, suggesting that the functional groups of Ti3 C2 Tx may act as dopants for the polymers. The increased interlayer spacing and enhanced conductivity of Ti3 C2 Tx /CP improved electrochemical performance, as showed by measurements at a three-electrode setup. Optimal concentration of CPs (10 wt%) increased capacitance from 175 F g−1 (Ti3 C2 Tx ) to 255 F g−1 (Ti3 C2 Tx /PANI) and 270 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 (Ti3 C2 Tx /PPy). Investigations of energy storage mechanisms by Trasatti and Dunn's methods revealed that CPs increase capacitive contribution in terms of surface capacitance, indicating a larger exposed electroactive area, faster electron transfer, and smaller diffusion distance of the ions when compared to pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . Additionally, Ti3 C2 Tx /PPy showed larger contribution of pseudocapacitance feature, attributed to the favourable redox reactions of the CP at the optimized potential window. Similar trend was observed by the symmetric solid-state SCs based on Ti3 C2 Tx and Ti3 C2 Tx /CPs electrodes, in which PANI and PPy increased specific capacitance in 72 % and 208 %, respectively. Cycling stability of the devices also exhibited an impressive capacitance retention after 5000 CV cycles of 100 % and 98 % for PANI and PPy, respectively, against only 88 % of the pristine device. These results indicate that the polymeric nanoparticles doped with the DBSA organic acid acted as effective interlayer spacers, preventing MXene re-stacking during the charge and discharge cycles. In conclusion, we demonstrate a viable method to fabricated efficient and more stable Ti3 C2 Tx /CPs electrodes for SCs. The use of water-dispersible PANI and PPy as additives, besides increasing capacitance and stability of SCs, provides an environmentally and “green” alternative for the device assemble, in addition to reduced costs. title: High-performance flexible supercapacitor based on PEDOT:PSS wrapped delaminated Ti3C2Tx composite: Experimental and DFT validation
authors: Gourab Nandy, Swati Shaw, Subhradip Ghosh, Ashok Kumar Dasmahapatra
conclusion: In this work, we have adequately synthesized delaminated Ti3 C2 Tx (d-Ti3 C2 Tx ) by a low-cost method, integrating the mixed acid etching method followed by DMSO intercalation. Furthermore, PP/d-Ti3 C2 Tx binary composites have been prepared with different ratios by the solvent mixing method and coated on the flexible activated carbon cloth. The conformation of the prepared composites was validated by several characterization techniques such as XRD, RAMAN, UV–Vis, FTIR, FESEM, EDS, and FETEM. In three electrodes electrochemical performance PP, and d-Ti3 C2 Tx with a ratio 1:2 respectively (P1M2) exhibit great results in 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte. The P1M2 electrode shows a brilliant specific capacitance value of 741. 23 F g−1 at a scan rate of 5 mV/s, and 718. 67 F g−1 at a current density of 3. 5 A g−1 . P1M2 electrode shows brilliant E s 35. 93 Whkg−1 (at P s 1049. 90 Wkg-1 ), and 5. 68 Whkg−1 (at Ps 5996. 48 Wkg-1 ). Detailed DFT calculations confirmed that the charge transfer is doubled in the case of PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx in comparison to PEDOT@Ti3 C2 Tx . The charges flow from PEDOT and MXene to PSS. Consequently, PSS possesses the electron-rich region. The DFT calculated solar absorption spectrum for PEDOT:PSS, Ti3 C2 Tx , and PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx agree very well with the experiments. Such excellent agreement substantiates the proposed morphology of the composite i.e. PEDOT wrapped d-Ti3 C2 Tx , aided by multiple PSS carrier pathways. For a flexible and wearable electronic device, we prepared a P1M2-P1M2 SSC and a P1M2-rGO ASC assembly using a gel electrolyte (PVA-H2 SO4 ). The highest specific capacitance has been achieved at 260. 23 F g−1 (at 0. 5 A g−1 ) by the P1M2-P1M2 SSC device; whereas P1M2-rGO ASC has a value of 176. 46 F g−1 (at 0. 1 A g−1 ). The specific energy (specific power) was from 13. 01 Whkg−1 (600 Wkg-1 ) to 2. 63 Whkg−1 (12035 Wkg-1 ) for the SSC device; and from 35. 29 Whkg−1 (240 Wkg-1 ) to 26. 22 Whkg−1 (1200 Wkg-1 ) for ASC device. Both SSC and ASC exhibit excellent performance over various bending and twisting cycles, ASC can operate in a larger potential window and longer durations at low current regions. Moreover, the ASC device shows excellent specific capacitance retention of 89.03 % for 5000 GCD cycles. Subsequently, a red LED was glowed using three ASC devices in series. Hence the P1M2 electrode possesses enormous potential to be used in portable and wearable electronics. title: Fabrication of a flexible asymmetric supercapacitor using molybdenum selenide and titanium carbide mxene (MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx) nanocomposite on carbon cloth
authors: Kuppu Sakthi Velu, Sonaimuthu Mohandoss, Yong Rok Lee, Jeong Hyun Seo
conclusion: Herein, flower-like MoSe2 -decorated Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheets were successfully prepared via a simple hydrothermal method and applied on CC for ASC studies. The as-prepared MoSe2 and Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited flower- and sheet-like surface morphologies, confirmed via FE-SEM and HR-TEM image analysis. FE-SEM of the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite exhibited flower-like MoSe2 petals decorating the sheets-like Ti3 C2 Tx surfaces, with TEM images clearly showing the nanostructure grains embedded on the Ti3 C2 Tx sheets. AFM analysis provided insights into the surface topography, revealing the hexagonal symmetry of MoSe2 nanoflowers, the honeycomb lattice structure of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, and the successful decoration of MoSe2 on the Ti3 C2 Tx sheets in the composite. XPS analysis confirmed the chemical composition and bonding states, confirming the presence of Mo, Se, Ti, C, O, and F elements in the nanocomposite. The XRD pattern confirmed the 1T-phase or metallic nature of MoSe2 -decorated Ti3 C2 Tx . Raman spectra further highlighted the specific phases of the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite. The ASC studies using MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx //KOH//AC nanostructured electrode achieved an excellent specific capacitance 660 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 current density, with an energy density of 33.3 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 1683 W kg−1 . EIS analysis indicated enhanced electrical conductivity and charge transfer capabilities, further confirming the suitability of the material for energy storage applications. Cycle stability tests demonstrated the outstanding durability of the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite, with a capacity retention of 97.35 % after 10,000 cycles at a high current density of 10 A g−1 . The solid-state supercapacitor device assembled with the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite demonstrated a specific capacitance of 223.12 F g⁻1 , an energy density of 7.74 Wh kg⁻1 , and a power density of 292.60 W kg⁻1 . It exhibited a capacity retention of 96.04 % and a Coulombic efficiency of 98.69 % over 10,000 cycles. The MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite emerged as a highly promising material with superior morphological, structural, and electrochemical characteristics. Its unique combination of flower-like MoSe2 and Ti3 C2 Tx sheets, along with excellent cycle stability, underscores its potential for practical and high-performance applications in energy storage, particularly in supercapacitors. title: Flexible, temperature-tolerant supercapacitor based on Ti3C2Tx MXene in ionic liquid gel electrolyte
authors: Jingdi Shang, Libo Wang, Ying Gao, Ji’a Yang, Qixun Xia, Qianku Hu, Aiguo Zhou, Bo Wang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  A simple PVDF-HFP-EMIMBF 4 gel polymer electrolyte was fabricated using the casting method, and a solid-state supercapacitor was assembled with Ti 3 C 2 T x as the electrode material. The ionic polymer electrolyte broadens the operating window of MXene-based capacitors, enhancing its energy and power densities. Moreover, the EMIMBF₄-PVDF-HFP gel polymer electrolyte extends the operational range of the designed capacitor, allowing it to maintain a high specific capacitance at 100 °C, making it suitable for extreme conditions. The capacitor also exhibits stable capacitance under torsional and repeated bending conditions. More importantly, the constructed device demonstrates excellent specific capacitance at 180° bending and 360° twisting angles and retains remarkable stability after 1000 bending cycles at 180°. These findings confirm its potential to enhanced energy density by extending the voltage window of flexible solid-state energy devices.

title: Integrating V-doped CoP on Ti3C2Tx MXene-incorporated hollow carbon nanofibers as a freestanding positrode and MOF-derived carbon nanotube negatrode for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Ishwor Pathak, Bipeen Dahal, Debendra Acharya, Kisan Chhetri, Alagan Muthurasu, Yagya Raj Rosyara, Taewoo Kim, Syafiqah Saidin, Tae Hoon Ko, Hak Yong Kim
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this work, unique nanostructures of vanadium-doped cobalt phosphide nanorods uniformly anchored over Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene-integrated hollow carbon nanofibers and cobalt nanoparticles distributed carbon nanotubes at carbon nanofibers were judiciously designed. The freestanding V-CoP@MX/HCF (positrode) and Co-CNT@CNF (negatrode) exhibit superior specific capacitances of 1896.8 F g −1 and 405.5 F g −1 , respectively, at 1 A g −1 and a high cycling life. The as-developed flexible asymmetric device (V-CoP@MX/HCF//Co-CNT@CNF) displays a desired energy density of 72.4 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 800.12 W kg −1 and demonstrate superior cycling performance over 10,000 cycles. The device is adequately flexible and displays a stable performance at different bending angles. Additionally, the two ASCs in series connection lit up a 1 W LED for ∼ 10 min, demonstrating the device’s application potential. Overall, this work highlights unique engineering approaches to rationally design novel and efficient freestanding positive and negative electrodes for supercapacitors, which will significantly contribute to the rising demand for flexible energy storage devices.

title: Ti3C2Tx MXene based hybrid electrodes for wearable supercapacitors with varied deformation capabilities
authors: Jingmin Zhang, Degang Jiang, Leiping Liao, Liang Cui, Rongkun Zheng, Jingquan Liu
conclusion: In summary, we have demonstrated a simple template method for the preparation of the arbitrary-shaped and N-doping MGC hybrid foam through the procedures of “dip-coating”, reduction, freeze-drying and annealing treatment. Significantly, the commercial MF cannot only works as cost-efficient and arbitrary-shaped template, but also introduces the heteroatom nitrogen into the Ti3 C2 Tx /rGO nanosheets. Because of the interconnected and alternating Ti3 C2 Tx /rGO cellular walls, the resultant N-doped MGC-500 hybrid foam incorporates good compressibility and electrochemical performance, making it an ideal material as freestanding electrode. Thanks to the enhancement of PVA-H2 SO4 electrolyte, the as-prepared SSC device showed stable capacitance at different compressive states. In addition, the compressed SSC still exhibited good flexibility and stability at different bending or twist angles. In a word, this template method for fabrication of SSC based on MGC hybrid foam may pave the way for the future development of scalable, arbitrary-shaped and free-standing electrode materials with multiple deformation capabilities.

title: Designing an electrochemical energy storage device using recycled Ti3C2Tx MXene and reduced graphene oxide spent wastewater adsorbents
authors: Marcelo A. Andrade, Olivier Crosnier, Patrik Johansson, Thierry Brousse
conclusion: This study expands the concept of directly repurposing spent wastewater adsorbents into functional energy storage devices through the electrochemical behavior of various heavy metal cations in various electrolytes. Our findings demonstrate that the adsorption of redox-active heavy metals brings tunable faradaic contributions that synergistically merge with the pristine capacitance, improving the total capacities. Beyond the initial proof-of-concept, we demonstrate how newly explored adsorbents and adsorbates, including Pb2+ , Cu2+ , and multi-cation combinations, such as Hg2+ and Cu2+ , significantly expand the tunability of redox activity of recycled rGO and MXene-based electrodes, with the former being superior for both adsorption of Cu2+ cations and as electrodes. Furthermore, the coupling of different adsorbed cations enables the tuning of the voltage plateau, and we also present the assembly and evaluation of full cells using recycled metal-loaded adsorbents as both positive and negative electrode materials. The unique electrochemistry of each cation is also determined by the choice of electrolyte, influencing how effectively the redox activity can be used. Furthermore, the capacity fading, caused by cation dissolution, is also electrolyte-dependent and improved upon by multiple and quite different types of aqueous electrolytes, although not yet completely mitigated. Overall, this study paves the way for a new class of multifunctional materials derived from environmental waste streams, offering both ecological remediation and alternative energy solutions. title: Butanedioic acid unlock shelf-stable Ti3C2Tx (MXene) dispersions and their electrochemical performance in supercapacitor
authors: Jai Kumar, Razium Ali Soomro, Baomin Fan, Jiayi Tan, Ning Sun, Bin Xu
conclusion: A chemically modified MXene nanosheet covered with succinic acid has been developed. This nanosheet exhibits exceptional antioxidation properties in aqueous solutions. Succinic acid effectively filled the reactive sites of MXene nanosheets by chemical bonding, hence preventing aqueous and oxygen assaults. The examination of the ultraviolet-visible (UV–Vis.) spectrum indicates that the impact of SSA on the water-based dispersion of Ti3 C2 Tx (0.05 mg mL−1 ) relies on its concentration. The antioxidant activity is maximally achieved when the concentration of SSA added to the dispersion reaches 1 mg mL−1 . After being exposed for 42 days, the MXene dispersion showed no signs of oxidation, and a time constant of 243 days was found by fitting first-order reaction kinetics. An electrochemical study demonstrates that the Ti3 C2 Tx membrane electrode, following 42 days of SSA protection, retains exceptional electrochemical performance. In addition, multi-scale simulation results show that SSA tends to be adsorbed on the edges and basal surface defects of Ti3 C2 Tx . Electron transfer occurs between the O atom on the carboxylic acid carbonyl group (-COOH) and the Ti atom at the defect site, which makes SSA chemically adsorbed on MXene oxidation-sensitive sites. Therefore, the addition of succinic acid functionalized modification can significantly prolong the lifespan of MXene nanosheets and fully satisfy the needs of a new MXene water-based solution, making it suitable for future applications. title: Heterostructured bimetallic–sulfide@layered Ti3C2Tx–MXene as a synergistic electrode to realize high-energy-density aqueous hybrid-supercapacitor
authors: Muhammad Sufyan Javed, Xiaofeng Zhang, Salamat Ali, Abdul Mateen, Muhammad Idrees, Muhammad Sajjad, Saima Batool, Awais Ahmad, Muhammad Imran, Tayyaba Najam, Weihua Han
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, we have successfully embedded NCS nanoflowers into exfoliated Ti 3 C 2 T  x  –MXene nanosheets through a facile hydrothermal process to build a heterostructure NCS@MXene composite electrode. The nanoflowers of NCS were uniformly dispersed over the MXene layers and formed a sandwich-like structure. An optimized HS−NCS@MXene sample exhibits a remarkable capacitance/capacity of 2637 F g –1 (1582 C g –1 ) at 2.5 A g –1 with stable cycling life (96%) over 10,000 cycles. The assembled HS−NCS@MXene//AC–AHSC can operate at a broad potential range of 1.6 V and deliver a high capacitance 226 F g –1 at 1.5 A g –1 with stable cyclic life (92%) up to 20,000 cycles. Moreover, the HS−NCS@MXene//AC–AHSC also possesses the highest energy density of 80 Wh kg –1 at a power density of 1196 W kg –1 , exceeding the recently published similar work. The excellent results were verified by DFT calculations, which suggest that the conductivity of HS−NCS@MXene is better than pristine MXene and NCS. The synergistic effects of NCS and MXene enable the HS−NCS@MXene composite to deliver outstanding electrochemical performance for AHSCs.

title: Cellulose nanofiber/MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/liquid metal film as a highly performance and flexible electrode material for supercapacitors
authors: Tao Yuan, Zhen Zhang, Qian Liu, Xiu-Tong Liu, Shao-Qu Tao, Chun-li Yao
conclusion: In summary, this paper introduces the CNF/MXene/GI composite films with high capacitance and mechanical flexibility. The CNF/MXene/GI films exhibit a notable areal specific capacitance of 871.3 mF cm−2 at 1 mA cm−2 , along with exceptional cycling stability (96.9 % capacitance retention after 2000 cycles), thus demonstrating their potential as a promising electrode material for supercapacitors. Moreover, when the CNF/MXene/GI films were employed as electrodes in the supercapacitor, a high areal capacitance of 188.2 mF cm−2 at 5 mA cm−2 was achieved, accompanied by satisfactory electrical stability. Furthermore, the supercapacitor demonstrated an areal energy density of 106.7 μWh∙cm−2 at an areal power density of 420 μW∙cm−2 , while maintaining good cycle stability (83.7 % retention after 5000 cycles). In this work, a supercapacitor electrode material with high capacitance and mechanical flexibility was demonstrated by adding liquid metal to the CNF matrix and combining it with MXene. As spacers, CNF and GI effectively separate adjacent MXene sheets, increase MXene's ion-accessible surface area, and provide a rich channel for ion diffusion. GI acts as a bridge between the MXene lamella, making the temporal structure of the material more complete, overcoming the self-stacking phenomenon of MXene films, and improving the electron transport rate. This study presents a promising approach towards the advancement of cellulose-based flexible electrodes, while concurrently propelling the progress of flexible supercapacitors characterized by high storage capacity and exceptional mechanical properties. title: A novel CoS/Ti3C2Tx MXene conductive filler effectively improves the pseudocapacitive performance of conductive hydrogel electrode materials for all-solid-state supercapacitors
authors: Ting Yu, Siyu Ge, Mingmao Hu, Haoran Wu, Shenghua Yao
conclusion: Optimising the microstructure of the active materials, suppressing the stacking, and agglomeration phenomena of the active materials are vital for maintaining the specific capacitance of flexible all-solid-state supercapacitors. A simple and green two-step method was employed in this study to combine highly conductive CoS/Ti3 C2 Tx with PAA/CS hydrogel matrix. The CoS effectively suppresses the build-up of reactive Ti3 C2 Tx under excessive mass loading, and the constructed physical dual network structure improves the mechanical properties of the conducting hydrogel. Compared to hydrogels with only a single conductive filler, CoS/Ti3 C2 Tx has better electrochemical properties due to the presence of CoS functioning as an electronic bridge, which accelerates the transfer of photogenerated electrons. The conductivity of the PCCT conductive hydrogel was driven to 0.029 S/cm, which is a significant increase of about 1.4 times compared to PCT (0.021 S/cm). Meanwhile, the hydroxyl groups contained on the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene surface and the CS branched chain segments form transient hydrogen bonding, which makes the hydrogel have a self-healing effect and the self-healing hydrogel repair interface is still clear with no rediffusion after self-healing. A new insight into the preparation strategy of MXene-based hydrogel materials for electrochemical energy storage is provided in this work. title: Etching duration as a key parameter for tailoring Ti3C2Tx MXene electrochemical properties
authors: P.E. Lokhande, Udayabhaskar Rednam, Syed Khasim, Taymour A. Hamdalla, Amol Vedpathak, Deepak Kumar, Kulwinder Singh
journal: Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids
conclusion: This study investigated the impact of etching duration on the electrochemical performance of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Three samples were synthesized via hydrofluoric (HF) acid etching of Ti3 AlC2 -MAX phase, with etching times of 48, 72, and 96 h. Structural analysis showed that longer etching durations led to increased interplanar spacing and higher dislocation densities. FESEM imaging further confirmed the expansion of layered structures with prolonged etching. Although the 96-h etched sample exhibited the largest interlayer spacing, the 72-h sample demonstrated the best electrochemical performance, achieving a specific capacitance of 488 Fg-1 at a current density of 0.25 Ag-1 . Studies on rate capability and cyclic stability also indicated the superior performance of this sample. To assess its practical application, an all-solid-state supercapacitor device was fabricated using the 72-h etched material, delivering an energy density of 5 Whkg−1 and a power density of 1000 Wkg-1 , along with excellent cycling stability. These results highlight the importance of optimizing etching duration to enhance the electrochemical properties of MXene, emphasizing its potential for advanced energy storage applications. title: Flexible all-solid-state asymmetric supercapacitor based on Ti3C2Tx MXene/graphene/carbon nanotubes
authors: Yanling Jin, Jiahui Geng, Yilan Wang, Zirui Zhao, Zhengyan Chen, Zhengzheng Guo, Lu Pei, Fang Ren, Zhenfeng Sun, Peng-Gang Ren
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  Herein, MXene/graphene/CNTs films were successfully fabricated by a vacuum assisted filtration. Introducing electrochemical exfoliated graphene and carbon nanotubes between the MXene nanosheet layers to increase the spacing and specific surface area of the sample layers, alleviate the stacking of MXene nanosheets, and improve the electrochemical properties. The prepared MXene/graphene/CNTs possesses increased specific surface area, average pore size, pore volume (112.259 m 2  g  −1 , 9.982 nm, 0.276 cm 3  g  −1 ), compared to MXene (93.088 m 2  g  −1 , 3.786 nm, 0.088 cm 3  g  −1 ). Consequently, MXene/graphene/CNTs delivers high area specific capacitance of 1862.5 mF cm −2 at 1 mA cm −2 and excellent rate capability (1525 mF cm −2 , 81.88 % at 20 mA cm −2 ). Flexible asymmetric supercapacitors constructed with MXene/graphene/CNTs and active carbon as positive and negative electrodes, and PVA/H 2 SO 4 gel as solid electrolyte, achieves an energy density of 133.75 μWh cm −2 at the power density of 750 μW cm −2 . In addition, at a current density of 10 mA cm −2 , there is still 94.9 % of the initial performance after cycling 8000 charge/discharge cycles, exhibiting a single-turn decay rate down to 0.00019 %. the Besides, this flexible supercapacitor manifests outstanding electrochemical stability at different bending times. These fascinating properties make this prepared flexible supercapacitor device very promising for wearable electronics applications.

title: Ti3C2Tx MXene-based (Cobalt–Vanadium) bimetallic sulfides 0D@2D heterostructure composite for asymmetric supercapacitor application
authors: Mahmoud Dardeer, Kisan Chhetri, Devendra Shrestha, Rupesh Kandel, Chan Hee Park
conclusion: In summary, a new heterostructure type of 0D@2D CoVS2 @MXene hybrid composite was synthesized through single-step hydrothermal process for the practical supercapacitor application. The morphology and structure of the hybrid composite reveal that the CoVS2 NPs are successfully decorated over the surface of the 2D MXene substrate, resulting in enriched active sites, and easy pathways for ion/electron transfer. As cathode material, the CoVS2 @MXene hybrid achieved a high-capacity value of ∼423 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1 , with an outstanding capacity retention of ∼93.1 % after 5000 GCD cycles. Remarkably, the assembled CoVS2 @MXene//VS2 @MXene ASC device delivered a significant energy density of about ∼57.78 W h kg−1 at 832 W kg−1 , and a negligible cycling change. Therefore, this work reveals the promising potential for the development of MXene-based composites for future energy storage electronics. title: Cu1.5Mn1.5O4 hollow sphere decorated Ti3C2Tx MXene for flexible all-solid-state supercapacitor and electromagnetic wave absorber
authors: Shuai Zhang, Ying Huang, Jiaming Wang, Xiaopeng Han, Guozheng Zhang, Xu Sun
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, CuMnHS decorating between MXene nanosheets can considerably enhance the electrochemical and microwave absorption capabilities of NXene. The improvements include 3D structure with rich interfaces, greater interlayer spacing, higher relaxation polarization, optimized impedance matching, and interlayer ion transport efficiency. The CuMnHS@MX electrode has a specific capacitance of 2089 mF/cm 2 and 99.89% high capacity retention rate after 8000 cycles. The symmetrical flexible all-solid-state supercapacitor assembled by CuMnHS@MX hybrid film has a specific capacitance of 382.9 mF/cm 2 and energy density of 53.18 μWh/cm 2 at 277.8 μW/cm 2 power density. For microwave absorption performance, when the thickness is 4 mm, the RL min of CuMnHS@MX reaches −53.42 dB at 6.08 GHz. It is worth noting that CuMnHS@MX has adjustable absorbing properties, and the absorbing energy efficiency can cover X and most C, Ku bands. For electrochemical energy storage and electromagnetic wave absorption, CuMnHS@MX is a potentially bifunctional material.

title: Interface engineering based NiCoMoO4/Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructure for high-performance flexible supercapacitors
authors: Wei Li, Bita Farhadi, Miaomiao Liu, Peiru Wang, Jiayi Wang, Yaoyao Zhang, Guoxiang Ma, Runnan Huang, Jiayi Zhao, Kai Wang, Yao Tong
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: In conclusion, we have successfully developed NiCoMoO4 /MXene heterostructure electrode materials with exceptional electrochemical properties via a facile co-precipitation method. This method effectively addresses the issue of MXene layer restacking during the preparation process. Notably, the NiCoMoO4 / MXene-2 heterostructure achieves a high specific capacitance of 1900 F/g at 1 A/g, surpassing that of pure NiCoMoO4 (932 F/g) and MXene (230 F/g). It also exhibited outstanding rate performance (1290 F/g at 20 A/g) and excellent cyclic stability (94.73 % initial capacity retention rate after 10,000 charge and discharge cycles). The electrochemical performance of the electrode materials reported in this paper outperforms that of previously reported MXene composite materials [52] ,[53] ,[54] . This remarkable performance can be attributed to the synergistic effect between the heterostructure and oxygen vacancy. Additionally, our DFT calculations demonstrate that enhanced electron coupling in the NiCoMoO4 /MXene heterostructure is also responsible for its superb electrochemical performance. Impressively, the constructed NiCoMoO4 /MXene//AC FSSCs achieve a maximum energy density of 72.89 Wh kg−1 at power densities up to 850 W kg−1 while maintaining significant cycle stability and flexibility. Thus, this paper provides a straightforward approach for preparing MXene metal composites with high specific capacitance and long cycle stability, offering new insights into developing electrode materials with flexible and superior electrochemical properties for next-generation portable wearable electronics. title: Ti3C2Tx MXene@rGO composite electrodes for high-performance supercapacitor applications
authors: Avinash Rundla,  Priyanka, Bheem Kumar, Prashant Tripathi, Pushpendra Kumar, Kedar Singh
conclusion: In summary, Ti3 C2 Tx was synthesized through a selective etching process to remove the Al layer from its pristine MAX phase (Ti3 AlC2 ) precursor. Comprehensive characterization of the synthesized materials was performed using Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), BET analysis, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping. The electrochemical performance of as-prepared Ti3 C2 Tx and Ti3 C2 Tx @rGO composites was evaluated in a three-electrode system comprising a 1M H2 SO4 electrolyte, with Ti3 C2 Tx -based electrodes serving as the working electrodes, Pt as the counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl as the reference electrode. The results reveal that Ti3 C2 Tx @rGO composites, particularly at optimized mass ratios, significantly enhance the electrochemical performance of supercapacitors. Among the tested compositions, the (Ti3 C2 Tx )90 (rGO)10 composite electrode achieved a remarkable specific capacitance of 357 F/g at 1 A g−1 , surpassing the 220 F/g of the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx electrode. This enhancement is attributed to the synergistic effect of reduced graphene oxide (rGO) within the Ti3 C2 Tx matrix, which facilitates improved ion transport and charge storage. Furthermore, the (Ti3 C2 Tx )90 (rGO)10 electrode demonstrated excellent cycling stability, retaining 85.35 % of its capacitance after 12,000 charge-discharge cycles. In this composite, rGO acts as a conductive bridge, connecting Ti3 C2 Tx layers, accommodating volume changes during cycling, and serving as a nanoscale secondary current collector. These findings underscore the potential of Ti3 C2 Tx @rGO composites as high-performance electrode materials for next-generation supercapacitors. title: Nitrogen-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene prepared by thermal decomposition of ammonium salts and its application in flexible quasi-solid-state supercapacitor
authors: Man Cai, Xiaochun Wei, Haifu Huang, Fulin Yuan, Cong Li, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Jin Guo
conclusion: A simple N-doping method for Ti3 C2 Tx MXene was developed herein based on the thermal decomposition of ammonium salts. A nitrogen doping level of about 1.42 at.% was obtained in the N-Ti3 C2 Tx by heat treatment with ammonium chloride at 350 °C for 3h. The resulting N-Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited an excellent electrochemical performance, with a high specific capacitance of 449 F g−1 , an outstanding cyclic stability (about 80.4 % retention after 8000 cycles), and a high energy density of 9.57 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 250 W kg−1 for quasi-solid-state flexible device. The capacitance improvement was attributed to the positive effect of nitrogen doping on MXene. For example, nitrogen doping increased the number of Ti3 C2 Tx surface active sites and the related defects that can enhance surface capacitive contribution, and effectively increased the interlayer spacing of the Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, thereby facilitating the rapid diffusion and transmission of electrolyte ions in the electrode, and increasing the charge storage capacity and cyclic stability. The significant improvement in electrochemical performance indicates that the N-Ti3 C2 Tx can be used as a promising high-performance energy storage electrode material. The proposed thermal decomposition of ammonium salts is a simple and convenient strategy, thereby opening up a new pathway for the heteroatom doping of MXenes.

title: Construction of CoMoO4 nanosheets arrays modified by Ti3C2Tx MXene and their enhanced charge storage performance for hybrid supercapacitor
authors: Xiaochun Wei, Man Cai, Fulin Yuan, Cong Li, Haifu Huang, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Jin Guo
journal: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
conclusion: A novel synergistic 3D nanoarrays structure in CoMoO4 -Ti3 C2 Tx /NF is designed for improving the performance of CoMoO4 . The large CoMoO4 layer and small Ti3 C2 Tx layer support each other, which facilitates the electrolyte to penetrate into the electrode material, improves the utilization rate of the active material and facilitates rapid transfer of electrons and ions. In addition, the introduction of Ti3 C2 Tx improves the conductivity of the CoMoO4 materials and enriches the active sites of the reaction for redox action, thus enhances the energy storage capacity of electrode material. As expected, the specific capacity reaches 870.7 C g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 and the retention rate is 68.2 % after 6000 cycles for CoMoO4 -Ti3 C2 Tx /NF. The hybrid supercapacitor composed of CoMoO4 -Ti3 C2 Tx /NF and N-rGO/NF electrode has a high specific capacitance of 148 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 . Comparing to the initial specific capacitance, this hybrid supercapacitor remines 90.3 % after 6000 cycles. Besides, the power density of the device reaches 370 W kg−1 and 7500 W kg−1 , corresponding energy density of 46.3 Wh kg−1 and 25.6 Wh kg−1 , respectively. These results demonstrate that Ti3 C2 Tx MXene plays a significant role in modifying the structure and electrochemical performance of CoMoO4 materials, which opens a way to achieve metal oxides with high charge storage capacity and long cycling stability performance. It is believed that this simple preparation method will be extended to improve the charge storage performance of other metal oxides. title: Heterostructured Ti3C2Tx loaded NiCoCu-based layered double hydroxide as a high-performance cathode for hybrid supercapacitors
authors: Disong Wang, Xiaohui Guan, Liu Yang, Baoyang Tian, Jiqing Zhang, Ruotong Li, Tao Zou, Penggang Yin, Guangsheng Wang
conclusion: In conclusion, this study demonstrates an effective approach to enhance the electrochemical property of NiCo-LDH through strategic Cu doping and MXene loading, creating heterostructures. Ti3 C2 Tx @NiCoCu-LDH delivers an exceptional specific capacity of 1891.4 F·g−1 (262.2 mAh·g−1 ). The rationally designed hierarchical porous architecture effectively mitigates structural stress during charge-discharge processes, ensuring excellent cyclic performance. The Ti3 C2 Tx @NiCoCu-LDH//AC HSC achieves remarkable energy storage performance, with a high energy density of 35.5 Wh·kg−1 at 826.8 W·kg−1 , surpassing most reported counterparts. Theoretical calculations further substantiate that Ti3 C2 Tx @NiCoCu-LDH exhibits superior electrical conductivity, active electron transfer, and enhanced interactions with charge carriers compared to pristine NiCoCu-LDH, leading to significantly improved electrochemical activity. This work establishes a viable strategy for designing advanced heterostructural cathodes for high-performance supercapacitors. title: Cost-effective synthesis route for ultra-high purity of Ti3AlC2 MAX phase with enhanced performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene and MXene/NiO composite for supercapacitor application
authors: Kapil Dev Verma, Kamal K. Kar
conclusion: This study introduced an optimized synthesis route that enhances the scalability and cost-effectiveness for the preparation of high-purity Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. The presence of impurities such as TiC, TiAl, and Ti2 AlC has impeded previous attempts to alleviate the cost burden by utilizing TiO2 as a precursor. It proposed an optimized synthesis method that was designed to produce an ultra-high pure Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase. The method involves the use of an optimized molar ratio of precursors (3TiO2 :6.1Al:2C), a calcination process (1350°C, 2.5 hrs dwell time), and HCl washing. The resulting material was subsequently transformed into pure MXene (Ti3 C2 Tx ) through a mild etching process, contributing to its long-term stability. In addition, a composite of MX/NiO was synthesized through bath sonication to resolve the issues of restacking and the limited performance of MXene for supercapacitor applications. Utilizing Raman spectroscopy, XRD analysis, FT-IR spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, BET analysis, XPS analysis, and SEM imaging, the comprehensive investigation of MXene, NiO, and MX/NiO demonstrates their effective fabrication. The electrical conductivity of MXene films was measured and verified by illuminating LED bulbs, thereby emphasizing their potential for electronic applications and energy storage. This study also examined the electrochemical efficacy of MXene and MX/NiO-based electrodes with H2 SO4 and KOH electrolytes for supercapacitor applications. Ti3 C2 Tx MXene possesses a specific capacitance of 358.5 F g−1 . The MX/NiO composite achieved a specific capacitance of 892 F g−1 within a potential window of −0.6–0.4 V when using 2 M H2 SO4 electrolyte at a current density of 1 A g−1 . These materials-based symmetric supercapacitors exhibit specific capacitances of 171 F g−1 and 461 F g−1 , respectively, at a current density of 1 A g−1 in a 6 M KOH electrolyte. Further, the DFT-based theoretical analysis of MAX phase, MXene, and MX/NiO composite demonstrated superior quantum capacitance and pseudocapacitance compared to the MAX phase, attributed to their increased surface area and enhanced reactivity. This study solves the problems of MXene's high cost, short life span, and tendency to self-stack for supercapacitor applications by using inexpensive precursors, a moderate etching synthesis route, and the synthesis of MX/NiO composites. title: Construction of CuCo2O4 hollow microspheres/Ti3C2Tx MXene composite for electrode material of hybrid supercapacitors
authors: Xiaobo Chen, Mengwen Zhou, Yi Min
journal: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
conclusion: In summary, the CuCo2 O4 -HS/MXene composite was synthesized as a positive electrode material for HSC by a simple electrostatic assembly approach. The CuCo2 O4 hollow microspheres were highly bound together with conductive MXene sheets, which provides fast electron transport pathway. The highly porous structure provides abundant reactive sites for Faradic reaction and improves the efficiency of rapid redox reactions. Electrochemical measurements showed that CuCo2 O4 -HS/MXene-3 had a high specific capacity (1341.4 C g−1 at 1 A g−1 ) and outstanding cycle performance (about 90.9% retention after 10 000 cycles at 5 A g−1 ). Furthermore, the assembled CuCo2 O4 -HS/MXene-3//AC device achieves an excellent specific energy of 66.3 W h kg−1 at a specific power of 724.3 W kg−1 , and exhibits 97.3% retention after 10,000 cycles at 8 A g−1 . Therefore, all these above indicate the CuCo2 O4 -HS/MXene composites are prospective candidates for high-performance supercapacitors. title: Hierarchical NiGa-LDH/Ti3C2Tx MXene composites for enhanced capacitance in alkaline all-solid-state energy storage
authors: Wendong Xu, Mai Li, Haotian Hu, Waqar ul Hasan, Chenxi Li, Qinglin Deng, Zheyi Meng, Xiang Peng
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: The NiGa-LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrode was designed for all-solid-state asymmetric supercapacitors (AASCs). The hierarchical nanocomposite of NiGa-LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene was synthesized using a hydrothermal method, with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene as a template for layered double hydroxide(LDH) nanoflakes. Compared to the direct integration of Ni-LDH on Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, the tuned NiGa-LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene anode at 1 mA cm−2 demonstrates impressive (618.66 F g−1 ) specific capacitance along with cycling stability (retention of 93.75 % capacitance after 5,000 cycles). The orderly NiGa-LDH nanoflakes within the two-dimensional Ti3 C2 Tx MXene not only increase the specific surface area for enhanced ion and electron transport but also serve as spacers, improving interlayer separation and enabling efficient charge exchange across the electrode and electrolyte. The AASCs comprising NiGa-LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene//activated carbon(AC) exhibits a notable energy density of 20 Wh kg−1 , coupled with a power density of 400 W kg−1 . It also demonstrates impressive cycling stability, retaining 86.2 % of its capacitance after 5,000 cycles, along with a high Coulombic efficiency of 98.33 % over the same cycle count. The NiGa-LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene hierarchical nanostructure offers a novel approach for incorporating MXene-based nanomaterials into energy storage practical applications and boosting the pseudo-capacitance of LDH materials. This work presents a facile and environmentally friendly synthesis approach for the fabrication of hierarchical NiGa-LDH/Ti3 C2 Tx MXene materials with superior electrochemical properties, which are highly promising for supercapacitor application. Compared to other Ni-based Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes, the incorporation of Ga element significantly improves the material's stability and specific capacitance. title: Cation-induced Ti3C2Tx MXene@melamine sponge aerogels with large layer spacing and high strength for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Debin Cai, Shuai Wu, Zhen Tian, Li Guo, Yanzhong Wang
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: In summary, a series of three-dimensional porous M−Ti3 C2 Tx @MS aerogels were successfully fabricated by using melamine sponge as a scaffold and cations as crosslinkers. The 3D porous MS serve as an ideal support for enhancing the strength of M−Ti3 C2 Tx @MS aerogels, and the inserted cations not only induce the formation of MXene hydrogel but also improve the layer spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets. The experimental results show that Mg-Ti3 C2 Tx aerogel is uniformly distributed in the framework of MS, which not only encapsulates on the skeletons but also fills the pores of MS. The unique structure of M−Ti3 C2 Tx @MS aerogels is beneficial to the accessibility of the electrolyte ions, impeding the restacking of MXene nanosheets and revealing abundant active sites. The as-prepared Mg-Ti3 C2 Tx @MS aerogel exhibits high area capacitance of 603.12 mF cm−2 at a current density of 100 mA cm−2 , which outperforms the electrochemical performance of MXene-based aerogels in the previous report [48–50] . Furthermore, the asymmetric supercapacitor has a high areal energy density of 93.87 μWh cm−2 at a high power density of 7999 μW cm−2 , and it also indicates high stability with the capacity retention of 90.2 % after 10,000 cycles. This paper provides a simple method to prepare MXene-based aerogels with high mechanical strength and large layer spacing for high-performance supercapacitor. title: Synthesis effect on surface functionalized Ti3C2Tx MXene supported nickel oxide nanocomposites with enhanced specific capacity for supercapacitor application
authors: Prabhakar Nikhil, S. Vasanth, N. Ponpandian, C. Viswanathan
conclusion: An interlayer design approach using surface-functionalized Ti3 C2 Tx MXene with nickel oxide incorporation was presented using three alternative nanocomposite synthesis techniques to provide consistent, more open, and increased ionic conductive and electrochemically active space for ion transport. As an intercalant, tetramethylammonium hydroxide effectively separates neighboring exfoliated MXene sheets, increasing the ion-accessible surface area and resulting in rapid ion diffusion in several directions. By virtue of bath sonication, Nickel Oxide nanocomposite may uniformly adhere to MXene flakes, and the likelihood of fall-off is less compared to the other two approaches for enhancing electron transport. Consequently, BS- DLMX/NiO at a current density of 1 A/g has a reversible capacitance of 770C/g and a capacitance retention of 97.2 % after 3500 cycles at 8 A/g, proving the existence of -OH-enhanced functional groups. MXene sheets may trap large-sized ions between interlayers and operate as space-maintaining pillars, which may increase the additional capacitance. Furthermore, symmetric supercapacitors based on BS-DLMX/NiO exhibit excellent power and energy densities. The general hybrid method, which entails anchoring nanoparticles inside a 2D metallic network, might be used to develop high-performance electrodes for surface-enhanced energy storage devices. The current study proposes a way to lessen the self-restacking phenomena of Ti3 C2 Tx films without sacrificing conductivity; this approach applies to various layered electrode materials for energy storage applications with a fresh route for improved electrochemical performances. title: Co-precipitation synthesis of pseudocapacitive λ-MnO2 for 2D MXene (Ti3C2Tx) based asymmetric flexible supercapacitor
authors: B. Thanigai Vetrikarasan, Abhijith R. Nair, T. Karthick, Surendra K. Shinde, Dae-Young Kim, Shilpa N. Sawant, Ajay D. Jagadale
conclusion: In summary, the nanoplates-like λ-MnO2 was successfully synthesized using a facile, single-step and scalable co-precipitation method. This λ-MnO2 nanoplates-like material depicted a high specific surface area of 64.13 m2 g−1 with a meso-macro porous structure. It displayed a maximum specific capacitance of 288.5 F g−1 at the scan rate of 5 mV s−1 . Moreover, the λ-MnO2 //Ti3 C2 Tx ASC device exhibited a high ED of 15.5 Wh kg−1 at the PD of 1100 W kg−1 . title: Binder-free flexible Ti3C2Tx MXene/reduced graphene oxide/carbon nanotubes film as electrode for asymmetric supercapacitor
authors: Wenlong Luo, Qianwen Liu, Baozhong Zhang, Jie Li, Ruidong Li, Tingxi Li, Zhiqiang Sun, Yong Ma
conclusion: In this work, CNTs and rGO nanosheets enriched with oxygen-containing functional groups are obtained using the nitro-sulfur mixed acid method and the ascorbic acid reduction method, respectively. Then, MXene films, MC films, MG films, and MGC films are successfully prepared by vacuum-assisted filtration. The intercalation of CNTs or rGO nanosheets gives the films more stable ion transport channels, and exposes MXene to more ion-accessible active sites, thus allowing the films to exhibit excellent electrochemical properties. Accordingly, the electrochemical performances of MGC film perform particularly well, providing a high specific capacitance of 463.5F g−1 at 1 A g−1 . The MGC//MnO2 ASC is assembled through using the best-performing MGC film as negative electrode with MnO2 as positive electrode. The device has a voltage window of up to 1.7 V and a high capacitance retention of 92.9% after 8000 cycles at 3 A g−1 . Simultaneously, the ASC offers a high energy density of 33.95 Wh kg−1 at the power density of 814.8 W kg−1 , and even at a high power density of 2352.1 W kg−1 still offers an energy density of 20.45 Wh kg−1 . The MGC film prepared by vacuum-assisted filtration have the advantage of being simple and easy to prepare, and this strategy provides an effective guide for the research of flexible advanced electrode materials.

title: Ti3C2Tx MXene coated carbon fibre electrodes for high performance structural supercapacitors
authors: Bhagya Dharmasiri, Ken Aldren S. Usman, Si Alex Qin, Joselito M. Razal, Ngon T. Tran, Piers Coia, Timothy Harte, Luke C. Henderson
conclusion: Herein, we have developed a MXene coated CF electrode with excellent specific capacitance, mechanical properties and interfacial adhesion in epoxy-based composites, targeted for SSC applications. The best performing electrode developed from MXene coated on CF functionalized with a poly(o -phenyelenediamine) coating exhibited a specific capacitance of 157 F g−1 at 5 mV s−1 , a 725-fold improvement in capacitance compared to pristine unfunctionalized CF. The mechanical strength of the CF was not degraded via the surface modification and coating process. Moreover, the MXene coating also improved the interfacial adhesion of the electrode to an epoxy-based resin by 54 %. The SSC device fabricated with MXene coated CF preforms as electrodes with an epoxy-solvate ionic liquid bicontinuous solid electrolyte, showed a specific capacitance of 908 mF g−1 at 0.5 mA g−1 (∼42-fold improvement compared to the control).. As such this work opens new avenues of investigation of the use of MXenes in macroscale applications, especially in structural energy optimization.

authors: Sophy Mariam Varghese, Visakh V. Mohan, Sruthi Suresh, E. Bhoje Gowd, R.B. Rakhi
conclusion: The study highlights the remarkable potential of MXene-based nanocomposite materials, specifically the Ti3 C2 -PANI structure, as advanced electrode materials for electrochemical energy storage applications. The self-stacking issue of MXene nanosheets is addressed by the incorporation of high-conducting polymers as intercalators, resulting in enhanced interlayer spacing and enlarged ion contact area. The MXene-PANI symmetric supercapacitor exhibits a higher specific capacitance of 430 F g−1 , outperforming MXene-PPy and pure MXene supercapacitors. The device also demonstrates a maximum gravimetric energy density of 38 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 800 W kg−1 . The self-assembled PANI nanostructures within the MXene layers increase the number of active sites, allowing for enhanced ion diffusion and transportation, facilitating electrolyte ion acquisition by the active surface area. The strategy holds great promise for the development of advanced symmetric supercapacitors using MXene composite materials, leveraging their potential for future energy storage applications. title: Flexible Ti3C2Tx MXene/polypyrrole composite films for high-performance all-solid asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Wenlong Luo, Yue Sun, Yongqin Han, Jianxu Ding, Tingxi Li, Chunping Hou, Yong Ma
conclusion: In summary, flexible M-PPy composite films with adjustable thickness have been successfully prepared using the vacuum-assisted suction filtration of MXene nanosheets and PPy nanofibers. The layer spacing of MXene nanosheets is expanded by introducing PPy nanofibers to provide more transport channels and ion accessibility sites. The introduction of PPy nanofibers effectively prevents MXene nanosheets from self-stacking, while the layer gap of MXene nanosheets effectively overcome PPy expansion during charging and discharging tests. The results show that the optimized structure of the M-PPy3 film presents a gravimetric capacitance of 563.8 F g − 1 at 0.5 A g − 1 in 1 M H2 SO4 . Next, flexible all-solid M-PPy3//MnO2 ASC is assembled with the MnO2 as cathode and the M-PPy3 as the anode in 1 M PVA/H2 SO4 . The ASC delivers a gravimetric capacitance of 130.8 F g − 1 at 0.5 A g − 1 . The device provides nearly 100% coulombic efficiency and 86.8% capacitance retention after 6000 cycles at 2 A g − 1 . Calculations reveal that the ASC can provide an energy density of 35.3 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 486.1 W kg−1 , and even at 973.3 W kg−1 still provide 20.1 Wh kg−1 . This electrode optimization strategy not only demonstrates the feasibility for the development of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, but also provides a reference for the development of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene in small wearable electronic devices. title: Flexible, self-supporting Ti3C2Tx thin film electrodes prepared through vacuum filtration and applied for supercapacitors
authors: Runchen Shi, Mengyang Zhang, Xuehua Yan, Jianmei Pan, Jamile Mohammadi Moradian, Zohreh Shahnavaz
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In this work, we successfully exfoliated the Al layer to obtain d-Ti 3 C 2 T x by in-situ etching and ultrasonic assistance. Moreover, MXene thin films with a layered structure were utilized by vacuum filtration. The thin film electrode's structure, morphology and physicochemical properties were systematically explored to analyze its potential as electrode materials in supercapacitors. The microstructure and morphology of the thin film electrode were analyzed. The single-layer Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets have been successfully peeled off by AFM, XRD and TEM characterization methods, and this unique low-layer structure enables Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets to assemble into self-supporting films. In addition, the cross-section SEM showed the thin film's orderly, parallel, and compact stacked nanosheets composition leading to the excellent flexibility of thin films. The thin film electrode exhibited excellent electrochemical performance to achieve a specific capacitance of 293.3 F g −1 at the current density of 1 A g −1 . After 8000 cycles, the capacity retention rate is as high as 91 %, indicating the high stability of the layered structure of the MXene film. The energy density of the device assembled with MXene thin film electrode can still reach 5.8 Wh kg −1 at 1000 W kg −1 power density. The charge storage mechanism of MXene thin films as electrode materials is revealed by distinguishing current types. The energy storage mechanism of MXene thin film electrodes includes both diffusion control and surface control processes, and diffusion control contribution plays a dominant role at a low scan rate.

title: 1T-VS2/MXene network-like heterostructure realizes ultra-high energy density aqueous ammonium ion hybrid supercapacitors and their charge storage mechanism
authors: Xiaofeng Zhang, Salamat Ali, Peiao Lu, Qian Zhang, Wei Xu, Jiakun Luo, Dan Zhao, Bing Bai, Kui-Qing Peng
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In this work, 1T-VS 2 nanosheets were grown in-situ at MXenes via a hydrothermal method to construct a network-like heterostructure. The 1T-VS 2 nanosheets are vertically and uniformly arranged on the surface of the MXene nanosheets. This unique structure considerably increases the specific surface area, which provides more active sites for NH 4  + . In addition, the heterostructure effectively inhibits the recombination of carriers, thereby improving the efficiency of redox reactions. The HS-1T-VS@MXene//AC-AAHSC provides an ultrahigh energy density of 156.9 Wh/kg at a power density of 3,240 W/kg and still has a capacitance retention of 96.2 % after 10,000 cycles. The DFT calculations confirmed the electronic properties of the HS-1T-VS@MXene electrode material. The results show that, compared with pristine 1T-VS 2 and MXene, HS-1T-VS@MXene possesses enhanced conductivity, which benefit the rate performance of the electrode material. This work provides a new idea for the development of AAHSCs devices with high energy density.

title: Nonhazardous in-situ exfoliation approach for Ta-Nb2CTx MXenes as sustainable supercapacitor electrode applications
authors: Uzair Ahmed, Ghulam Nabi
conclusion: Concussively, the successful exfoliation of Nb2 CTx and Ta doped Nb2 CTx in a non-hazardous way has been explored for application as super capacitor electrode material. The study reveals that the enhancement of specific capacity of Ta-Nb2 CTx is attributed to the accordion-like 2D layered structure with intercalated ions inserted between layers causing layers to expand and provide more space for ion transportation as observed by SEM. XRD peaks, HRTEM and SAED confirmed that the doped samples have high crystallinity. title: Green synthesis of MXene@TiO₂ nanocomposites for high-performance flexible supercapacitors: Synergistic enhancement via polypyrrole polymerization and dopant engineering
authors: Hatice Yasemin Ulgunar Iskender, Osman Eksik, Melih Besir Arvas, Sibel Yazar
conclusion: In this study, flexible and conductive nanocomposite films—PPy, PPy/MXene, PPy/MXene/TiO₂GC, and PPy/MXene@TiO₂GC—were successfully fabricated on ATCC substrates and utilized as supercapacitor electrodes. The introduction of MXene into the polypyrrole matrix significantly improved the capacitive performance. Among the synthesized materials, the PPy(10 mg)/MXene@TiO₂GC(20 mg) electrode exhibited the highest specific capacitance of 467.7 F g⁻¹ at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ in a three-electrode system. The co-doping of TiO₂GC was also found to enhance electrochemical performance, suggesting a strong synergistic interaction among the components. The Dunn method analysis further confirmed that the charge storage mechanism is hybrid in nature, with diffusion-controlled processes dominating at low scan rates due to effective ion intercalation pathways, while surface capacitive contributions increase at higher scan rates, emphasizing the role of redox and electric double-layer mechanisms. This dual behavior highlights the complementary electrochemical roles of PPy, MXene, and TiO₂GC. In symmetric supercapacitor configuration, the highest energy and power densities achieved were 5.0 Wh kg⁻¹ at 0.1 mA cm⁻² and 1000 W kg⁻¹ at 1.0 mA cm⁻², respectively. Moreover, the device retained 82.03 % of its initial capacitance after 10,000 cycles, demonstrating excellent cycling stability. These results affirm the potential of PPy/MXene@TiO₂GC as a high-performance electrode material for flexible and durable energy storage applications. Such performance characteristics make this electrode material a promising candidate for next-generation flexible energy storage systems, particularly in applications such as wearable electronics, portable devices, and integrated energy-storage components in smart textiles and microelectronic systems. title: Nitrogen-doped MXene for supercapacitor: A review
authors: Ahmed Jalal Salih Salih, Ahmad Huseyin
conclusion: 6  Conclusion and recommendations  Doping MXene with nitrogen gives it improved morphological, chemical, and physical properties. This review demonstrates that nitrogen doping addresses the issue of MXene layer restacking, providing greater freedom for electrolyte ion movement and better accessibility to the MXene electrode surface. Simultaneously, the presence of nitrogen atoms increases electronic density and enhances redox activity. These improvements contribute to a higher electrode capacitance. Additionally, doping with nitrogen enhances conductivity, structural stability, and wettability. In light of the discussion on doping mechanisms, doping methods, and the effects of doping on electrochemical performance, several recommendations can be proposed here;   1.  Doping MXene with nitrogen has demonstrated clear success in supercapacitors, suggesting the potential for expanding theoretical and experimental studies of nitrogen doping to include other MXenes beyond Ti 3 C 2 Tₓ.    2.  Although doping in many studies occurs through multiple mechanisms simultaneously, one mechanism tends to dominate while others occur to a lesser extent. It would be beneficial to give greater attention to each mechanism within a single study to achieve successful doping through multiple mechanisms at higher levels.    3.  Most studies focus on the reduction of fluorine functional groups after doping, often neglecting hydroxyl functional groups, despite their significant impact on electrochemical performance. Greater emphasis should be placed on this aspect, especially since the effect of doping on hydroxyl groups can be easily diagnosed.    4.  It would be beneficial to conduct studies on doping that focus on the mechanism of surface adsorption, as there is a notable lack of research in this area.    5.  Further investigation into the different nitrogen doping configurations within the carbon lattice of MXene would be highly valuable. The contribution of each of the three forms (pyridinic, pyrrolic, and graphitic nitrogen) to performance enhancement requires further clarification. and then it is possible to control to some extent the selection of the best electrochemically performing configuration among the three forms during the doping process.

title: Defect enriched luminescent MXene-derived TiO2 for supercapacitors
authors: Ghrutanjali Sahu, Annu Balhara, Laxmidhar Besra, Divya Nechiyil, K. Sudarshan, Jyoti Prakash, Santosh K. Gupta, Sriparna Chatterjee
conclusion: The work focuses on comprehensively understanding the intricate relationships between the structure, optical properties, and electrochemical performance of MXenes and their derivatives, which is crucial for advancing the development of high-performance materials for energy storage and conversion. We have synthesized MXene-derived TiO2 that demonstrates excellent PL properties and serves as an electrode material for energy storage in supercapacitors. This behavior is attributed to the intrinsic features of MXene, which impart the MXene-derived TiO2 with various types of defects, such as surface defects, oxygen vacancies, and titanium vacancies. The exceptional PL and supercapacitive performance of MXene-derived TiO2 are mainly ascribed to the presence of titanium vacancies. This finding has been corroborated using EPR (electron paramagnetic resonance) analysis. However, the nanocomposite of MXene-derived TiO2 and NiO does not show significant improvement in light emission or supercapacitor performance, as the addition of NiO leads to a reduction in defect density. title: MoO3-x-assisted MXene-derived TiO2/C-graphene composite structure for high-capacitance electrode materials of ionic liquid-based supercapacitors

title: A review of recent progress in the synthesis of 2D Ti3C2Tx MXenes and their multifunctional applications
authors: Mojtaba Rostami, Alireza Badiei, Ghodsi Mohammadi Ziarani
conclusion: 3  Conclusion and future perspectives  To ensure excellent quality Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes for versatile applications such as HER, RBs, and SCs, the etching process and conditions need to be carefully manipulated. While 2D Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes exhibit excellent properties for various applications, their properties are strongly affected by surface termination functional groups and coupled materials. While the non-aqueous MS etching method has been investigated to enhance the physical and chemical characteristics of MXenes, such as mechanical properties and electrical conductivity, the accordion-like structure of the resulting MXenes renders them inappropriate for making nanoscale complexes. Cl-terminated MXenes offer the best HER catalytic activity due to their termination modification, which enhances better stability, interlayer spacing and Cl-ion conductivity. The hybridization of transition metal compounds with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes improves light absorption, electron transfer, and separation, as well as active sites. The hybridization process would be aided by the presence of edge-terminal groups that are evenly distributed on the surface of 2D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes, particularly hydrophilic oxide groups bound to Ti. The MS etching process is the most effective way to balance the stability and activity of HER catalysts based on transition metals in an alkaline electrolyte. The findings of this study greatly increase the range of uses for MXene and MAX nanomaterials by providing a novel method for the manufacture of additional MAX-phase materials at lower temperatures. Additionally, different Lewis acid MS show that it is possible to create unique MAX phases by replacement reactions.  The MS 3 method stands out among other MXene synthesis techniques because it eliminates the need for hazardous reactants and inert gas protection. The two carbide/nitride MXenes may be quickly synthesized using this approach, and it is easily scaled up to etch up to 60 g of the MAX phases. In conclusion, the MS 3 -MXene production process represents a significant breakthrough in the field, and is expected to generate substantial interest among both MXene researchers and industry professionals due to its potential for rapid and scalable production of high-quality MXene materials. The precursor material, hexagonal Ti 3 AlC 2 , featured a spiral chiral symmetry structure with diameters ranging from 200 nm to 2 m, and was made utilizing the “one-pot melting and Lewis salt additive” method. The resulting hexagonal Ti 3 AlC 2 nanomaterial maintained its interlayered structure and a well-defined layered microstructure with a large interlayer distance, which played a key role in ensuring its excellent long-term cycle stability. The flexible hexagonal Ti 3 C 2 nanosheets production has significantly advanced the investigation development of Ti 3 C 2 nanomaterials in the field of electrochemical energy storage (SCs and RBs), especially in terms of achieving super specific capacitance and long cycle stability. The surface terminal groups can undergo one-pot production from in single-step MS method, which considerably reduces the modification procedures and broadens the range of surface endings available. In this method, no acidic liquid waste is generated after creation, and the salt can be recycled, making it an environmentally-friendly, low-cost, fast and sustainable approach.  The utilization of TBAOH-treated MS-Ti 3 C 2 T x as an anode material in LIBs demonstrated a remarkable improvement in energy storage through enhanced electrochemical performance, super specific capacity, improved wettability, and outstanding rate capability. The increase in N content and reduction of F element in Ti 3 C 2 T x resulted in the development of N-N-Ti 3 C 2 T x electrode, which showed excellent capacitance retention, superior specific capacitance, good rate performance, high electrochemical activity area, and good electrical conductivity. These findings pave the way for the progress of Ti 3 C 2 T x nanomaterials with outstanding retention performance and high specific capacitances, highlighting the significance of surface chemistry tuning of MXene in enhancing their electrochemical properties. The study provides valuable insights for the development of a new generation of MXene negative electrodes that can be used in high-power batteries.  MXenes have garnered considerable attention due to their potential utility across diverse domains, encompassing the HER, RBs, and SCs. Nonetheless, they are also encumbered by specific constraints necessitating mitigation for further progress in these arenas. (i) HER: Limitations: (a) limited active sites: MXenes present a constrained quantity of active sites for the HER owing to surface termination and diminished surface area. (b) High overpotential: Achieving efficient HER performance with MXenes typically mandates high overpotentials. (c) Poor stability: MXenes are susceptible to surface oxidation in oxygen-rich environments, culminating in performance deterioration. Strategies to Overcome Limitations: (a) Surface functionalization: Augmenting the number of active sites for HER by introducing functional groups or doping MXenes. (b) Alloying: Enhancing catalytic activity and mitigating overpotential through MXene alloying with other metals, with molten salt Lewis acid etching representing a significant approach. (c) Surface Passivation: Enhancing MXene stability in oxygen-rich environments by developing protective coatings of metal oxide or metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). (ii) RBs: Limitations: (a) Volume expansion: MXenes undergo substantial volume expansion during cycling, resulting in mechanical degradation and capacity loss. (b) Limited specific capacity: MXenes often exhibit restricted specific capacity due to their low theoretical capacity. Strategies to overcome limitations: (a) Structural Engineering: Accommodating volume changes and enhancing mechanical stability by designing composite structures or nanoarchitectures with MOF derivatives and 2D nanomaterials. (b) Alloying and Intercalation: Increasing specific capacity and enhancing electrochemical performance by introducing other elements or ions into MXenes' structure, with molten salt Lewis acid etching being a key strategy. (c) Surface modification: Augmenting stability and performance through protective layer coatings or incorporation into conductive matrices. (iii) SCs: Limitations: (a) Low mass transfer: MXenes may exhibit constrained ion diffusion kinetics, resulting in low rate capability and energy density. (b) Limited capacitance retention: Capacitance degradation over cycling due to structural alterations and surface oxidation can afflict MXenes. Strategies to overcome Limitations: (a) Porosity Enhancement: Improving ion diffusion and augmenting accessible surface area through the introduction of hierarchical or porous structures. (b) Electrode thickness reduction: Enhancing rate capability by fabricating MXene electrodes with reduced thickness to shorten ion diffusion pathways. (c) Electrochemical stabilization: Mitigating capacitance degradation and enhancing stability through control of MXene surface chemistry or application of surface coatings, with molten salt Lewis acid etching playing a significant role. In addition to the aforementioned strategies, ongoing research endeavors are directed toward exploring novel synthesis methodologies, optimizing MXene compositions, and advancing characterization techniques to comprehensively address and surmount MXene limitations across various applications. These concerted efforts aim to bolster MXene performance, stability, and scalability, thereby facilitating their wider adoption in energy storage and catalytic domains.

title: Scalable assembly of polyaniline/Ti3C2Tx MXene modified cotton yarn flexible electrode for high-performance wearable energy storage
authors: Yang Zhang, Shenao Zhang, Kangxin Qi, Yazi Wang, Wei Chen, Jian Xu, Yusen Wang, Diwei Gu, Xiangxiang Pi, Bin Sun, Wangyang Lu
conclusion: In summary, the PTC yarn electrode, with the core of cotton yarn and the sheath of PT layer, was fabricated via scalable coating method. The cotton yarn regards as robust skeleton, endowing large mechanical properties, various deformation ability and integration ability for the PTC yarn electrode. Besides, the Ti3 C2 Tx layer on cotton yarn provides continuous conductive pathways for electron transfer. Moreover, the PANI nanoparticles as fillers can not only impede the self-restacking of Ti3 C2 Tx layer exposing larger surface area and richer ions diffusion channels, but also deliver pseudo-capacitance for adequate redox reaction sites. Due to the designed structure and synergistic effect, the PTC yarn electrode displays large capacitance (417.6F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ) and good rate performance (54 % capacitance retention at 10 A g−1 ) in three-electrode system. After assembling to symmetric F-SCs, the flexible device displays high capacitance of 175.6F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 , huge energy density of 6.1 Wh kg−1 , admired long-term cycling performance (98.5 % capacitance retention after 2000 cycling) and remarkable mechanical endurance, illustrating a huge application potential in wearable system. title: Unveiling the potential of M2X MXenes: Structure, properties, synthesis strategies, and supercapacitor applications
authors: Onkar Jaywant Kewate, Iftikhar Hussain, Megha Prajapati, Rita Kumari, Yosephine Intan Ayuningtyas, Dattakumar S. Mhamane, Mukund G. Mali, Mohan V. Jacob, Jeng-Yu Lin, Chhaya Ravi Kant, Sathyanarayanan Punniyakoti
conclusion: 7  Conclusion  In recent decades, the blossoming of supercapacitor applications has gained significant attraction for the materials science community. Extensive research on supercapacitors has been going on due to their exceptional characteristics. For an electrode material of supercapacitors, various materials have been utilized to boost the electrochemical performance. After graphene, in 2011 another wonder material was discovered known as MXenes. These MXenes have unique and excellent properties which help to improve the performance of various applications, especially supercapacitors. Owing to these advantages, the authors are presenting a thorough review article on the M 2 X MXenes. The review article is divided into various sections such as the introduction, structures, properties, synthesis approaches, M 2 X MXenes for supercapacitors, and conclusion, challenges, and future perspectives. In the introduction section, an overview of MXenes, various energy storage systems, a variety of electrode materials, and M 2 X MXenes is discussed appropriately. Next, MXenes consist of various structures. Here, only the structure of M 2 X MXenes is mentioned. In the coming section, diverse properties such as electronics, optical, magnetic, thermal, chemical, and mechanical are appropriate to supercapacitors explained properly. Afterward, the most important part is the synthesis of M 2 X MXenes. In this, a wide range of etching methods such as HF, MILD , molten salts, electrochemical, hydrothermal, supercritical, and Lewis acid for various M 2 X MXenes are explained thoroughly. Fluoride salt-based etching techniques, particularly those that employs minimally fluorinated or completely fluoride-free etchants, are gaining more recognition because of their enhanced safety, effectiveness, and environmental friendliness. In addition, to environmental and safety factors, these etching techniques produces MXenes with controlled terminations, enhancing their properties for specific applications (e.g., supercapacitors). Reduces defects and oxidation compared to traditional HF methods. Avoids severe handling hazards associated with HF-based methods. However, to avoid a completely HF-free process there is a requirement for green methods. Following the synthesis approaches, various M 2 X (Ti 2 CT  x  , Nb 2 CT  x  , V 2 CT  x  , Ta 2 CT  x  , Cr 2 CT  x  , Mo 2 CT  x  , V 2 NT  x  , Mo 2 NT  x  ) MXenes utilized as an electrode material for supercapacitors are discussed thoroughly. However, there remain obstacles to solve in the study of M 2 X-based materials for electrodes of supercapacitors.
